<meta>This page continues the spiritual interpretation of Genesis Chapter 4. It focuses on the figure of Abel, who represents "charity" or love in action, following the previous discussion of Cain, who represents faith or intellectual belief.</meta>

-># GENESIS.<-

342. The second "child" born of the church is <term>charity<note>In this context, "charity" (from the Latin *caritas*) refers to a deep, spiritual love for one's neighbor and a desire to do good, rather than simply giving money to the poor.</note></term>. This is clear because the church only truly conceives and brings forth two things: faith and charity. This same concept is symbolized by the first sons born to *Leah* and *Jacob*: *Reuben* represents faith, *Simeon* represents faith put into action, and *Levi* represents charity (see Genesis 29:32, 33, 34). Because of this, the tribe of *Levi* was assigned the priesthood and represented the *shepherd of the flock*. Since charity is the second "offspring" of the church, it is called a *brother* and is named *Abel*.

343. It should be obvious to anyone that a *shepherd of the flock* is someone who practices the "good of charity." This is a common image used throughout the Old and New Testaments. A person who leads and teaches is called a *shepherd*, while those being led and taught are the *flock*. Anyone who fails to lead people toward the good of charity is not a *true shepherd*; likewise, anyone who is not led toward what is *good*, or who refuses to learn what is good, is not part of the *flock*. It is hardly necessary to prove this meaning of *shepherd* and *flock* with many quotes, but we can look at these examples:

From Isaiah: "Then shall He [the Lord] give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal, and bread of the increase of the ground;—in that day shall *thy cattle feed in large pastures*," (30:23). In this passage, the *bread of the increase of the ground* refers to charity. 

Again: "The Lord Jehovah shall *feed his flock like a shepherd*; he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young," (40:11). 

In David: "Give ear, O *Shepherd of Israel*, thou that *leadest* Joseph like a *flock*; thou that dwellest between the cherubim, shine forth," (Psalm 80:1). 

In Jeremiah: "I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman; the *shepherds* with their *flocks* shall come against her; they shall pitch their *tents* against her round about; they shall *feed* every one in his place," (6:2, 3). 

In Ezekiel: "Thus saith the Lord God,—I will increase them with men like a *flock*, as a *holy flock*, as the *flock of Jerusalem* in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with *flocks of men*," (36:37, 38). 

And again, in Isaiah: "All the *flocks of Kedar* shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee," (60:7). 

Those who *lead the flock* toward the good of charity are the ones who *gather the flock*. Those who do not lead them in this way actually *disperse the flock*. This is because all gathering and all unity come from charity, while all scattering and division come from a lack of charity.

344. What is the point of faith—or the knowledge, rules, and doctrines of faith—if not to lead a person to live by them? And the primary goal of those teachings is <term>charity</term> (see Mark 12:28–35 and Matthew 22:34–39). This is the ultimate goal of every rule of faith. If this goal isn't reached, all the knowledge and doctrine in the world are empty and mean nothing.

345. A **tiller of the ground** represents someone who lacks <term>charity<note>In this spiritual context, "charity" means an active, heartfelt love for others, not just giving to the poor.</note></term>, even if they claim to have a faith based on religious principles. However, faith without love is not true faith at all. This becomes clear in the story that follows: the Lord (Jehovah) had no respect for Cain's offering, and Cain eventually killed his brother, an act that symbolizes the destruction of charity (represented by **Abel**). Those who focus primarily on physical and worldly matters are described as "tilling the ground." This is consistent with what was written in the second chapter (verses 19–23), where the man was sent out of the Garden of Eden specifically to **till the ground**.

346. Verse 3. *And in the course of time, it happened that Cain brought an offering to the Lord from the fruit of the ground.* The phrase **end of days** refers to the passage of time. The **fruit of the ground** refers to religious works or "fruits" that come from faith without love. An **offering to the Lord** signifies the act of worship that grows out of that mindset.

347. It is obvious that the "end of days" means as time progresses. This specific religious system—here called "Cain"—does not seem to have been so unacceptable when it was first created and accepted in its simple form. This is suggested by the earlier exclamation, *I have gotten a man, the Lord.* When it first began, faith was not yet so completely separated from love as it became in the **end of days** (or over time). This pattern of decline is actually seen in every system of religious faith.

348. The fact that the **fruit of the ground** signifies religious works performed without love is also shown by what follows: the actions of a faith lacking love are actually works of unfaithfulness. They are "dead" because they only come from the "external man" <note>The "external man" refers to our outward behaviors and worldly identity, as opposed to our "internal" or spiritual life.</note>. Regarding these, the prophet Jeremiah wrote: "Why does the way of the wicked prosper? You have planted them, they have taken root; they grow and they bring forth **fruit**. You are near in their mouths, but far from their <term>reins<note>original: "reins" (Latin: *renibus*). Historically, the kidneys or "reins" were thought to be the seat of a person's deepest emotions and hidden motives.</note></term>. How long shall the land mourn, and the plants of every field wither?" (12:1, 2, 4). Those who have God "near in their mouth" but "far from their reins" are people who act from faith alone without love; the prophet says of them that the "land mourns." These outward actions are also called the **fruit of their doings** elsewhere in the same book: "The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked; who can know it? I, the Lord, search the heart; I try the reins, to give to every man according to his ways, and according to the **fruit of his doings**," (17:9, 10). Similarly, in Micah: "The land shall be desolate because of those who live there, for the **fruit of their doings**" (7:13). That such fruit is actually **no fruit** at all—meaning the work is spiritually dead and both the fruit and root will perish—is declared in Amos: "I destroyed the Amorite before them, who was as tall as cedars and strong as oaks; yet I destroyed his **fruit** from above, and his roots from beneath" (2:9). And in David: "Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed..."

350. *And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. 352. *The firstlings of the flock* signify that which is of the Lord alone, as appears from the statement that the *firstlings* or *first-born*, in the <term>representative church<note>A "representative church" is a religious system (like the ancient Israelite religion) where physical rituals and laws were intended to mirror deeper spiritual realities.</note></term> were all holy, because they had relation to the Lord, who is alone the *first-born*. Let it be observed, that the *first-born* of worship signifies the Lord, and the *first-born* of the church, faith.

As celestial things are of innumerable genera, and still more numerous species, they are described in a general way in the song which Moses recited before the people: “Butter of kine, and *milk* of sheep, with *fat* of lambs and of rams, the <term>sons of Bashan<note>Bashan was a region famous for its rich pastures and strong livestock; spiritually, this represents a high quality of natural good.</note></term>, and of goats, with the *fat* of the kidneys of wheat; and thou didst drink the pure *blood* of the grape,” (Deuteronomy 32:14.) It is impossible for any one to know the signification of those expressions except from the <term>internal sense<note>The "internal sense" is the hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and historical accounts.</note></term>, for without the internal sense, such expressions as the *butter of kine*, the *milk of sheep*, the *fat of lambs*, the *fat of rams and goats*, the *sons of Bashan*, the *fat of the kidneys of wheat*, and the *blood of the grape*, would be sounds without meaning, when, nevertheless, all and every one of them signifies some genus or species of celestial things.

354. That Jehovah’s having respect to Abel, and to his *offering*, signifies that the works of charity, and worship grounded therein, are pleasing to the Lord,—was explained above, as also what is meant by *Abel*, and by an *offering*.

The *will* constitutes the real man, and not the thought or speech which he does not *will*: for every one derives his particular nature and disposition from the *will*, because that communicates its character to the whole man. If, however, any one thinks what is good, the essence of faith, which is charity, is also within the thought, since it includes the *will* of good; but if he says that he thinks what is good, and yet lives an evil life, it is impossible he can *will* any thing but evil, and he is, consequently, destitute of real faith.

Lord distinguished faith in a particular manner, that it might be preserved.

393. Before we proceed to elucidate the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning hidden beneath the literal words of the Bible.</note> of the words before us, it may be expedient to state some particulars respecting faith. The <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>According to the author, this refers to the earliest, most spiritually pure era of humanity.</note> acknowledged no faith but that which originated in love, and its members were unwilling even to mention the word faith, because they enjoyed a perception, by means of love from the Lord, of every thing appertaining to it. Such also are the <term>celestial angels</term> <note>The highest rank of angels, who are motivated by pure love rather than just intellectual understanding.</note> of whom we have spoken above. As it was, however, foreseen that mankind could not continue in this state, but that they would separate faith from love towards the Lord, and make it a distinct doctrine, it was therefore provided that faith might be separated, yet in such a mode as that by its means, or by the means of the knowledges of faith, men should still receive charity from the Lord. Thus knowledge or hearing was to precede, and by this a way was to be opened for the impartation of charity, or neighborly love and mercy from the Lord. Hence charity was not only to be inseparable from faith, but was also to be its principal, and then instead of the perception which the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> enjoyed, conscience succeeded; and as this was procured by faith adjoined to charity, it dictated, not what is true, but that such and such things are true because the Lord has spoken them in his Word. The churches after the flood were for the most part of this character, as also the primitive or first church after the Lord's advent, and by this the <term>spiritual</term> are distinguished from the <term>celestial angels</term>.

394. Now as this was foreseen, and provision made in consequence, to secure mankind from perishing by eternal death, therefore it is here declared that *none should do violence to Cain*, by whom is signified faith separate from charity, and further that *a mark was set upon him*, which means that the Lord distinguished faith in a particular manner, in order to secure its preservation. These are <term>arcana</term> <note>Sacred secrets or hidden spiritual truths.</note> which have been hitherto undiscovered, and are referred to by the Lord in what he said respecting marriage, and eunuchs, in Matthew: 
> "There are some eunuchs who were so born from their mother's womb; and there are some eunuchs who were made eunuchs of men: and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it let him receive it," (xix. 12.) 
The subjects of the <term>celestial marriage</term> <note>The spiritual union of heart and mind, or love and faith.</note> are denominated eunuchs; those born from the womb are such as resemble the <term>celestial angels</term>; those *made of men*, such as are like the <term>spiritual angels</term>; and those *made so of themselves*, are similar to <term>angelic spirits</term>, being not so much influenced by charity as by obedience.

sacred and inviolable, as is evident from the meaning of *Cain*, which denotes faith separate from charity, and from the number *seven*, as relating to what is holy. The number *seven* was esteemed holy, as is well known, by reason of the *six days of creation*, and of the *seventh*, which is the <term>celestial man</term> <note>In this context, the "celestial man" refers to the highest state of human development, where one acts purely from love and lives in a state of spiritual peace.</note>, in whom is peace, rest, and the sabbath. Hence this number occurs so frequently in the rites of the <term>Jewish church</term> <note>The author uses this term to describe the religious system and people of the Old Testament.</note>, and is everywhere held sacred, and hence also times were distinguished into *seven*, both the greater and the lesser intervals, and were called weeks <note>original Latin: *septimanæ*</note>. The greater intervals of time until the coming of the Messiah are spoken of in Daniel (9:24, 25), and the time of seven years is called a *week* <note>original Latin: *septimana*</note> by Laban and Jacob (Genesis 29:27, 28). Indeed, wheresoever the number *seven* occurs, it is esteemed holy. Thus we read in David: "Seven times a day do I praise thee" (Psalm 119:164). As man passes through six distinct states of <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or growth into a better person.</note>, previously to entering upon the *seventh*, or that of the celestial man, so also the times of his <term>vastation</term> <note>A theological term for a period of testing or "emptying out" of old ways before a new spiritual state can begin.</note> are distinguished, before the entire separation of every thing celestial takes place. Towards the east of *Eden* signifies being near the intellectual mind, where love had previously reigned, and also near the rational mind, which had been formerly under the government of charity. This is evident from what has been said regarding the meaning of *the east of Eden*: namely, that the "east" represents the Lord, and *Eden* represents love. Among the people of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The author's term for the earliest state of humanity, characterized by a direct, intuitive connection to God through love.</note>, the mind—consisting of the will and the understanding—was a single whole. For them, the will was everything because the understanding flowed directly from the will. They made no distinction between love (which belongs to the will) and faith (which belongs to the understanding), for love was their "all in all," and faith proceeded from that love. When, however, faith came to be separated from love—as was the case with the group represented by *Cain*—the will no longer held dominion. Yet, because the understanding began to regulate the mind instead of the will (or faith instead of love), it is said that he "dwelt towards the east of *Eden*." As previously noted, faith was distinguished, or had a "mark" set upon it, so that it might be preserved for the future use of mankind.

399. Verse 17. *And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bare Enoch; and he was building a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.* Cain "knowing" his wife, and her conceiving and bearing *Enoch*, signifies that this <term>schism</term> <note>A formal division or separation within a spiritual or religious body.</note> or heresy produced another one derived from itself, named *Enoch*. By the *city which he built* is signified every doctrinal and heretical principle derived from that original error. Because this new schism was named *Enoch*, it is said that the *name of the city was called after the name of his son, Enoch*.

400. *Cain's knowing his wife, and her conceiving and bearing Enoch*, signifies that this heresy gave rise to another. This is clear from what was said before, as well as from the first verse regarding *Adam* and *Eve his wife* producing *Cain*. The subsequent conceptions and births—whether of the true church or of heresies—had their genealogies recorded because they spread in a similar way; many different heresies, just like many different churches, can spring from a single source.

401. That *Enoch* here represents a heresy and its associated doctrines is demonstrable from the word *Enoch* itself, which signifies "instruction" beginning or originating from that point <note>original: "Enoch" (Hebrew: חֲנוֹךְ, Chanokh), often translated as 'dedicated' or 'initiated,' related to the root for teaching or training.</note>.

402. *The city which he builded* signifies all the doctrinal and heretical opinions derived from that heresy. This is shown in every passage of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> in which the name of a city occurs; in these contexts, "city" never refers merely to a physical city, but always to something doctrinal or heretical. Angels are entirely unaware of what a physical city is or the names of specific cities; because their thoughts are spiritual and celestial, they perceive only the internal meaning of a city and its name. This is how they perceive the *holy city*, which is also called the *holy Jerusalem* <note>In this symbolic system, Jerusalem represents the Church and its core teachings rather than a geographical location.</note>.

When the internal is signified he is called *Israel*; but of those churches, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said hereafter.

423. *Tubal-Cain* is stated to be an *instructor of every artificer*, and not a *father*, as was the case with *Jabal* and *Jubal*; the reason is, because celestial and spiritual, or internal things, had previously no existence [in the church.] Now the term *father* is applied to *Jabal* and *Jubal*, as denoting that such internal things then first began to exist; but as natural or external things did exist before, and were now applied to internal things, therefore *Tubal-Cain* is not denominated a *father*, but *an instructor of every artificer.*

From the spirits newly arrived in the other world, I had the best possible opportunity of ascertaining what notions they had formed respecting heaven and heavenly joy, for when left to themselves they think as they would do in the material body. I am permitted to mention a few examples.*

451. *A certain spirit who, during his life in the body, had been in the possession of pre-eminent power, retained his love of command when he came into the other world. He was, however, told that he was in another and an eternal kingdom, that his own authority had expired on earth, and that every one was estimated in the spiritual world according to the degree in which he is principled in <term>the good and the true</term> <note>A technical term in the author's work referring to the combination of selfless love (the good) and wisdom/faith (the true).</note>, and the mercy of the Lord. On hearing this he was ashamed.*

452. *I have conversed with spirits who conceived heaven and heavenly joy to consist in this, that they should be the greatest. It was, however, told them, that in heaven he is the greatest who is the least; for whosoever desires to be the least, has the greatest happiness, and since he enjoys the greatest happiness who is the least, it follows that he is the greatest. For what is true greatness but to be the most happy? It is this which the powerful seek to attain by power, and the rich by riches. They were further informed, that heaven does not consist in desiring to be least with a view to being the greatest, for such desire is the <term>lust of pre-eminence</term>, but in every one's wishing from his heart better to others than to himself, and in serving others with a view to their happiness, from love, and not for any selfish ends.*

453. *Some entertain so gross an idea of heaven, as to suppose it to consist merely in admission; regarding it as a closed place, into which they are admitted through a door which is opened for the purpose, by those who there act as door-keepers.*

454. *Some believe it to consist in leading an indolent life, and being waited upon by others; but they are informed, that happiness by no means consists in a state of idleness and rest, for were it so, every one would desire happiness for himself alone, and thus none could possess it. Moreover, in such an inactive, idle life, they would become torpid, although it must be known to every one, that without activity of life there can be no happiness. The angelic life consists in <term>use</term> <note>original: "usus". This refers to performing useful services or functions for the benefit of the community, which the author argues is the true source of joy.</note>, and in the goods of charity.*

## CHAPTER 5

...is more delightful to the angels than to instruct and teach spirits coming from the world,—to serve mankind by inspiring them with what is good, and by restraining the evil spirits attendant on them from passing their proper bounds,—to raise up the dead to eternal life, and afterwards, if their souls be of such a quality as to render it possible, to introduce them into heaven. In the performance of these offices they perceive an indescribable degree of delight. Thus they are images of the Lord, for they love their neighbor more than themselves, and where this feeling exists, there is heaven. Angelic happiness then is in **use**, from **use**, and according to **use** <note>The author uses the term "use" to mean a specific function, service, or useful work performed for the benefit of others.</note>; or, in other words, it is according to the goods of love and charity. Those who entertained the idea, that heavenly joy consists in indolence and in indolently quaffing eternal delight, were, for the purpose of making them ashamed of their opinions, led to perceive the nature of such life. And they perceived that it is most thoroughly sorrowful; for being destructive of every delight, it soon becomes irksome and disgusting.

455. A certain spirit, who, during his life on earth, had been particularly distinguished for his knowledge of <term>the Word</term> <note>A term referring to the Holy Scriptures, specifically the inner spiritual meaning the author believes they contain.</note>, had conceived the idea that heavenly joy consists in luminous glory, similar to the light of the sun when its rays appear of a golden hue, and thus also that it was a life of indolence. In order that he might know that he was in error, such a light was furnished to him, and he was placed in the midst of it. At this he was so much delighted, that he said he was in heaven; but he could not remain there long, for it speedily grew tiresome to him, and lost its power of pleasing.

456. Those who were the best educated, declared heavenly joy to consist in a life separated from the good offices of charity, and in merely praising and worshipping the Lord, and called this an active life. They were, however, told that thus to praise and worship the Lord is not active life, but the effect of that life, for the Lord has no need of praises, but is desirous that all should perform the good deeds of charity, and, according as they do these, they receive happiness from the Lord. Notwithstanding this, these learned spirits could form no idea of delight, but rather of slavery, as consisting in the performance of charitable actions; nevertheless the angels testified that such good offices were consistent with the most perfect freedom, and attended with inexpressible felicity.

457. Almost all who come into the other life suppose that there is the same hell and the same heaven for every one, although, in fact, there are infinite differences and varieties of both; for no two people ever dwell in a precisely similar hell or heaven, just as no two men, spirits, or angels, are exactly alike. *459. There are three heavens: the first is the abode of good spirits, the second of angelic spirits, and the third of angels, all of whom—as well the spirits as the angelic spirits and angels—are distinguished into two orders, <term>celestial</term> and <term>spiritual</term>. <note>In this system, "celestial" refers to those motivated primarily by love and the heart, while "spiritual" refers to those motivated by truth, intellect, and the principles of faith.</note> The celestial are such as have received faith from the Lord by means of love, like the men of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The author's term for the first metaphorical "golden age" of humanity described in the early chapters of Genesis.</note> treated of above; and the spiritual, those who have received charity from the Lord by means of the knowledges of faith, and who make this their principle of action.*

## THE CONTENTS.

460\. This chapter treats specifically of the expansion of the *Most Ancient Church* <note>The author uses this term to describe the first, most perfect spiritual state of humanity.</note> through successive generations, almost until the time of the great flood.
461\. The Most Ancient Church itself, which was "celestial" <note>In this context, 'celestial' refers to a state of being motivated by pure love and direct perception of divine truth, rather than just intellectual belief.</note>, is what the scripture calls *Man and a likeness of God* in verse 1.
462\. A second church, which was not as heavenly as the Most Ancient Church, is named *Seth* in verses 2 and 3.
463\. A third church was named *Enos* (verse 6); a fourth *Cainan* (verse 9); a fifth *Mahalaleel* (verse 12); a sixth *Jared* (verse 15); a seventh *Enoch* (verse 18); and an eighth church *Methuselah* (verse 21).
464\. The church called *Enoch* is described as organizing a system of doctrine based on what was revealed to and perceived by the Most Ancient Church. Although this doctrine was not used at that time, it was preserved for the benefit of future generations. This preservation is signified by the statement that *Enoch was not, because God took him* in verses 22, 23, and 24.
465\. A ninth church was named *Lamech* (verse 25).
466\. A tenth church—the parent of three churches that would emerge after the flood—was named *Noah*. This church is referred to as the "Ancient Church" <note>The 'Ancient Church' succeeded the 'Most Ancient Church' and represents a shift toward a more symbolic or intellectual form of worship.</note> in the explanation of verses 28 and 29.
467\. *Lamech* is described as having lost the direct spiritual perception that the Most Ancient Church once enjoyed, while *Noah* is described as a New Church (verse 29).

---

Therefore, we can see that the *names* in this chapter do not refer to individual people, but to "things"—specifically, the various doctrines or stages of the church that were preserved throughout their changes from the time of the Most Ancient Church down to *Noah*. Furthermore, every church naturally declines over time, and in the end, there remains only

### 469. Verse 1. 
*This is the book of the generations of Man. In the day that God created man, into the likeness of God made he him. The book of the generations* is the account of those who proceeded from the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The "Most Ancient Church" is the author's term for the very first spiritual era of humanity (the "Adam" state), characterized by a direct, heart-centered connection to the Divine.</note>. *In the day that God created man* denotes his being made <term>spiritual</term> <note>To be "spiritual" here means to have a mind formed by truth and understanding.</note>, and *into the likeness of God made he him*, signifies, that he was made <term>celestial</term> <note>To be "celestial" is a higher state than "spiritual," where the heart is ruled by love and goodness.</note>: thus it is a description of the Most Ancient Church.

### 470. 
*The book of the generations* is an account of those who proceeded from the Most Ancient Church, as is very evident from what follows; for, from this to the eleventh chapter, or to the time of <term>Eber</term> <note>Eber is a biblical figure who represents the start of the "Hebrew Church," the transition toward a more external, ritualistic form of worship.</note>, names never signify persons, but things. In the most ancient time mankind were distinguished into *houses, families*, and *tribes*; a *house* consisting of the husband and wife with their children, and domestic servants; a *family*, of a greater or lesser number of houses, which were at no great distance, but were still separate from each other; and a *tribe*, of a larger or smaller number of families.

### 471. 
The reason why they thus dwelt, namely, apart one among another, divided only into *houses, families*, and *tribes*, was, that by this means the church might be preserved entire, and all the houses and *families* might be dependant on their parent, and thereby remain in love and in true worship. It is to be remarked also that each *house* had a peculiar genius or temper distinct from every other; for it is well known that children, and even remote descendants, derive from their parents a particular disposition, and such characteristic marks as cause a difference in their faces, and other parts of their persons; to prevent therefore a confusion of tempers and dispositions, and to preserve the distinction accurately, it pleased the Lord that they should dwell in this manner. Thus the church was a living representative of the kingdom of the Lord; for in the Lord's kingdom there are innumerable societies, each distinguished from every other, according to the differences of love and faith. This, as we observed above, is what is meant by *living alone*, and by *dwelling in tents*. For the same reason also it pleased the Lord that the Jewish church should be distinguished into *houses, families*, and *tribes*, and that they should contract mar

### 472.
In the day that God created man, denotes his being made spiritual, and by God's making him into his likeness is represented his being made celestial, as appears from what was said and shown above. <note>In this system of thought, "spiritual" refers to a state of being led by truth or the intellect, while "celestial" refers to a higher state of being led by love or the heart.</note> The expression *to create*, properly relates to man when he is created anew, or <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of spiritual rebirth where a person is transformed from a self-centered state to a God-centered state.</note>; and the phrase *to make*, when he is perfected; wherefore in the Word there is an accurate distinction observed between *creating, forming, and making*, as was shown above in the second chapter, where it is said of the spiritual man made celestial, that *God rested from all his work, which God created in making*, and in other passages also, *to create* relates to the spiritual man, and *to make*, that is, *to perfect*, to the celestial man.

### 473.
*A likeness of God* is a celestial, and *an image of God* a spiritual man, as has been also previously shown. An *image* is preparatory to a *likeness*, and a *likeness* is a real resemblance, for the celestial man is entirely governed by the Lord after his own *likeness*.

### 474.
Since therefore the subject here treated of is the generation or propagation of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The Most Ancient Church refers to the earliest, most innocent state of humanity, symbolized by "Adam."</note>, it is first described as proceeding from a spiritual into a celestial state, its propagation being subsequent thereto.

### 475.
*Verse 2. Male and female created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Man, in the day when they were created.* By *male* and *female* the marriage between faith and love is signified, and by calling their name *Man* is denoted that they constituted the church, which is, in an especial sense, denominated *humanity* <note>original Latin: "homo," referring to the human being in a general sense, rather than a male specifically.</note>.

### 476.
By *male* and *female* is signified the marriage between faith and love. This was declared and proved above, where it was shown that the *male* or *man* <note>original Latin: "vir," referring specifically to the male individual.</note> represents the understanding and whatever belongs to it, consequently every thing of faith; and that the *female* or *woman* signifies the will, or the things appertaining to the will, consequently whatever has relation to love; wherefore she was also called *Eve*, a name signifying life, which is derived from love alone. By a *female* therefore is also represented the church, as has been previously shown, and by a *male* a *man of the church*: the state of the church is here treated of when it was spiritual, and about to be made celestial, wherefore *male* is mentioned before *female*, as in chapter 1:26, 27. The expression *to create*, also has reference to the spiritual man; but afterwards when a marriage has been effected, or the church made celestial, then it is no longer called either male or female, but *a human being* <note>original Latin: "homo"</note>, who, by reason of their marriage, signifies both; wherefore it presently follows, *and he called their name Man*, by whom is signified the church.

# 477.
That Man is the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>In this context, the "Most Ancient Church" refers to the earliest spiritual state of humanity, characterized by a direct, heart-centered relationship with God.</note> has been often said and shown above; for in a supreme sense the Lord Himself alone is man; hence the <term>celestial church</term> <note>A state of the church where people are led by love for the Lord.</note> is called Man, as being a likeness, and hence too the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>A state of the church where people are led by truth and faith.</note> is so called as being an image: but in a general sense every one is called man who has human understanding; for man is man by virtue of understanding, and according thereto one person is more man than another, although the distinction of one man from another ought to be made according to faith as grounded in love to the Lord. 

That the <term>Most Ancient Church</term>, and every true church, and hence those who are of the church, or those who are principled in love and faith towards the Lord, are especially called man, is evident from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures.</note>; as in Ezekiel: “I will cause *man* to multiply upon you, all the house of Israel, all of it; I will cause to multiply upon you *man and beast*, that they may be multiplied and bear fruit; and I will cause you to dwell according to your *ancient times*; and I will do better unto you than at your *beginnings*; and I will cause *man* to walk upon you, my people Israel,” (xxxvi. 10, 11, 12;) where by *ancient times* is signified the <term>Most Ancient Church</term>; by *beginnings* the ancient churches; by the *house of Israel* and *people Israel*, the primitive church, or church of the Gentiles; all which churches are called *man*. 

So in Moses: “Remember the *days of eternity*, consider the *years of generation and generation*: when the *Most High* divided to the nations an inheritance, when He separated the *sons of man*, He set the *bounds of the people* according to the number of the *sons of Israel*,” (Deut. xxxii. 7, 8;) where by the *days of eternity* the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> is meant; by *generation and generation* the ancient churches: the *sons of man* are those who were principled in faith towards the Lord, which faith is the *number of the sons of Israel*. 

That a <term>regenerate person</term> <note>Someone who has been spiritually reborn through a change of heart and mind.</note> is called *man*, appears from Jeremiah: “I beheld the earth, and lo it was empty and void; and the heavens, and they had no light; I beheld, and lo, no *man*, and every *bird of the heavens* were fled,” (iv. 23, 25;) where *earth* signifies the <term>external man</term>, *heaven* the <term>internal</term>; *man* the love of goodness; the *bird of the heavens* the understanding of truth. 

Again: “Behold the days come, saith Jehovah, that I will sow the house of Israel, and the house of Judah, with the *seed of man*, and with the *seed of beast*,” (xxxi. 27;) where *man* signifies the <term>internal man</term>, *beast* the <term>external</term>. 

So in Isaiah: “Cease ye from man in whose nostrils is breath, for wherein is he to be accounted of,” (ii. 22;) where by *man* is signified a man of the church.

It is observed that the church decreases and degenerates, and that its original integrity decays, chiefly because of the increase of **hereditary evil** <note>The concept that spiritual or moral inclinations—not just physical traits—are passed down from parents to children.</note>. Every parent who commits an actual evil adds a new layer of corruption to what they themselves inherited. When a person repeatedly chooses an evil action, it takes on the "appearance of nature" and becomes natural to them. This addition to their inherited nature is then transplanted into their children and posterity. Consequently, there is an immense increase in hereditary evil across succeeding generations. This is plain to anyone who observes the evil dispositions of children and sees the resemblance between them, their parents, and their forefathers.

It is a very false idea to believe, as some do, that there is no hereditary evil except for what was implanted by Adam (see section 313). In reality, every individual causes hereditary evil through their own actual sins, adding to what they received from their parents and increasing the "quantity" that remains in their descendants. This evil is never checked or tempered except in those who are **regenerated** <note>In this context, "regeneration" refers to a process of spiritual rebirth where the Lord replaces a person's selfish nature with a new, heavenly one.</note> by the Lord. This is the primary reason why every church eventually declines; and this was the case with the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The author uses this term to describe the first "age" or state of humanity, characterized by an instinctive, heart-centered connection to God.</note>.

495. How the Most Ancient Church declined cannot be seen unless the nature and meaning of **perception** be understood, for 그 church enjoyed a ***perception*** such as does not exist today. The ***perception*** of a church consists in this: its members ***perceive*** what is good and true directly from the Lord, just as the angels do. This is not so much about what is good and true regarding civil society, but what is good and true regarding love and faith toward the Lord. From a person's confession of faith, when confirmed by how they live, it may be seen what the nature of ***perception*** is, and whether it exists or not.

496. Verse 6. *And Seth lived a hundred and five years, and begat Enos.* **Seth**, as was observed, is another church, less **celestial** <note>"Celestial" refers to the highest spiritual state, defined by love rather than just intellectual understanding.</note> than the Most Ancient Church that was its parent, yet still considered one of the Most Ancient Churches. By "living *a hundred and five years*," specific periods and spiritual states are signified, as mentioned before. By "begetting *Enos*," it is signified that another church descended from it, which was called **Enos**.

497. Seth is another church less celestial than the Most Ancient Church, its parent, yet still one of the Most Ancient Churches, as shown by what was said earlier regarding Seth (verse 3). The situation with churches is that, by degrees and over time, they decrease in their essential qualities due to the causes mentioned above.

498. That begetting ***Enos*** signifies that another church descended from the previous one is also clear from the fact that the names in this chapter signify nothing else but various churches.

501. The case of the churches, succeeding each other at particular periods, and of which it is said that one was descended from another, may be compared with that of fruits and their seeds, in the midst or inmost parts whereof are contained, as it were fruits of fruits, and seeds of seeds, from which the other parts that succeed each other in order, receive life; for as each part is further removed from that inmost centre towards the circumference, in the same proportion it partakes less of the essence of the fruit or seed, till at length it becomes a mere skin or covering, wherein the fruits or seeds have their termination. Or as in the case of the brain, in the inmost parts whereof are subtile organical forms called the <term>cortical substances</term> <note>The "gray matter" of the brain. The author, drawing on his background in anatomy, uses the brain's structure to illustrate how spiritual life flows from a central core to the outer edges.</note>, from which, and by which the operations of the soul proceed: to those substances others succeed in order, first the purer coverings, then the denser, afterwards the common coats called <term>meninges</term> <note>The three membranes (dura mater, arachnoid, and pia mater) that envelope the brain and spinal cord.</note>, which are terminated in coverings still more common, and at last in the most common or general of all, which is the skull.

### 511—520. GENESIS.

The Most Ancient and the following Churches <note>In the author's system, the "Most Ancient Church" represents the earliest, most spiritually pure state of humanity.</note> acted with the design that such doctrine should serve as a rule whereby to know what was good and true: such persons were called *Enoch* <note>The Hebrew name *Chanokh* carries the meaning of "initiating" or "instructing."</note>. This is what is signified by these words, "**And Enoch walked with God:**" so also they called that doctrine; which is likewise signified by the name *Enoch*, meaning *to instruct*. The same is evident also from the signification of the expression *to walk*, and from this circumstance, that he is said to have walked with *God*, not with *Jehovah* <note>The author distinguishes between these two names for the Divine: "God" (Elohim) is associated with the intellect and truths of faith, while "Jehovah" is associated with the heart and the life of love.</note>: *to walk with God* is to teach and live according to the doctrine of faith, but *to walk with Jehovah* is to live the life of love.

*To walk* is a customary form of speaking signifying to live, as *to walk in the law, to walk in the statutes, to walk in the truth: to walk* has respect properly to a "way," <note>In biblical symbolism, a "way" or path often represents the specific truths or beliefs a person follows.</note> which relates to truth, consequently which relates to faith, or the doctrine of faith. What is signified in the Word by *walking*, may in some measure appear from the following passages; as in this from Micah: "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good, and what doth Jehovah require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to humble thyself by *walking with thy God*?" (vi. 8:) in this passage, *to walk with God* signifies also to live according to those things which he had showed: but here it is said "with *God*," but respecting *Enoch*, another word is used, which signifies also "*from with God*," so that the expression is of ambiguous meaning. 

So in David: "Thou hast delivered my feet from falling, that I may *walk* before *God* in the light of the living," (Psalm lvi. 13;) where *to walk before God* is *to walk* in the truth of faith, which is the *light of the living*: to the same purport in Isaiah: "The people that *walked* in darkness have seen a great light," (ix. 1.) So the Lord says by Moses: "I will *walk* in the midst of you, and will be your *God*, and ye shall be my people," (Levit. xxvi. 12;) signifying that they should live according to the doctrine of the law. 

So in Jeremiah: "They shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have *walked*, and whom they have sought," (viii. 2:) here is a manifest distinction made between the things relating to love, and the things relating to faith; the things relating to love are expressed by loving and serving; the things relating to faith are expressed by *walking* and seeking: in all the prophetical writings every expression is accurately attended to, nor is one expression ever adopted instead of another. But *to walk with Jehovah*, or *before Jehovah*, signifies, in the Word, to live the life of love.

### 521.
That by the expression, "**He was not, for God took him,**" is signified the preservation of that doctrine for the use of posterity, appears from the case above-mentioned respecting *Enoch*, that he reduced to doctrine what had been matter of *perception* <note>In this context, "perception" refers to an immediate, intuitive knowledge of what is good and true, which the author believes the first humans possessed without needing to be taught.</note> in the Most Ancient Church. This at that time was not allowable; for it is a very different thing to know what is good and true by *perception*, and to learn what is good and true by means of doctrine; those who know by perception have no need of the knowledge acquired in the way of systematized doctrines; as for example; he who knows how to think well, has no occasion to be taught to think by any rules of art, for hereby his faculty of thinking well would be impaired, as is the case with those who bury the thinking principle in the dust of school logic <note>A reference to "scholasticism," the medieval method of learning that focused on rigid logic and dialectic, which the author argues can stifle genuine thought.</note>. To such as are principled in perceptive knowledge, it is given from the Lord to know what is good and true by an internal way; but to such as are taught by doctrine, knowledge is given by an external way, or that of the bodily senses; and the difference of knowledge in these two cases is like the difference between light and darkness: add to this, that the *perceptions* of the celestial man <note>The "celestial man" is a technical term for a person who acts from a heart full of love rather than just an intellectual understanding of rules.</note> are such as to admit of no description for they extend to the most minute and particular things, with all variety according to states and circumstances. But whereas it was foreseen that the *perceptive* faculty of the Most Ancient Church would perish, and that afterwards mankind would learn by doctrines what is true and good, or would come by darkness to light, therefore it is here said that God took him, that is, preserved the doctrine for the use of posterity.

### 522.
The state and quality of *perception*, with those who were called *Enoch*, were also made known to me by experience; it was a kind of general obscure *perception* without any distinctness; for the mind in such case determines its intuition out of or without itself into doctrinals <note>The author is suggesting that once truths are written down as "doctrines," the mind looks "outside" itself to a book or a teacher, rather than "inside" to a direct spiritual connection.</note>.

### 524.

man, and the more *remains* <note>The term "remains" (Latin: *reliquiae*) refers to the traces of goodness and truth from childhood or earlier spiritual states that God preserves in a person's interior.</note> there are, the more he is a man: *remains* are to man as a sort of heavenly star; the less it is, so much the less light proceeds from it, but the larger it is, so much the more light it emits. The few things which *remained* from the Most Ancient Church, were reserved amongst those who constituted the Church called Noah: but these were not *remnants* of perception <note>Perception was the immediate, intuitive knowledge of God held by the first humans.</note>, but of integrity, and also of doctrine derived from the objects of perception in the Most Ancient Churches; wherefore a new church was now first raised up by the Lord, which being of a different complexion from the Most Ancient Churches, is to be called the Ancient Church; Ancient on this account, because it commenced at the end of the ages before the flood, and at the earliest period after the flood: of this church, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said hereafter.

531. ***By comforting us concerning our work and toil of our hands, out of the ground which Jehovah hath cursed***, is signified doctrine, whereby what had been perverted would be restored, will also be made to appear, by the divine mercy of the Lord, in the following pages: by *work* is signified, that they could no longer perceive what was true, but with labor and difficulty: by *toil of the hands out of the ground which Jehovah hath cursed*, is signified, that they could do nothing that was good: thus Lamech is described, or the church <term>vastated</term> <note>In this context, a "vastated" church is one that has been emptied of its spiritual life and truth.</note>. *Work and toil of our hands* are predicated, when the state is such, that men are impelled to inquire what is true, and to do what is good, from themselves, or from <term>proprium</term> <note>original: *proprium*; This technical term refers to a person's "selfhood" or the ego—the sense of "self" that feels independent of God.</note>; what is thereby produced is the *ground which Jehovah hath cursed*, that is, it is nothing but what is false and evil: what is signified by Jehovah cursing may be seen above, n. 245. *To comfort* has respect to the son, or Noah, whereby is signified a new generation, that is, a new church, which is the Ancient Church; by which, or by Noah, is therefore likewise signified rest, and comfort proceeding from rest, as was the case with the Most Ancient Church, in that it was the seventh day, whereon the Lord rested, see n. 84 to 88.

537. *A certain spirit applied himself to my left side and asked me whether I knew how he might enter into heaven; to whom it was given to me to reply, that it belongs to the Lord alone, who only knows the state and quality of every person, to give admission into heaven. This is the case with very many who, upon their first entrance into another life <note>original: "in alteram vitam" — Swedenborg's common term for the immediate state of the soul after the death of the body.</note>, are inquisitive only about how to be admitted into heaven, being in utter ignorance of the nature of heaven and of heavenly joy—specifically, that heaven consists in mutual love, and that heavenly joy is the joy derived from that love. Therefore, in consideration of this ignorance, they are first informed what heaven is and what heavenly joy is, even by vivid experience. *...desire to be admitted into heaven, had his <term>interiors</term><note>interiors: The inner levels of a person's mind or soul, which in the afterlife are opened to reveal one's true character.</note> opened, in order that he might perceive the nature and quality of heaven, and be made sensible of heavenly joy: but no sooner did he feel the <term>heavenly influx</term><note>heavenly influx: The spiritual energy, light, and love that flows from the Divine through the heavens.</note>, than he began to cry out in great agony, praying earnestly to be delivered, and declaring that he should die if his pain were not removed; wherefore his interiors were closed towards heaven, and he was thus restored to himself again. 538. *Certain others also were desirous of going into heaven, who were in like manner ignorant of the nature of heaven; and it was told them, that to go into heaven, unless they were principled in a faith grounded in love, was as dangerous as to walk into a fire: still however they persisted in their desire; but when they came to the outermost verge of heaven, or to the inferior <term>sphere</term><note>sphere: A spiritual atmosphere or "aura" emanating from an individual or a community that affects others nearby.</note> of angelic spirits, they were so affected, that they instantly cast themselves headlong down again; hereby they were instructed how dangerous a thing it is even to approach towards heaven, before the spirit is prepared by the Lord to receive the affections of faith.*

539. *A certain spirit, who during his life in the body had made light of adulteries, was, agreeably to his desire, admitted to the verge of heaven: but when he was come thither, he began to be tortured, and to smell as it were the stench of a dead body, arising from himself, which was intolerable: it also appeared to him that to advance further would be attended with most fatal consequences to him; wherefore he threw himself down headlong to the earth beneath, and was enraged to think that he should be made sensible of such tortures on being admitted to the verge of heaven, because he was then admitted into a sphere which was opposite to adultery; this spirit is amongst the unhappy.*

540. *Almost all who come into another life are ignorant of the nature of heavenly blessedness and felicity, by reason of their ignorance respecting the nature and quality of internal joy, of which they form a judgment merely from corporeal and worldly pleasures and satisfactions; wherefore what they are ignorant of they think can have no existence, when nevertheless bodily and worldly joys, compared with such as are internal, are respectively of no account, and rather to be considered as impure and filthy; wherefore the upright and well-disposed spirits, who are unacquainted with the nature of heavenly joy, as a means of their instruction herein, are introduced first to a sight of paradisiacal scenes which exceed every idea of the imagination, concerning which, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said in a future part of this work. As soon as they are introduced, they immediately suppose that they are come to a celestial paradise; but*

*543. Certain spirits were desirous to know the nature of heavenly joy; accordingly it was permitted them to have a perception of their own inmost life, at least so far as they could bear; still, however, this was not angelic joy, scarcely amounting to the least of what might be called angelic, as was given me to perceive by a communication of their joy, which was so slight that it seemed like something of a coldish quality, and yet to them it appeared otherwise, and they called it most heavenly, because it was their inmost; hence it was evident, not only that there are different degrees of life and joy, but also that the inmost of one degree scarcely reaches to the outermost or middle of another; and further, that when any one receives his own inmost degree, he is then in possession of his own heavenly joy, and cannot bear an interior degree, but would find it painful.*

# GENESIS.

## CHAPTER THE SIXTH.

### OF HEAVEN AND HEAVENLY JOY.

547. The souls who enter the next life are all initially ignorant of the true nature of heaven and heavenly joy. Most imagine it is a kind of joy to which anyone may be admitted, regardless of how they lived—even if they have harbored hatred toward their neighbor or made light of adultery. They do not realize that heaven actually consists of mutual and chaste love, and that heavenly joy is the deep happiness that grows out of such love.

548. I have sometimes spoken with spirits who had recently arrived from this world concerning their eternal state. I pointed out to them that it was a matter of great importance for them to know who was the sovereign of this kingdom, what its constitution was, and what its specific form of government looked like. I noted that if people traveling to a foreign country in this world consider it vital to learn about these things, it is surely of even greater importance to be informed of them in the kingdom where they now are, and where they will live forever. Therefore, they needed to know that the **Lord** <note original: "Dominus">The author uses "the Lord" to refer to the Divine as the central ruler of the spiritual world.</note> alone was the King of heaven and the governor of the universe, for both must necessarily have the same ruler. Consequently, they were now the Lord’s subjects. Furthermore, I explained that the laws of His kingdom are eternal truths, based on that universal and essential law: *to love the Lord above all things, and their neighbor as themselves.* Indeed, I added that if they wished to be like the angels, they ought to love their neighbor **more** than themselves. Upon hearing this, they were struck dumb. <note>struck dumb: The spirits were likely shocked because the concept of prioritizing another's well-being above one's own is entirely contrary to the self-centered nature of the world they just left.</note>

<summary>This page describes the cold, statue-like appearance of spirits who rely on their own intellect and clarifies that heaven is a state of mutual love rather than a mere destination. It emphasizes that the fundamental law of heaven is to love others more than oneself, a concept that baffles newly arrived spirits.</summary>

<keywords>intelligence, self-reliance, heaven, heavenly joy, mutual love, the Lord, laws of heaven, neighborly love, spirits, angels</keywords>

<page-num>182</page-num>
->GENESIS. [CHAP. 6.<-

*...for even though they might have heard of such a teaching while in this world, they did not believe it. They were amazed that such love could exist even in heaven—specifically, that it was possible for someone to love their neighbor more than themselves. However, they were informed that every kind of good increases immensely in the next life. In this world, because of the imperfections of human nature and the influence of the physical body, few can go further than loving their neighbor as themselves. But once these physical obstacles are removed, true love becomes purer and is raised to an <term>angelic degree</term><note>angelic degree: A state of being where the soul is no longer restricted by earthly selfishness, allowing for a higher, more selfless form of love.</note>, which is to love one's neighbor more than oneself. Regarding whether such love is actually possible, they were told that many proofs exist even in our world. Examples include the <term>conjugal state</term><note>conjugal state: The relationship between married partners.</note>, where one spouse has been known to face death to save the other; mothers who would rather suffer hunger than see their children go without food; and even instances among birds and animals. The same is seen in the sincere love of friends, where one will face danger for another’s sake. Even in polite society, where this love is merely mimicked for the sake of manners, it is common for well-bred people to offer the best things to others out of civility. Finally, they were told that the very nature of true love is to do good for others, not for selfish reasons, but out of genuine, disinterested affection. Despite these arguments, those who were deeply rooted in self-love or who had been greedy for <term>filthy lucre</term><note>filthy lucre: A traditional phrase referring to money or profit gained in a shameful or dishonorable way.</note> in this world could not accept this teaching—the covetous least of all.*

*549. The angelic state is such that every individual shares their own happiness and joy with everyone else. In the next life, there is a shared and incredibly sensitive perception of thoughts and feelings. Because of this, every person communicates their joy to all others, and everyone else communicates theirs back to that individual. In this way, every person is like a center point for everyone else’s happiness. This is what is called the <term>celestial form</term><note>celestial form: The organized structure of heaven where everyone is interconnected in a web of mutual love.</note>. Therefore, as the number of people in the Lord’s kingdom increases, their collective happiness grows even greater; this is why the joy of heaven is beyond description. This total sharing occurs when people love others more than themselves. But if someone should value themselves more than others, then self-love takes over. Self-love shares nothing; it only projects its own selfish image, which is considered foul and defiled in heaven. As soon as such a selfish thought is sensed, it is immediately pushed away and rejected.*

*550. Just as every single part of the human body works together for the benefit of the whole, so it is in the kingdom of the Lord. The Lord's kingdom acts as a single entity and is called the* **GRAND MAN** <note>original Latin: "Maximus Homo". This is a central concept in this philosophy, suggesting that the entire heaven, with all its diverse societies, functions together like the organs and limbs of a single giant human being.</note>. *Within this Grand Man, every individual member contributes...*

<summary>This page explains that heavenly joy is rooted in "altruistic love," where individuals love others more than themselves, a concept that forms the "Grand Man"—the interconnected structure of the spiritual world.</summary>

*551. The universal heaven has relation to the Lord alone, and each and every one therein has the same relation, both in general and most singularly, as has been often proved to me by much experience; this relationship is the true cause and ground of order, of union, of mutual love and happiness; for by virtue thereof each individual regards the well-being and happiness of the whole body at large, and the body at large regards the well-being and happiness of each individual.*

*552. By like repeated experience I have been convinced, that all the joy and happiness known in heaven are from the Lord alone; one instance of which experience it is here permitted me to relate: I observed some <term>angelic spirits</term><note>In this context, these are individuals in the early stages of their heavenly life who are being prepared to become fully realized angels.</note> busily employed in forming a candlestick, with its sconces and decorations, all after a most exquisite taste, in honor of the Lord. It was given me to attend to them for an hour or two, during which time I was witness to the pains they took, in order that the whole and every part might be beautiful and <term>representative</term><note>representative: In the spiritual world, internal thoughts and affections are physically manifested as external objects that symbolize those inner states.</note>; they supposing that what they did was done independently and from themselves; but it was given me to perceive clearly, that it was not in their power to devise or invent any thing of themselves; at length after some hours they said, that they had constructed a most beautiful representative candlestick in honor of the Lord, whereat they rejoiced from the inmost ground of their hearts; but I told them, that they had neither devised nor constructed any part of the workmanship of themselves, but that the Lord alone had done it for them: at first they would scarcely believe what I said, but being angelic spirits, they received <term>illustration</term><note>illustration: A moment of spiritual enlightenment or clarity where the truth of a matter is suddenly understood.</note>, and confessed that it was really so. The same is true with respect to all other representatives, and with all and every thing belonging to affection and thought, and consequently with all heavenly joys and happinesses, that even the smallest of them all is from the Lord alone.*

*553. Such as are principled in mutual love, are continually advancing in heaven to the spring-time of their youth; and the more thousands of years they pass, they attain to a more joyous and delightful spring, and so continue on to eternity, with fresh increments of blessedness, according to their respective proficiencies and gradations of mutual love, charity, and faith. Those of the female sex, who had departed this life broken with the infirmities of old age, but after having lived in faith towards the Lord, in charity towards their neighbor, and in <term>conjugial love</term><note>original: "amor conjugialis". A technical term used by the author to describe a spiritual, eternal marriage-love that goes beyond mere physical attraction or civil contract.</note> with their husbands, after a succession of ages appear to advance towards the bloom of youth, with a beauty surpassing all description; for goodness and charity form their own image in such persons, and express their delights and beauties in every feature.*

<summary>This page explains that all heavenly happiness and creativity originate solely from the Lord, illustrating this with a story of spirits creating a symbolic candlestick. It also describes a "heavenly youthfulness" where those who lived in love and faith grow younger and more beautiful over thousands of years.</summary>

Those who have lived in faith towards the Lord, that is, in a faith grounded in charity, become such forms, or such beauties, in another life; all the angels are such forms with an infinite variety; and of these heaven is composed.*

## CHAPTER VI.

1. AND it came to pass, that man began to multiply himself on the faces of the ground, and daughters were born unto them.
2. And the sons of God saw the daughters of man that they were good; and they took to themselves wives of all that they chose.

4. There were <term>Nephilim</term><note>original: "Nephilim." Traditionally translated as "giants," the term literally refers to "those who have fallen." In this context, it refers to a specific group of people before the flood who were consumed by self-importance and false beliefs.</note> in the earth in those days; and especially after the sons of God came in unto the daughters of man, and they bare to them; the same became mighty men, who were of old, men of a name. <note>The phrase "men of a name" is a literal translation of the Hebrew idiom for "men of renown" or famous men.</note>
5. And Jehovah saw that the wickedness of man was multiplied on the earth, and that all the fashion of the thoughts of his heart was only evil every day.
6. 7. And Jehovah said, I will destroy man whom I have created, from off the faces of the ground, from man even to beast, even to the creeping thing and even to the fowl of the heavens, for it repenteth me that I have made them.
8. And Noah found grace in the eyes of Jehovah.

### THE INTERNAL SENSE.

560. BEFORE we proceed further, it may be expedient to relate the condition of the church before the flood. In general it resembled succeeding churches,—as the Jewish church before the Lord’s advent, and the Christian church, after his advent, because it had corrupted and adulterated the <term>knowledges</term><note>In this context, "knowledges" refers to the specific facts and intellectual understandings of spiritual truths.</note> of true faith: and specifically considered, its members in process of time conceived dreadful persuasions, and immersed the goods and truths of faith in their filthy lusts, to such a degree, that there were scarcely any remains left in them; and when they were reduced to this state, they were, so to speak, suffocated of themselves, inasmuch as man cannot live without *remains*; for remains, as was before observed, give man the capacity of receiving life above the brute creation; since from *remains*, or by *remains*, from the Lord, man has a capacity to be as man, to know what is good and true, to reflect upon each, consequently to think and reason; for remains alone are receptive of spiritual and <term>celestial life</term><note>The highest level of spiritual existence, characterized by love to the Lord rather than just intellectual faith.</note>.

These states, along with the goodness and truth they contain, are impressed upon the memory and are called <term>remains</term><note>A technical term in this theology referring to the "treasures" of innocence and kindness stored by God in a person's inner mind during childhood to be used later in life.</note>. These *remains* are preserved in man by the Lord and are stored up, without the person being aware of it, in their <term>internal man</term><note>The deeper, spiritual part of the human mind that is capable of receiving divine influence.</note>. They are carefully separated from the things that belong to man's <term>proprium</term><note>original: "proprium." A Latin term for one's "own" self or ego, which is naturally inclined toward selfish and worldly desires.</note>—that is, from evils and falsities. 

All these states are so perfectly preserved by the Lord that not even the smallest of them is lost. I have been allowed to know this by the fact that every state of a person's life, from infancy to extreme old age, not only *remains* in the next life but also returns. When these states return, they are exactly as they were during the person's time in this world. Thus, not only do the goodness and truth stored in the memory *remain* and return, but so do all the states of innocence and charity. When states of evil, falsehood, or wicked fantasies recur—which also *remain* and return down to the smallest detail—they are softened and balanced by the Lord’s divine influence through those earlier good states. From this, it is evident that unless a person had some *remains*, they could not possibly avoid eternal condemnation, as can be seen in the previous discussion in section 468.

562. The people who lived before the flood were eventually left almost entirely without *remains*. This was because of their specific nature; they were infected with terrible and foul persuasions regarding everything they thought about, and they were completely unwilling to let go of them. This was chiefly caused by self-love, which led them to believe they were like Gods and that whatever they thought was divine. This specific type of "persuasion" has never existed in any other people before or since, as it has a fatal and suffocating quality. Because of this, in the afterlife, these <term>antediluvians</term><note>A term for the people who lived "before the flood" (Latin: ante diluvium).</note> cannot associate with other spirits. When they appear, their presence robs others of the power to think through the sheer force of their stubborn beliefs. Other details about them will be discussed later in this work, by the Lord's mercy.

563. When a person is possessed by such a persuasion, they become like a sticky, glue-like substance. Goodness and truth become entangled in this substance, so that the things intended to be *remains* cannot be stored up, or if they are stored, they cannot be used. 564. Verse 1. *And it came to pass that man began to multiply himself on the faces of the ground, and daughters were born unto them.* By *man* <note>original: "homo"</note> is here signified the race of mankind existing at that time. By the *faces of the ground* is signified all that region where the church was planted. By *daughters* are here signified the things belonging to the will of that man, and consequently, his <term>lusts</term><note>In this context, "lusts" refers to any distorted desires or selfish cravings of the human will that have turned away from divine goodness.</note>.

565. That *man* here signifies the race of mankind existing at that time—specifically a race that was evil or corrupt—can be seen from the following passages: “My spirit shall not always reprove *man*, for he is flesh,” (verse 3). “The wickedness of *man* was multiplied on the earth, and the fashion of the thoughts of his heart was only evil,” (verse 5). “I will destroy *man* whom I have created,” (verse 7); and in the following chapter, (verses 21, 22): “All flesh died that crept upon the earth, and every *man*, in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of lives.” 

It was observed above regarding *man*, that the Lord alone is <term>Man</term><note>The author teaches that God is the only true "Human" or "Man," and humans only earn the title by receiving life and goodness from Him.</note>, and that from Him every celestial person, or the celestial church, is called *man*. For this reason, all others are called *men* to distinguish them from animals, regardless of their level of faith. Nevertheless, a person is not truly *man*, or distinct from the <term>brutes</term><note>Refers to animals or people acting on purely animalistic instincts.</note>, except by virtue of <term>remains</term><note>The preserved states of childhood innocence and truth mentioned on the previous page.</note>, which belong to the Lord. Therefore, even a wicked person is called *man* because he possesses these *remains* from the Lord; without them, he would not be a *man* at all, but the vilest of animals.

566. That the *faces of the ground* signify the entire region where the church existed is evident from the meaning of *ground*. In the Word of God, a precise distinction is made between *ground* and *earth*. By *ground* <note>original: "humus" or Hebrew "adamah"</note> is everywhere signified the church, or something relating to the church; this is also where the name of man, or *Adam*, is derived, which means *ground*. By *earth* <note>original: "terra"</note> is meant a place where the church is not, or where there is nothing relating to the church. For example, in the first chapter of Genesis, only *earth* is mentioned, because at that stage there was no church or <term>regenerate man</term><note>A person who has undergone a spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note>. In the second chapter, *ground* is mentioned for the first time because by then a church existed. 

In the same way, it is said here and in the next chapter (verses 4, 23) that *every substance should be destroyed from off the faces of the ground*, meaning the region where the church was. In that same chapter (verse 3), when speaking of a church about to be created, it says, “to make seed alive on the faces of the ground.” *Ground* has this same meaning in other parts of the Bible, such as in Isaiah: “Jehovah will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and will set them in their ground, and the people shall take...

### 567.
All that region is called the tract of the church, where those inhabit who are instructed in the doctrine of the true faith;—as the land of Canaan, when the Jewish church was planted therein, and as Europe, where the Christian church now is;—the lands and countries, which are without, are not tracts of the church, or *faces of the ground*. Where the church was before the deluge, may also appear from the lands, which the rivers encompassed that came forth from the garden of Eden, by which in all parts of the Word are likewise described the boundaries of the land of Canaan; it is evident also from what follows concerning the *Nephilim that were in the land*: that these <term>Nephilim</term><note>A Hebrew term (נְפִילִים) often translated as "giants," used here to represent powerful delusions or those who have fallen away from spiritual truth.</note> dwelt in the land of Canaan, is plain from what is said of *the sons of Anak, that they were of the giants*, (Numbers 13:33.)

### 568.

The present passage treats of man in a corrupt state, who has no will, but mere lust instead of will, which is supposed by him to be will, and is also so denominated; and as what is predicated is always determined in its signification by the quality of the thing whereof it is predicated, so as *man* means here man in a corrupt state, as was shown above, it is of this of which *daughters* are predicated.
