### 569.
Verse 2. *And the sons of God saw the daughters of man that they were good, and they took to themselves wives of all that they chose.* By the sons of God are signified the <term>doctrinals of faith</term><note>The specific teachings, principles, or "rules" that constitute a religious belief system.</note>; by daughters, here as before, lusts: by the sons of God seeing the daughters of man that they were good, and taking to themselves wives of all that they chose, is signified, that the doctrinals of faith conjoined themselves with lusts, and this, indeed, indiscriminately.

### 570.
By the *sons of God* are signified <term>doctrinals of faith</term>, as is manifest from the signification of *sons* just given, and also in the preceding chapter, verse 4, where *sons* signified the truths of the church. The truths of the church are doctrinals, which being derived, in the present instance, by tradition from the most ancient people, were real truths, and therefore are called *the sons of God*;—this name is also given them respectively, because lusts are denominated *the daughters of man*. The quality of the members of this church is here described, namely, that they immersed the truths of the church, which were holy, in <term>cupidities</term><note>Derived from the Latin "cupiditas," meaning strong, often selfish or worldly desires and lusts.</note>, and thereby defiled them; hence also they confirmed their principles already most deeply rooted in the ground of <term>persuasion</term><note>In this work, "persuasion" refers to a state where a person is so convinced of their own false ideas that they can no longer see the truth.</note>. How this occurred may be easily conceived by any one, from observing what passes in himself and others: those who persuade themselves in regard to any subject, confirm themselves in such persuasion by every thing which they imagine to be true, even by what they find contained in the Word of the Lord; for whilst they adhere to principles which they have received, and rooted in themselves by persuasion, they force every thing to favor and flatter those principles, and the more any one is under the influence of self-love, so much the more he confirms himself in them. Such was this people here described, of whom, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said in the following pages, when we come to treat of their direful persuasions, which are of such an extraordinary nature, that it is never permitted them to enter into other spirits by <term>influx</term><note>The spiritual process by which thoughts, feelings, or energy flow from one being or state into another.</note> from their reasonings, because they would thus destroy the rational principle of such spirits, but only to enter by influx from their cupidities. Hence it appears what is signified by *the sons of God seeing the daughters of man that they were good, and taking to themselves wives of all that they chose*, namely, that the doctrinals of faith joined themselves with lusts, and this, indeed, without distinction.

### 572. 
*And Jehovah said, My spirit shall not always reprove man, for that he is flesh; and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.* By Jehovah's saying, *My spirit shall not always reprove man*, is signified, that man would not be so led any longer; *for that he is flesh* signifies, because he was become <term>corporeal</term><note>Focused entirely on the physical body and worldly senses, rather than spiritual matters.</note>; *and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years* signifies, that he ought to have *remains* of faith;—it is also a prediction concerning a future church.

### 573. 
By Jehovah's saying, *My spirit shall not always reprove man*, is signified, that man would not be so led any longer, as is evident from what precedes and follows;—from what precedes, because they were reduced to such a state by the immersion of the doctrinals or truths of faith into their lusts, as to be no longer capable of reproof, or of being taught what evil was, for the <term>perceptive faculty</term><note>The ability to intuitively sense truth and goodness without having to be taught or reason it out; a trait attributed to the earliest humans.</note>, necessary for the discernment of truth and goodness, was entirely extinguished by persuasions, so that they thought that alone to be true which was agreeable to their persuasions. It is also evident from what follows, because the man of the church, which succeeded the flood, was altogether differently formed, being gifted with <term>conscience</term> instead of <term>perception</term>, by means of which he was capable of reproof; wherefore by *reproof from the spirit of Jehovah*, is signified an internal dictate, perception, or conscience; and by the *spirit of Jehovah* the influx of truth and goodness; as appears also from Isaiah: "I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth, for the spirit would fail before me and the souls which I have made," (lvii. 16.)

### 574.

In David: "Thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all *flesh* come," (Psalm lxv. 2;) where *flesh* denotes every man. In Jeremiah: "Cursed is the man that trusteth in man, and maketh *flesh* his arm," (xvii. 5;) where *flesh* signifies man, and arm power. And in Ezekiel: "That all *flesh* may know," (xxi. 4, 5;) and in Zechariah: "Be silent, <unclear>O all flesh, before the Lord</unclear>" <note>Original text cuts off; the verse is Zechariah 2:13.</note>

That the land of Canaan <note>original: "terra Canaan"</note>, or the holy land, is taken for love, and consequently for the will of the celestial man <note>The "celestial man" refers to a person who acts from a state of pure love and goodness rather than just obedience to rules.</note>, might be proved by many passages from the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used here for the Holy Scriptures.</note>; in the like manner, that the *lands* of the different nations are used to signify the different kinds of love prevalent in the inhabitants, which in general are self-love and the love of the world; but as such passages occur so very frequently, it would be tedious to transcribe them. The *fashion of the thoughts of the heart being only evil continually*, signifies that there was no perception of truth and good, by reason, as has been said and shown, that they immersed the doctrinals of faith in their filthy lusts, and when this occurred, all perception was lost, and in the place thereof a dreadful persuasion succeeded, or a most deep-rooted and deadly phantasy, which was, moreover, the cause of their extinction and suffocation. A *fashion* is that which man *fashions* to himself, and of which he is self-persuaded, as in Habakkuk: "What profiteth a graven image, that the *fashioner* thereof hath graven it? the molten image and teacher of lies, that the *fashioner* trusteth to his *fashion*, to make dumb idols," (ii. 18:) a *graven image* signifies false persuasions originating in principles self-conceived and brought forth: the *fashioner* is one who is thus self-persuaded, of whom the *fashion* [or thing fashioned] is predicated. So in Isaiah: "Shall the potter be reputed as the clay, that the work should say to him that made it, He made me not; and the thing *fashioned* say to him that fashioned it, He had no understanding?" (xxix. 16:) the *thing fashioned* here signifies thought originating in <term>proprium</term> <note>Proprium refers to the human "selfhood" or the ego—that which a person considers their own, which in this theology is the source of all evil and falsity when separated from the Divine.</note>, and the persuasion of false thence derived. **586.** Verse 6. *And it repented Jehovah that he made man on the earth, and it grieved Him at His heart.* He repented, signifies mercy: *he grieved at the heart*, has a like signification: *to repent* respects wisdom; *to grieve at the heart* respects love.

**587.** Jehovah’s repenting that he made man upon the earth signifies mercy, and *his grieving at heart* has a like signification, as is evident from this circumstance, that Jehovah never repents, because He foresees all and every thing from eternity; and when he made man, that is, created him anew, and perfected him till he became <term>celestial</term> <note>In this context, "celestial" refers to the highest state of human development, characterized by pure love for the Divine.</note>, he also foresaw, that in process of time he would become such as here described, and because he foresaw that he would become such he could not repent Himself; which appears plainly from what Samuel said: “The invincible One of Israel doth not lie, nor repent, for He is not a man that he should repent,” (1 Sam. xv. 29.) And in Moses: “God is not a man that He should lie, or the son of man that he should repent; hath He said, and shall He not do; or hath He spoken, and shall He not make it good?” (Numb. xxiii. 19.) 

But *to repent* signifies to be merciful. The mercy of Jehovah, or of the Lord, involves all and every thing done by the Lord towards mankind, who are in such a state, that the Lord pities them, and each one according to his state; thus He pities the state of him whom He permits to be punished, and pities him also to whom he grants the enjoyment of good; it is of mercy to be punished, because mercy turns all the evil of punishment into good; and it is of mercy to grant the enjoyment of good, because no one merits any thing that is good; for all mankind are evil, and of himself every one would rush into hell, where-fore it is a mercy that he is delivered thence; nor is it any thing but mercy, inasmuch as He has need of no man. Mercy has its name from the circumstance of its delivering man from miseries and from hell; thus it is called mercy in respect to mankind, because they are in such a state of misery, and is the effect of love towards all, because they are so.

**588.** But repentance and grief of heart are predicated of the Lord, because such appear to be in all human mercy, where-fore what is said here of the Lord’s *repenting* and *grieving*, is spoken according to appearance, as in many other passages in the Word. What the mercy of the Lord is, none can know, because it infinitely transcends the understanding of man: but what the mercy of man is, man knows that it is to repent and grieve; and unless man were to form his idea of mercy according to his own apprehension, he could not have any conception of it, and thus he could not be instructed; and this is the reason why the Lord’s qualities are described by human properties, especially that he punishes, that he leads into temptation, that he destroys, and that he is angry, when yet he never punishes, never leads into temptation, never destroys, and is never angry.

It emphasizes that God's foreknowledge is absolute and His actions are always rooted in love and mercy, even when they involve punishment.</summary>

590. *To repent relates to wisdom, and to grieve at heart relates to love. This cannot be explained to human understanding except through human ideas—that is, through appearances.* In every human thought, there is something derived from the understanding and something from the will (or from the <term>thinking-principle</term> and the <term>love-principle</term> <note>These terms refer to the two basic faculties of the human mind: the ability to process information (thought) and the driving force of desires and intentions (will/love).</note>). Any idea that does not contain something from the will or love is not truly an idea, for otherwise, a person could not think at all. There is a constant and inseparable marriage between thought and will; consequently, the things of the will or love are always present within the ideas of thought. 

From this human perspective, it is possible to understand—at least through a simplified idea—what is contained in the Lord's mercy: namely, wisdom and love. Thus, in the prophets, especially in Isaiah, two expressions are generally used for every occasion: one involves what is <term>spiritual</term> and the other what is <term>celestial</term>. <note>In this theological framework, "spiritual" refers to the intellect and truth, while "celestial" refers to the heart, will, and love.</note> The spiritual aspect of the Lord’s mercy is wisdom; the celestial aspect is love.

Thus, it is to be understood here how it is said of *Jehovah* that *He would destroy man*, when in fact it was man himself who destroyed and extinguished himself.

The *Most Ancient Church* enjoyed immediate revelation by consort with spirits and angels, and also by visions and dreams, from the Lord, by virtue whereof it was given them to know in general what was good and true, and when they had attained such general knowledge, then by means of perceptions they confirmed those general ideas as a sort of principles in innumerable instances, which innumerable instances were the particulars, or <term>singulars</term> <note>In this context, "singulars" refers to the smallest, individual components or specific examples of a general truth.</note> of the general ideas to which they had relation; thus general ideas as principles were every day strengthened and confirmed; whatsoever was not in agreement with those general ideas, they perceived was not true, and whatsoever was in agreement, they perceived to be true:—such is the state also of the celestial angels. 

In the *Most Ancient Church* these general principles were celestial and eternal truths; as that the Lord rules the universe, that all goodness and truth are from the Lord, that all life is from the Lord, that man's <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium"; a Latin term referring to one's "own" self or ego, which the author describes as being inherently void of life and goodness.</note> is nothing but evil, and that in itself it is dead; besides many other truths of a like nature; in all which they received a perception from the Lord respecting the innumerable things tending to confirm them, and to harmonize with them: love with them was the principal of faith, and by means of love it was given them of the Lord to perceive whatever had relation to faith, in consequence whereof faith with them was love, as was said above. But it was very different with the *Ancient Church*, as will be shown, by the divine mercy of the Lord, in its proper place.

598. The phrase ***finding grace in the eyes of Jehovah*** signifies that the Lord foresaw a way for humanity to be saved. This is evident from the following points: The Lord’s <term>mercy</term> <note>In this context, mercy is the divine love reaching down to those who are in a state of love and goodness.</note> inherently concerns the salvation of the entire human race, and the same is true for ***grace***; therefore, the salvation of mankind is what is meant by ***grace***. By ***Noah*** is signified not only a <term>New Church</term> <note>Specifically the "Ancient Church," which began after the metaphorical flood.</note>, but also the specific faith of that church, which was a faith rooted in charity (love in action). Thus, the Lord foresaw that through faith rooted in charity, the human race might be saved.

However, the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> makes a distinction between ***mercy*** and ***grace***, based on the different nature of the people receiving them. ***Mercy*** is applied to those who are <term>celestial</term> <note>The "celestial" are those guided primarily by their hearts and a direct love for the Divine.</note>, while ***grace*** is applied to those who are <term>spiritual</term> <note>The "spiritual" are those guided by their intellect, conscience, and a sense of duty.</note>. This is because the celestial acknowledge nothing but ***mercy***, whereas the spiritual acknowledge almost nothing but ***grace***. The celestial do not truly know what ***grace*** is, and the spiritual hardly know what ***mercy*** is, often treating them as the same thing. This difference arises from the way each group experiences humility: those who are in a state of "humiliation of heart" plead for the Lord's ***mercy***, but those in a state of "humiliation of thought" petition for ***grace***. If the spiritual do pray for mercy, it is usually only during times of trial <note>original: "tentatio" (temptation or spiritual struggle)</note>, or they say it with their lips rather than their hearts. Because the New Church called ***Noah*** was not celestial but spiritual, it is described as having found ***grace***, rather than ***mercy***, in the eyes of Jehovah.

The distinction made in the Bible between ***mercy*** and ***grace*** is clear from many passages where Jehovah is called both "merciful" and "gracious," such as in Psalm 103:8, 111:4, 112:4, and Joel 2:13. They are also distinguished in other passages, such as in Jeremiah:

> “Thus says Jehovah: The people who survived the sword found ***grace*** in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to give him rest. Jehovah appeared to me from far away, saying: I have loved you with an everlasting love <note>original: "charitate saeculi" (love of an age/everlasting love)</note>; therefore with ***mercy*** have I drawn you.” (Jeremiah 31:2, 3)

In this passage, ***grace*** refers to the spiritual principle and ***mercy*** refers to the celestial principle. Similarly, in Isaiah:

> “Therefore Jehovah will wait to give ***grace*** to you, and therefore He will lift Himself up to have ***mercy*** on you.” (Isaiah 30:18)

Here, ***grace*** again relates to what is spiritual, and ***mercy*** to what is celestial. This is also seen when Lot says to the angels:

> “See now, your servant has found ***grace*** in your eyes, and you have shown great ***mercy*** to me by saving my life <note>original: "vivificando animam meam" (making my soul alive/vivifying my soul)</note>.” (Genesis 19:19)

***Grace*** relates to spiritual things, such as faith or the understanding—which is why Lot is said to have found grace in the *eyes* of the angels—while ***mercy*** relates to celestial things, such as love or the will, which is why the angel is said to have "done mercy" and "given life to the soul."

## THE INTERNAL SENSE.

605. It now treats of the formation of a new church <note>In this context, a "church" refers to a specific state of religious and spiritual life among humanity in a particular era.</note>, which is named *Noah*, and its formation is described by *the ark, into which were received living things of every kind*; but before that new church could exist, the man of the church, as is usual, must needs endure many temptations <note>Spiritual struggles or crises of faith.</note>, which are described by the elevation, fluctuation, and continuance of that ark on *the waters of the flood*; and at length, his becoming a true spiritual man, and being set at liberty, is described by *the cessation of the waters, and several things which follow*. 

It is impossible for any one to see these spiritual contents, who abides only in the sense of the letter, for this reason particularly, because all these things have an historical connection, and suggest the idea of a history of events; but such was the style of writing at that time, which to those ancient people was most agreeable—namely, that all things should be involved in types <note>Symbols or allegories where physical things represent spiritual realities.</note>, and these types be reduced to, and connected in, some historical arrangement; and the more perfect such connection was, so much the more suitable was it to their genius and temper; for in those ancient times they did not apply themselves so much to the sciences, as men do at this day, but to profound thoughts, from whence resulted such historical arrangements. This was the wisdom of the ancients.

606. *The flood, the ark, and consequently the things described concerning the flood and the ark, signify regeneration, and also the temptations which precede it, as is known in some measure to the learned at this day, by whom regeneration and temptations are likewise compared to the waters of a flood.*

That *just* has relation to the <term>good of charity</term> <note>The active practice of neighborly love and kindness.</note>, and *upright* to the <term>truth of charity</term> <note>The principles or laws of faith that are lived out through love.</note>, is evident from the Word; as in Isaiah: "They shall seek me daily, and shall desire the knowledge of my ways, as a nation that doeth *justice*, and doth not forsake the *judgment* of their God; they shall ask of me the *judgments of justice*; they shall desire the approaching of God," (lviii. 2;) where *judgment* signifies what has relation to truth, and *justice* what has relation to good: to do *judgment and justice* was a customary form of speech denoting what is true and good, (as Isaiah lvi. 1; Jerem. xxii. 3, 15; xxiii. 5; xxxiii. 15; Ezek. xxxiii. 14, 16, 19.) The Lord said, "The *just* shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of my Father," (Matt. xiii. 43;) signifying those who are principled in charity: also, speaking of the consummation of the age, he said, "The angels shall go forth, and shall sever the wicked from the midst of the *just*," verse 49 of the same chapter; signifying likewise those who are in the good of charity. But *upright* <note>original: "integer," meaning whole, complete, or blameless.</note> signifies what is true originating in charity; for truth may be derived from sundry origins, but that which originates in the good of charity from the Lord, is called *upright*, and an *upright man*; as in David: "Who shall sojourn in thy tent? who shall dwell in the mountain of thy holiness? he that walketh *upright*, and doeth *justice*, and speaketh the truth in his heart," (Psalm xv. 1, 2;) giving a description of the *upright*. So again: "With the holy thou behavest thyself holily, with the upright man thou showest thyself *upright*," (Psalm xviii. 25;) where an *upright man* signifies one who is principled in the holy principle or good of charity. Again: "Jehovah will not withhold good from them that walk in *uprightness*," (Psalm lxxxiv. 11.) That an *upright man* is one who is in truth from a principle of good, or who speaks and does what is true from charity, is evident from this consideration, that the expressions to *walk*, and *way*, and also *right*, or *rectitude*, which relate to truth, are often applied to the *upright* or to *uprightness*; as in David: "I will inform the *upright* in the *way*, when will he come unto me? I will *walk* in the *uprightness* of my heart in the midst of my house," (Psalm ci. 2;) and again: "He that *walketh* in the *way* of the *upright* shall minister unto me," verse 6, of the same Psalm; and again: "Blessed are the *upright* in the *way*, who *walk* in the law of Jehovah," (Psalm cxix. 1;) and again: "*Uprightness* and rectitude shall guard me," (Psalm xxv. 21;) and again: "Mark the *upright*, and behold the *right*, for the end of that man is peace," (Psalm xxxvii. 37.) Hence it appears that he is called *just*, who does good, and he *upright*, who does what is true from a good principle, which also is to do *justice and judgment*: holiness and *justice* are the <term>celestial principle</term> <note>The highest level of spiritual consciousness, characterized by a direct, heart-felt love for God.</note> of faith; *uprightness* <note>original: "integritas," meaning integrity or wholeness.</note> and *judgment*, are the <term>spiritual principle</term> <note>The second level of spiritual consciousness, characterized by a love for truth and neighborly charity.</note> thence derived.

613. From the sense of the letter, which is historical, it appears that "generations" refers to a family lineage. However, since this text deals exclusively with internal, spiritual matters, **generations** signify the things that belong to faith. It is also clear from the surrounding context that "generations" cannot be understood in any other way. In the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, this same meaning often appears, as in Isaiah: “They shall build of thee the old waste places; thou shalt raise up the foundations of generation and generation, and thou shalt be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in,” (Isaiah 58:12 <note>The source cites this as lvi. 12, but it corresponds to chapter 58 in modern Bibles.</note>). In this passage, every expression signifies something related to faith: *the old waste places* signify the celestial things of faith <note>"Celestial" refers to things of the heart or love.</note>, and *the foundations of generation and generation* signify the spiritual things of faith <note>"Spiritual" refers to things of the intellect or truth.</note>. So again in the same prophet: “They shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of *generation and generation*,” (Isaiah 61:4); here the word *generation* is used in the same sense as before. Again in the same prophet: “They shall not labor in vain, nor generate to perturbation, for they are the seed of the blessed of Jehovah, and their *offspring* with them,” (Isaiah 65:23); in this passage, *to generate* is predicted of the things of faith, and *to labor* of the things of love. The latter are called *the seed of the blessed of Jehovah*, while the former are called *offspring*.

614. *To walk with God* signifies the <term>doctrine of faith</term> <note>The systematic teaching or set of principles that a person believes and follows.</note>, as may be seen in the explanation provided earlier concerning <term>Enoch</term> (Chapter 5:22, 24), of whom it is also said that *he walked with God*. In that instance, it signified the doctrine of faith preserved for the use of future generations; and since Noah’s people were the very descendants for whom that doctrine was preserved, the phrase is now repeated.

615. The nature of the person belonging to this church is described here in general terms. This does not describe what he was at that exact moment—for his actual formation is described later—but rather what he was capable of becoming. Specifically, through the knowledge of faith, he might be gifted with <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is not just giving to the poor, but a fundamental love and kindness toward one's neighbor.</note>, act from that charity, and through the "good" of that charity, recognize what is true. This is why the "good" of charity (the *just*) is mentioned first, followed by the "truth" of charity (the *upright*). Charity, as previously stated, consists of love toward our neighbor and mercy. It is a degree of love lower than that which existed in the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>According to this theology, the "Most Ancient Church" was the very first state of humanity, characterized by a direct, heart-centered love for the Divine.</note>, which was love toward the Lord. Thus, love "descended" or shifted to a more external form, which is called charity.

616. Verse 10. *And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth*. By <term>Noah’s begetting three sons</term> is signified that three kinds of doctrines originated from that state, which are represented by the names <term>Shem</term>, <term>Ham</term>, and <term>Japheth</term>.

620. Here the *earth* denotes the race, in which the all of celestial love, and of the church, was lost: for the subject always determines the predicate.

634. It is quite difficult to explain exactly what the "understanding of truth" and the "will of good" are in their true sense. This confusion arises partly from the way we use language and partly because humanity is currently focused almost entirely on physical, bodily concerns—living life on the most external level. Because of this, people are unaware that there are deeper levels within every human being: an interior level, a more interior level, and an **inmost** level. The <term>corporeal and sensual principle</term> <note>The lowest level of the human mind, which deals only with physical sensations and bodily needs.</note> is the outermost or lowest level. Above that, the "first interiors" consist of our basic desires and memories. Higher still are our rational thoughts and deeper affections. At the very center—the inmost—reside the **will of good** and the **understanding of truth**. All these layers are as distinct from one another as possible. A person focused only on the physical world lumps all these levels together, confusing them into one.

The *Most Ancient Church*, as has been frequently noted, knew whatever related to faith through love; or, what is the same, they possessed an understanding of truth through a will for what is good. However, their descendants, leaning through hereditary corruption toward the rule of their own lusts, immersed the doctrines of faith into those lusts, and thus became <term>the fallen ones</term> <note>original: "Nephilim" — a Hebrew term often translated as giants, here interpreted as those who have "fallen" into their own selfish desires.</note>. When the Lord foresaw that if man continued in such a nature, he would perish eternally, He ordered and provided that the <term>will-principle</term> <note>The fundamental faculty of the mind that drives choice, love, and desire.</note> should be separated from the intellectual principle. In this way, man would be formed not by a will for good as before, but through an understanding of truth he would be gifted with charity, which appears like a will for good. This new church, which is called *Noah*, was dealt with in this way, and therefore was of an entirely different nature and character from the *Most Ancient Church*. Besides this church, there were also others at that time, such as the church called *Enoch* (mentioned above in chapter 4:25, 26) and several others whose descriptions are not preserved. The church of *Noah* is described alone here because its character was entirely different from that of the *Most Ancient Church*.

For instance, **length**, when applied to **time**, signifies that which is perpetual and eternal, as in "length of days" (Psalm 23:6; 21:5). 651. **Verse 16.** *A window shalt thou make to the ark, and to a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; lowest, second, and third [mansions] shalt thou make it.* By the window, which was to be finished to a cubit above, is signified the intellectual faculty. By the door on the side is signified the sense of hearing. By the **lowest, secondary, and third** levels are signified <term>scientifics</term> <note>factual knowledge or data stored in the memory</note>, <term>rationals</term> <note>the faculty of reasoning and logic</note>, and <term>intellectuals</term> <note>the higher capacity for understanding spiritual truths</note>.

652. The window signifies the intellectual faculty and the door signifies hearing; thus, this verse deals with the intellectual part of the human being. This is evident from what was stated previously: that the people of this specific "church" or spiritual era were reformed in this manner. There are two lives within a human: one belongs to the will (the heart and desires), and the other to the understanding (the mind). These become two separate lives when the will is lost and replaced by mere lust. When this happens, the other part—the intellectual part—is what can then be reformed. Through this reformed intellect, a new will can later be given by God, so that the two may again form a single life consisting of charity and faith. Because the people at that time had no true will, but only lust, the part of the mind related to the will was closed off (as mentioned in verse 14), and the intellectual part was opened, which is what this verse describes.

Those spirits who excite lusts are kept entirely away. There are two kinds of evil spirits: those who target a person's reasonings, and those who target their lusts. The spirits who stir up reasonings bring out all of a person’s <term>falses</term> <note>incorrect or distorted spiritual principles</note> and try to convince them that these falsehoods are truths; they even try to turn actual truths into lies. During these times of trial, a person must fight against these influences. However, it is not actually the person who fights, but the Lord who fights on their behalf using angels who are joined to the person. Once these <term>falses</term> are separated and dispersed through these struggles, the person is prepared and able to receive the truths of faith. **654.** This agrees with what is at this day acknowledged in all churches, that faith comes by hearing. But faith is by no means a mere knowledge only of those things which relate to faith, for this is only <term>science</term> <note>meaning factual or academic knowledge, rather than the modern definition of laboratory science</note>: but it is acknowledgment; however acknowledgment cannot possibly exist in any one, unless he be possessed of the principle of faith which is charity, that is, love towards his neighbor, and mercy: where charity is, there is acknowledgment, or there is faith, and he who conceives of the matter otherwise, is as far from the knowledge of faith, as earth is far or away from heaven: when charity is present, which is the good of faith, then acknowledgment is present, which is the truth of faith: wherefore during man's regeneration according to <term>scientifics</term> <note>factual data stored in the memory</note>, <term>rationals</term> <note>the capacity for logical reasoning</note>, and <term>intellectuals</term> <note>the higher faculty of understanding spiritual truth</note>, it is with a view to prepare the ground, or his mind, for the reception of charity, so that afterwards he may think and act from charity, or the life of charity, at which time, and not before, he is reformed and regenerated.

# GENESIS.
## [Chap. vi.

The <term>celestial marriage</term> <note>a spiritual state where love and wisdom are united in a person’s soul, mirroring the union of the Lord and Heaven</note>, or conjunction, exists only with those who are <term>regenerated</term> <note>those undergoing "regeneration," or the process of spiritual rebirth</note>, thus <term>regeneration</term> itself in a most extended sense is signified by a *covenant*; for the Lord enters into a covenant with man when he regenerates him; wherefore with the ancients this alone was represented by a covenant. It is conceived from the literal sense of the Word, that the covenant entered into with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and so frequently with their descendants, had regard merely to them as particular persons, whereas they were such as to be incapable of being regenerated, inasmuch as they placed worship in externals, and supposed external things to be holy without reference to their connection with internal things, wherefore the covenants entered into with them were but <term>representations</term> <note>external people, objects, or actions that serve as symbols for internal, spiritual truths</note> of regeneration. This also was the case with all their rites and ceremonies, and likewise with Abraham himself, Isaac, and Jacob, who represented the things relating to love and faith; so also the high-priests and priests, of every description, even the most wicked, could represent the celestial and most holy priesthood. In representations it is not the *person* but the *thing* which is represented; thus all the kings of Israel and Judah, even the worst, represented the regal office or dominion of the Lord; yea, so did even Pharaoh, who exalted Joseph over the land of Egypt; hence and from many other considerations, which, by the divine mercy of the Lord, will be seen in the following pages, it may appear that the covenants so frequently entered into with the children of Jacob, were nothing else but representative rituals.

666. A covenant signifies nothing but regeneration, and what relates to regeneration, as may appear from the Word throughout, where the Lord himself is called a *covenant*, because it is he alone who regenerates, and is looked up to by the regenerate man, and who is the all in all of love and faith. That the Lord is the real essential covenant appears in Isaiah:
> “I, <term>Jehovah</term> <note>the Hebrew name for the Lord, signifying the Divine Being</note>, have called thee in righteousness, and hold thy hand and keep thee, and will give thee for a *covenant* of the people, for a light to the <term>Gentiles</term> <note>historically meaning non-Jewish nations, but here symbolizing those who are in ignorance of the truth but possess a desire for good</note>,” (xlii. 6:)

where covenant means the Lord, and *the light of the Gentiles* faith: (in like manner, xlix. 6, 8.) So in Malachi:
> “Behold, I send my angel, and the Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to his temple, and the angel of the covenant whom ye desire; behold he cometh; but who may abide the day of his coming?” (iii. 1, 2;)

where the Lord is called the *angel of the covenant*. The Sabbath is called an eternal covenant, (Exod. xxxi. 16,) because it signifies the Lord Himself, and the celestial man regenerated by him. Inasmuch as the Lord is the real essential covenant, it is evident that a covenant is all that which joins man with the Lord, consequently it is love and faith, and whatever appertains to love and faith; for those things are of the Lord, and the Lord is in them, consequently the real essential covenant.

667. *By his entering into the ark, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives, is signified, that he should be saved, as appears from what was said above, and from its being subsequently stated that he was saved, because he was regenerated.*

668. Sons are truths, and wives are goods, as was shown above, (chapter v. 4 :) where they are called *sons and daughters*, but here *sons and wives*, because *wives* are those goods which are adjoined to truths. It is not possible for any truth to be produced, unless from good, or delight. In good and delight there is life, but not in truth, except so far as it receives it from good and delight; from this truth is formed, and shoots forth in the way of <term>spiritual growth</term>, as also does <term>faith</term> (which appertains to truth,) originating in love, which appertains to good. Truth in this respect is like light, which cannot have birth except from the sun, or some sort of flame, and is thence alone formed; truth is only the form of good, and faith is only the form of love; truth is thence formed according to the quality of good, and faith according to the quality of love or charity <note>In this system, "charity" is the outward expression of "love," and "faith" is the outward form of that internal spark.</note>.

### 667—671.] GENESIS.

This then is the reason why *wife* and *wives*, which signify goods joined to truths, are here mentioned; hence also it is said in the following verse, that *pairs of all should enter into the ark, male and female*; for without goods being joined to truths, there is no <term>regeneration</term> <note>the process of being spiritually reborn through a change in heart and mind</note>.

669. Verse 19. *And of every living thing of all flesh, pairs of all, shalt thou cause to enter into the ark, to be made alive with thee; they shall be male and female.* By the *living soul* <note>original Latin: "anima vivente"</note> are signified those things which belong to the <term>understanding</term> <note>the faculty of the mind associated with thought, logic, and the reception of truth</note>; by *all flesh*, the things which belong to the <term>will</term> <note>the faculty of the mind associated with desire, love, and the reception of good</note>: by causing *pairs of all to enter into the ark*, is signified their regeneration: *male* is truth, *female* is good.

670. By the *living soul* are signified the things which belong to the understanding, and by *flesh* the things which belong to the will, as may appear from what has been said above, and also from what follows: by the *living soul* is signified, in the Word <note>a term for Sacred Scripture or the Bible</note>, every animal in general of every kind, (as in chapter i. verses 20, 21, 24; chapter ii. verse 19.) But here, because *all flesh* is immediately joined to it, it signifies the things which belong to the understanding, for a reason mentioned above: that the man of this church <note>referring to the "Ancient Church" symbolized by Noah</note> was to be regenerated first as to <term>intellectuals</term> <note>the parts of the mind dealing with the intellect</note>, which is why in the following verse mention is made first of *fowl* <note>birds</note>, which signify intellectuals, or <term>rationals</term> <note>the capacity for reasoning</note>, and afterwards of *cattle*, which signify the things pertaining to the will: *flesh* signifies in particular the corporeal <note>physical or bodily</note> part or principle, which belongs to the will.

671. By causing *pairs to enter into the ark to be made alive*, is signified their regeneration, as may appear from what was said in the preceding verse: that truths cannot be regenerated except by what is good and pleasant; consequently, those things which are of faith cannot be regenerated except by those things which are of charity. This is why it is said here that *pairs of all should enter*, that is, both of truths which belong to the understanding, and of goods which belong to the will. With a person who has not been regenerated, there exists neither a true understanding of truth nor a true will for good, though they only appear as if they existed and are called so in common conversation. There may, however, exist within such a person rational and scientific truths, but they are not "alive"; there may also exist a kind of "voluntary good" <note>original Latin: "voluntaria bona"; goods or kindnesses that stem from natural impulse or habit rather than spiritual rebirth</note> like that which exists among the Gentiles <note>those outside the church or without specific spiritual instruction</note>, or even among animals, but these are only similar to true good. They are never made alive in a person before he is regenerate, at which point they are given life by the Lord. In the other life <note>the spiritual world or afterlife</note>, it is very clearly perceived what is and what is not alive; truth which is not alive is instantly perceived as something material, like a mass of fibers or a shell; good which is not alive is perceived as something woody, bony, or stony. But truth and good given life by the Lord are open, vital, and full of what is spiritual and heavenly.

675. Still all these things can never be perfected to eternity, inasmuch as each particular genus, each particular species, and each particular state, comprehends indefinite things in simple objects, and much more when compounded. Man does not indeed know that this is the case, and still less does he know how he is regenerated; this is what the Lord declares to Nicodemus <note>a Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin mentioned in the Gospel of John</note> concerning the regeneration of man, when he says, “The spirit bloweth where it willeth, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, or whither it goeth; so is every one that is born of the spirit,” (John 3:8.)

677. With respect to the food of the man who is to be <term>regenerated</term> <note>the process of being spiritually reborn and transformed by God</note>, the case is this : before man can be regenerated, he must be furnished with all those things which may serve as means, that is, with the good and pleasant things of the affections, to serve as means in the <term>will</term> <note>the faculty of the mind driven by desire and love</note> ; and with truths from the Word of the Lord, and every other source from which those truths may be confirmed, for his <term>understanding</term> <note>the faculty of the mind driven by thought and logic</note>. Previously to man's being furnished with such things, he cannot be regenerated : such things are *meats* <note>an older English term for food in general</note> or *food*, which is the reason why man is incapable of being regenerated until he arrives at adult age : but every man has his peculiar, and as it were proper *foods*, which are provided for him by the Lord, before he is regenerated.

678. By *taking to him of all food that is eaten*, are signified things good and pleasant, as may appear from what has been already said, that the life of man is constituted by things good and pleasant, not so much by truths, for truths receive their life from what is good and pleasant. No scientific <note>referring to acquired knowledge or facts</note> and rational idea which man acquires, from infancy to old age, is ever insinuated into him except by what is good and pleasant ; which are therefore called *food* or *meats*, and are such because his soul lives from those things ; for without them the soul of man could not possibly live at all, as every one may know if he will but attend thereto.

679. Hence it appears, that by *gathering to him* are signified truths ; for to *gather* is predicated of those things which are in the memory of man, where they are gathered : it moreover implies, that both the former and the latter, that is goods and truths, should be gathered together in man before he is regenerated ; for without goods and truths so gathered, by which, as by means, the Lord may operate, it is impossible that man should ever be regenerated, as was said above : hence it now follows, that *being for food for him and them*, signifies both goods and truths.

680. Goods and truths are man's genuine *meats*, as may appear to every one, for as whosoever is deprived of them has not life, but is dead. The *meats*, with which his soul is fed, when he is dead <note>meaning spiritually dead, or focused entirely on worldly rather than heavenly life</note>, are the delights arising from evils, and the pleasures arising from <term>falses</term> <note>erroneous principles or beliefs that justify wrong actions</note>, which are the *meats of death* ; as also from corporeal, worldly, and natural things, which have nothing of life in them ; and moreover, such a man does not know what spiritual and celestial food is, insomuch that as often as mention is made of *meat*, or *bread*, in the Word <note>the Bible</note>, he imagines it to signify corporeal *food* ; thus in the Lord's Prayer, "Give us daily bread," he supposes to be a petition only for

681. What *celestial and spiritual food is*, can be best known in another life. The life of angels and spirits is not supported by any food like that of this world, but by every word which comes forth from the mouth of the Lord, as the Lord Himself teaches, (Matthew 4:4.) The fact is, that the Lord alone is the life of all; from Him come all and every thing which angels and spirits think, speak, and do; and not only those which are angels and good spirits, but also those which are evil spirits: the reason why the latter speak and do what is evil, is, because all the goods and truths, which are of the Lord, they thus receive, and pervert; for as is the form of the recipient, so is the reception and affection. 

This circumstance will admit of comparison with various objects which receive the light of the sun, and, according to their form and the disposition and determination of their parts, they turn the received light into unpleasing and ugly colors, or into such as are pleasing and beautiful. Thus the universal heaven and the universal world of spirits live by every thing which proceeds out of the mouth of the Lord, and every one has thence his life; nay, this is the case not only with heaven and the world of spirits, but also with the whole race of mankind. I am aware that men will not believe this; but from the continual experience of many years, I can positively assert that it is most true: the evil spirits in the world of spirits are also unwilling to believe this to be so, wherefore it is frequently proved to them by such lively and powerful demonstration, that they with indignation confess that it is so. If angels, spirits, and men, were deprived of this food, they would expire instantaneously.

Verse 22. *And Noah did according to all that God commanded him, so did he.* By *Noah’s doing according to all that God commanded him*, is signified that it was done so: its being twice said that he did so, implies, that which relates both to the will and to the understanding <note>In this context, the "will" refers to the seat of human desire and love, while the "understanding" refers to the intellect and faith.</note>.

Thus in the Word there is a conjunction of those things which are of the will, and of those which are of the understanding, or of the things that are of love and the things that are of faith, or, what is the same, of things <term>celestial</term> <note>Relating to the highest level of heaven, characterized by love to the Lord.</note> and things <term>spiritual</term> <note>Relating to the middle level of heaven, characterized by charity toward the neighbor and faith.</note>, so that in every part there may be a resemblance of a marriage, and that all things in the Word may have respect to the <term>heavenly marriage</term> <note>The union of divine goodness and divine truth.</note>. For the same reason, one expression here is repeated.

->OF THE SOCIETIES WHICH CONSTITUTE HEAVEN.<-

684. *THERE are three heavens; the first where good spirits are, the second where angelic spirits are, and the third where angels are; and one more interior and purer than the other: thus they are most distinct from each other. Each heaven, both the first, the second, and the third, is distinguished into innumerable societies, and each society consists of several individuals, who by harmony and unanimity constitute as it were one person; and all the societies together constitute as it were one man <note>This refers to the concept of the "Grand Man," where the entire collective of heaven functions with the organic unity of a single human body.</note>. The societies are distinguished from each other according to the differences of mutual love and faith towards the Lord; which differences are so innumerable, that it is impossible to recount even the most universal genera <note>original Latin: "genera," meaning types or categories.</note>: nor is there the least given difference, which is not arranged in the most orderly manner, so as to conspire <note>In this older sense, "conspire" means to breathe together or harmonize, rather than to plot.</note> unanimously to the common one, and the common one, to the unanimity of the individuals, and hence to the happiness of all as promoted by individuals, and of individuals as promoted by all. Thence every particular angel, and every particular society, is an image of the universal heaven, and a kind of heaven in miniature.*

### 682—687.] GENESIS.

->R<-

685. *Social associations in the afterlife are marvelous and are structured much like family relationships on earth. In that world, there is a shared recognition similar to that of parents, children, brothers, relatives, and friends; their love for one another is determined by these specific differences in connection. These differences are countless, and the perceptions shared between spirits are so sensitive and refined that they defy description. In these spiritual bonds, no regard at all is paid to the parents, children, or relatives one had on earth, nor to a person’s former social rank, wealth, or similar status. Instead, everything is based on the specific qualities of their mutual love and faith—the capacity for which each person developed from the Lord during their life in the world.*

686. *It is the Lord’s mercy—or to put it another way, His love toward the entire heaven and the whole human race—and thus the Lord alone, who organizes every individual into these societies. It is this mercy that produces <term>conjugial</term> <note>From the Latin "conjugialis," referring specifically to a spiritual, eternal marriage love between two souls, which the author considers the highest form of love.</note> love, and from it, the love of parents toward their children. These are the fundamental and primary types of love. From them spring all other varieties of love in endless diversity, all of which are perfectly arranged into distinct societies.*

687. *Because this is the nature of heaven, it is impossible for any angel or spirit to possess any life unless they belong to some society, moving in harmony with many others. A society is, in essence, nothing but a harmony of many individuals joined together; there is no such thing as an individual life existing entirely apart from the life of others. Indeed, it is impossible for any angel, spirit, or society to have life—meaning to be moved by what is good, to desire it, to be moved by what is true, or to think—unless they are connected through many members of their society to heaven and the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>In this context, the "world of spirits" is a transitional state or region where people first go after death before eventually entering heaven or hell.</note>. The same is true for the human race: no person can possibly live—that is, feel good, have a will, feel truth, or think—unless they also have a connection with heaven through associated angels, and a connection with the world of spirits (and even with hell) through the spirits who accompany them. For every person, while they live in the body, is part of some society of spirits and angels, even if they are completely unaware of it. It would be impossible to live for a single moment without this connection. This works just like the human body: any part that is not connected to the rest by <term>fibers and vessels</term> <note>Referring to the nervous system and the circulatory system.</note>, and thus through their shared functions, is not truly a part of the body; instead, it is immediately separated and rejected as having no life. The societies that people were part of during their physical life are revealed to them when they enter the next world. When they arrive at their own specific society after death, they enter into the very essence of the life they cultivated while in the body, and from that state, they begin a new life. Thus, according to the life they lived in the body, they either sink down into hell or are raised up into heaven.*

<header>GENESIS. [CHAPTER 7]</header>

688. *Because there is such a connection between everyone as a whole and each person individually, there is also a similar connection between even the tiniest details of our feelings and the tiniest details of our thoughts.*

689. *This creates a <term>balance</term> <note>Original Latin: "equilibrium." A core concept in the author's work, describing a state of perfect spiritual poise where a person is kept between the influence of heaven and hell, allowing for true free will.</note> in everything—whether heavenly, spiritual, or natural. No one can think, feel, or act except through their connection with others, yet every individual is led to believe they think, feel, and act entirely of their own free will. In the same way, nothing exists that is not balanced by its opposite, and by intermediate steps between it and that opposite; thus, both individuals and groups live in a state of perfect balance. No harm can come to anyone without it being immediately countered; when evil begins to outweigh the good, the evil person is corrected by this very law of balance as if by a natural consequence, but only so that a greater good may result. In this structure, and therefore in this balance, consists the heavenly order which is formed, arranged, and preserved by the Lord alone forever.*

690. *It should also be noted that no two communities in heaven are exactly alike, nor are any two individuals within those communities. Instead, there is a harmonious variety among them all. These variations are organized by the Lord toward a single purpose, which is achieved through love and faith toward Him. This is the source of their unity. For this reason, the heaven and the joy of one person are never exactly the same as another’s, as these experiences vary according to each person's specific capacity for love and faith.*

691. *This is a general description of the communities that make up heaven, based on extensive and daily experience. However, by the <term>Divine Mercy</term> <note>A common phrase in these writings referring to the Lord’s loving-kindness and providence.</note> of the Lord, this subject will be discussed in more detail in the following pages.*

# GENESIS.

## CHAPTER THE SEVENTH.

---

### ON THE NATURE OF HELL.

---

692. JUST as most people have only the most superficial idea of heaven, they have an even more obscure understanding of hell—so obscure, in fact, that it can hardly be called an idea at all. *societies, and the lives of the individuals who compose them, must needs have a most superficial idea of the earth, indeed, such as scarcely to deserve the name of an idea, so is it also in respect to heaven and hell, when nevertheless there are innumerable things contained in each, and indefinitely more than in any globe of earth, throughout the universe. This may be seen in some degree from this consideration, that as no two individuals have a similar heaven, so neither have any two a similar hell, and that all souls whatever, which have lived in the world since the first creation, are there admitted and collected together.*

693. *As love towards the Lord and our neighbor, together with the joy and happiness thence originating, constitute heaven; so hatred against the Lord and against our neighbor, together with the punishment and torment thence originating, constitute hell. There are innumerable genera <note>General categories or groups.</note>, and still more innumerable species <note>Specific types within those categories.</note>, of hatreds, and hence the hells are innumerable.*

694. *As heaven, from the Lord, by mutual love, constitutes as it were one man and one soul, and thus regards one end, which is the preservation and salvation of all to eternity, so, on the other hand, hell, from <term>proprium</term> <note>A Latin term used here to describe the "selfhood" or the human ego—the part of a person that wants to be independent of God and focused entirely on self-interest.</note>, by self-love and the love of the world, that is, by hatred, constitutes one devil and one mind [<term>animus</term> <note>Latin for the lower or emotional mind, often associated with worldly desires.</note>], and thus regards one end, which is the destruction and damnation of all to eternity. That such is the tendency of each, has been given me to perceive a thousand and a thousand times; wherefore, unless the Lord, every moment, and every smallest part of a moment, preserved all, they would inevitably perish.*

695. *But the hells have such a form and order induced by the Lord, that all are kept tied and bound by their lusts and phantasies <note>Deceptive mental images or false realities that feel completely real to those in the spiritual world.</note>, wherein the very essence of their life consists; which life, as originating in death, is changed into dreadful torments, such as cannot be described. The highest satisfaction of their life consists in being able to punish, torture, and torment each other, which they do by arts altogether unknown in the world, whereby they excite exquisite sensations, just as if they were in the body, and also direful and horrible phantasies, together with terrors and horrors, and many more things of a similar kind. The diabolical crew perceive so much pleasure in this, that if it were possible for them to increase and strain pangs and torments to infinity, they would not even then be satisfied, but would still burn with desire to go beyond the infinite: the Lord, however, frustrates their efforts, and mitigates the torments they inflict.*

697. *There are with every man at least two evil spirits, and two angels; by means of the evil spirits he has communication with hell, and by means of the angels with heaven: without such communication with both, it would be impossible for him to live a single moment. That society in which a man has been, is sometimes shown him in another life, for he returns into it, and thereby into the life which he had in the world, and thence either tends towards hell, or is raised up into heaven. Thus he who has not lived in the good of charity, and has not suffered himself to be led by the Lord, is one of the infernals, and after death moreover becomes a devil.*

There are many kinds of vastations, and the times of vastation are longer and shorter, some in a very short time being taken up into heaven, and some immediately after death.*

## THE CONTENTS.

701. IT here treats in general of the preparation for a new church, as to its **voluntary** <term>voluntary: relating to the "will," or the part of the mind that deals with desires and intentions, rather than just thoughts.</term> things, (from verse 1 to 5,) as previously concerning its **intellectual** <term>intellectual: relating to the "understanding," or the part of the mind that processes thoughts and truths.</term> things.
702. Afterwards its temptations are treated of, which are described as to its *intellectual* things, (from verse 6 to 10,) and as to its *voluntary* things, (verses 11, 12.)
703. 704. Finally, it treats of the nature of the last posterity of the Most Ancient Church, which was possessed by the persuasions of the false, and the lusts of self-love, so that it perished; from verse 19 to 24.

## THE INTERNAL SENSE.

705. THE subject here specifically treated of is the **deluge** <note>The author uses the "deluge" or flood as a metaphor for an overwhelming "flood" of negative thoughts and emotions that can drown the spirit.</note>, by which are signified, not only the temptations which the man of the church, called Noah, must needs sustain, before he could be regenerated, but likewise the desolation of those who were not in a capacity to be regenerated. Both **temptations** and **desolations** are in the Word compared to and called **floods** or **inundations** of waters. Temptations are thus adverted to in Isaiah:
> “In a small moment have I forsaken thee, and in great mercies will I gather thee; in an **inundation** <note>original: "inundatio." <note>Our author here follows the version of Schmidius <note>Schmidius: Sebastian Schmidt (1617–1696), a Lutheran theologian whose literal Latin translation of the Bible was preferred by the author for its precision.</note>, against most others, and amongst them the Hebrew as it stands in the received text. The word in the present Hebrew text is *shetsaph* <note>original: שֶׁצֶף</note>, which occurs nowhere else in the whole Bible, and is supposed to mean *a little*, but as shortness of duration is expressed by its being added, “I hid my face from thee for *a moment*,” several critics have supposed that one of the two words has been inserted by mistake. The word *shetsaph* <note>original: שֶׁצֶף</note> differs but little in appearance from *sheteph* <note>original: שֶׁטֶף</note>, wherefore Schmidius concluded the latter, which means **an inundation**, to be the word intended. Our author quotes the passage in two other places still following the same translation.</note>

"*waters of Noah* is this to me, to whom I have sworn that the *waters of Noah* should no more pass over the earth: thus have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee, O thou afflicted, tossed with tempests, and not comforted," (Isaiah liv. 7, 8, 9, 11;) speaking of the church about to be <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of spiritual rebirth or the transformation of a person's character from worldly to spiritual.</note>, and of *temptations*, which are called the *waters of Noah*. The Lord Himself also calls *temptations* an *inundation*, in Luke:

> "Jesus said, Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, is like a *man* who built a house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock; and when the *flood* came, the *stream* beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it, for it was founded upon a rock," (vi. 47, 48.)

> "The Lord causeth to ascend upon them the *waters of the river*, strong and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory; and he shall come up over all his channels, and he shall pass through Judah; he shall *overflow*, and go over, he shall reach to the neck," (viii. 7, 8;)

In Jeremiah:

> "Thus saith Jehovah, Behold, *waters* rise up out of the north, and they shall be an *overflowing flood*, and shall overflow the land, and the fulness thereof, the city, and them that dwell therein," (xlvii. 2, 3;)

speaking of the Philistines, by whom are represented those who assume false principles, and reason thence concerning spiritual things, which *inundate* man, as they did the <term>antediluvians</term>. The reason why both *temptations* and *desolations*, are in the Word compared to *floods*, or *inundations of waters*, and are so called, is, because their effects are similar; for evil spirits enter by <term>influx</term> <note>Influx describes the way spiritual influences—whether good or evil—flow into a person’s mind and heart.</note>, with their persuasions and the principles of the false, by which they are influenced, and excite similar things in man, and these with the man who is regenerate, are *temptations*, but with the man who is not regenerate, they are *desolations*.

Similar instances occur in other parts of the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible, viewed here as having a deep, internal spiritual meaning.</note>, especially in the prophets, where the same circumstance is related in various modes, and is sometimes even taken up anew and again described. The reason is, as was before observed, because there are two faculties in man, perfectly distinct from each other, the **understanding** and the **will**, and the **Word** treats distinctly of each. This is the cause of these repetitions; and that it is so in the present instance, will appear from what follows.

708. By *Jehovah’s* saying to Noah, is signified, that it was so done, as is evident from this consideration, that with Jehovah every thing is, <note>original: "non sit nisi quam esse"; translated: "is nothing else than to be"</note> what He says is made and done. Also in the foregoing chapter, verse 13, and in other passages, by Jehovah’s saying, is signified, to be made and done.

709. It is said *Jehovah*, because the subject now treated of is **charity** <note>In this context, charity is not just giving to the poor, but the internal affection of doing good.</note>. When intellectual things, or the truths of *faith*, are treated of, the term *God* is used, but when the things of the *will*, or the goods of *love*, the term *Jehovah* is employed; for intellectual things, or such as appertain to *faith*, do not constitute the church, but those of the *will*, or such as appertain to *love*. *Jehovah* is in *love* and *charity*, but not in *faith*, except it be the *faith* of *love* and *charity*; where-fore also in the **Word**, faith is compared to the *night*, but love to the *day*, as in the first chapter of *Genesis*, where speaking of the great luminaries, it is said, that the greater luminary, or the *sun*, which signifies *love*, rules by *day*, and the lesser luminary, or the *moon*, which signifies *faith*, rules by *night*, (Gen. i. 14, 16.) It is similar with the prophets, (Jerem. xxxi. 35; chap. xxxiii. 20; Psalm cxxxvi. 8, 9; also Rev. viii. 12.)

710. That a **house** signifies the *will*, and what is of the *will*, is evident from various parts of the **Word**; as from Jeremiah: “Their *houses* shall be trans-ferred to others, their *fields* and *wives* together,” (vi 12;) where *houses*, and *fields*, and *wives*, have reference to such things as appertain to the *will*. standing: and it is similar in other passages. *The house of Jehovah* also is frequently put for the church, where love is the principal; the house of *Judah* for the celestial church; and the house of *Israel* for the spiritual church; because a house is the church, and thence the mind of the man of the church, in which are voluntary and intellectual things, or what are of charity and faith, is a house.

711. To enter into the ark, signifies to be prepared, as was shown above, verse 18 of the preceding chapter, but it there signified that he was prepared as to things intellectual, which are the truths of faith; here, however, it denotes a preparation as to the things of the will, which are the goods of love, in order to salvation. Unless man be prepared, that is, instructed in what is true and good, he can never be regenerated, much less can he endure temptations; for the evil spirits, who are at that time with him, excite his falses and evils, so that unless truths and goods be present, to which falses and evils may be bended by the Lord, and by which they may be dispersed, he must necessarily fall in the temptation: truths and goods are the *remains* <note>In this context, "remains" refers to the spiritual goods and truths stored up by the Lord in a person's inner memory from childhood to be used later in life during spiritual trials.</note>, which are reserved by the Lord for such uses.

712. By *I have seen thee just in this generation*, is signified, that he had good, by which he could be regenerated, as was said and shown in the preceding chapter, verse 9, where *just* signifies the good of charity, and *upright* the truth of charity. It is there said *generations*, in the plural number, because it treats of things intellectual; but here *generation*, in the singular number, because it treats of things appertaining to the will; for the will comprehends in it intellectual things, but the understanding does not comprehend in it those of the will.

713. His good, yea even his highest loves are also very similar, as the love of associates of his own species, and the love of his wife and children, so that there is no real difference between them. The same applies to other instances. Although a person may live like a wild beast—loving nothing but himself and what belongs to him—the mercy of the Lord is so great (being divine and infinite) that He never leaves him. Instead, the Lord continually breathes His own life into him by the <term>instrumentality of angels</term> <note>The idea that angels act as mediators or messengers, influencing human thoughts and affections for the better.</note>. Even if a person receives this life perversely, it still gives him the capacity to think, to reflect upon, and to understand what is good or evil, whether it relates to moral, civil, worldly, or physical life, and thereby to discern what is true and false.

They even named them as such. They compared the things of the <term>will</term> to *beasts*, and the things of the <term>understanding</term> to *birds*. They also distinguished between good and evil affections: they compared good affections to lambs, sheep, kids, goats, rams, cows, and oxen, because these animals are good and gentle, and because of their use for food and clothing. These are the principal *clean beasts*. Those that are evil, savage, and thus unserviceable to life, are the *unclean beasts*.

Hence, in the Word, the number *seven* represents what is holy. Those who are in the internal sense, such as angels and angelic spirits, do not even know what a number is, and consequently do not know what the number *seven* is. That *seven* denotes what is holy, or such things as are holy, may appear from the rituals in the <term>representative church</term> <note>The "representative church" refers to ancient systems of worship, such as that of the Israelites, where physical actions and objects were used to symbolize deep spiritual truths.</note>, where the number *seven* so frequently occurs. Thus the sprinkling of blood and oil is directed to be done *seven times*; as in <term>Leviticus</term> <note>The third book of the Bible, largely concerned with the laws and rituals of the Israelite priesthood.</note>: “Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle, and all that was therein, and sanctified them. Again, it is said of Aaron when he entered into the holy place, that “he shall take of the blood of this bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the <term>mercy-seat</term> <note>The mercy-seat was the gold cover of the Ark of the Covenant, symbolizing the Lord’s presence and the communication of His mercy.</note> eastward, and before the mercy-seat shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger *seven times*.” In like manner, it is related of the altar, that “he shall sprinkle of the blood that is upon it with his finger *seven times*, and cleanse it, and hallow it,” (Levit. xvi. 14, 19.) Here, all and every thing mentioned, *as well the blood as the mercy-seat, the altar, and the east towards which the blood was to be sprinkled*, signify the Lord himself, consequently the holy principle of love, and of course the same is represented by the number *seven*. So also it is written of the sacrifices in Leviticus: “If a soul shall sin through ignorance,—and if a priest that is anointed do sin according to the sin of the people,—he shall kill a bullock before <term>Jehovah</term> <note>A traditional name for God in the Old Testament, representing the Divine Being itself.</note>,—and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and shall sprinkle of the blood *seven times* before Jehovah, towards the vail of the sanctuary,” (iv. 2, 3, 4, 6.) Here again *seven* denotes what is holy, because the subject treated of is <term>expiation</term> <note>The process of making amends for sin or being reconciled with the Divine.</note>, which is of the Lord alone, and thus it treats of the Lord. Similar ordinances were instituted respecting the cleansing of a <term>leper</term> <note>In a spiritual sense, leprosy was often seen as a symbol of the profanation of truth or spiritual sickness.</note>, and they are thus described in Leviticus: “He [the priest] shall take cedar-wood, and scarlet, and hyssop, and shall dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed—and shall sprinkle upon him that is to be cleansed from the leprosy *seven times*, and shall pronounce him *clean*; and in like manner of the oil, which is upon his left hand, *seven times* before Jehovah,” (xiv. 6, 7, also 27, 51, &c.) It must be manifest to every one that cedar-wood, scarlet, hyssop, oil, the blood of a bird, and consequently the number *seven*, are nothing, except so far as they are representative of what is holy; and if this be abstracted from them, there remains only what is dead, or profanely idolatrous. As, however, sacred things are signified thereby, they contain interiorly a divine principle of worship, which is represented only

724. We have also seen that *sevens* denote what is holy, and, in the present instance, truths which are holy in consequence of originating in good <note>In this theological context, "good" refers to the quality of love and the will, while "truth" refers to the intellect and faith.</note> ; for no truth is holy unless it proceed from good. A man may utter from memory many truths of the Word, but unless they are produced by love or charity, holiness cannot be predicated of them ; but if so produced, they are at the same time acknowledged and believed in, and thus spoken from the heart. Just so it is with faith, which is so frequently represented as being alone able to save, unless it originate in love or charity, it is no faith at all, since these alone can sanctify it. When faith is disjoined from love, the desire of his own praise or gain rules in man’s heart, and moves him to speak. Thus also it is with respect to faith, of which I have been convinced by much experience in the other world <note>The author frequently refers to his visionary experiences in the spiritual realm or afterlife to illustrate these points.</note> ; for those who in the life of the body have preached the Lord and faith with such eloquence, and at the same time such an appearance of devotion, as to beget astonishment in their hearers, but yet did it not from the heart, are in another life such as bear the greatest hatred towards the Lord, and are most bitter in persecuting the faithful.
