## [Chapter 7: 4]

726. ...life from the Lord, because there is life only in those things which are of the Lord, as must be evident to every one who reflects that there is no vitality in any thing unconnected with eternal life, or which does not regard eternal life. The life which is not eternal is not life, but in a little while perishes; nor can <term>Being</term> <note>original Latin: "Esse", literally "TO BE"; the author uses this to express that which exists from itself and is the core of reality</note> be predicated of those things which cease to be, but only of those which always continue to exist, consequently, to live; and <term>Being</term> only resides in what is of the Lord, or Jehovah, because all <term>Being</term> and eternal life are his. By eternal life is meant eternal happiness, concerning which see what was said and shown above, n. 290.

727. *Verse 4. For as yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights ; and I will destroy every substance which I have made from off the faces of the ground.* For *as yet seven days* signifies to the commencement of the temptation denoted by *to rain*, of which *forty days and forty nights* express the duration. By *I will destroy every substance which I have made from off the faces of the ground*, the abolition of man's <term>selfhood</term> <note>original Latin: "proprium"; the inherent nature or ego of a person, which feels as though it belongs to them alone</note> is signified, which is, as it were, destroyed when he becomes <term>regenerate</term> <note>the process of being spiritually reborn and made new by divine influence</note>, and it also signifies the death of those members of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>the first state of humanity, characterized by direct perception of God, before the symbolic "Fall"</note> who destroyed themselves.

728. *For as yet seven days* signifies here to the commencement of the temptation, as is manifest from the internal sense of every expression in this verse, the subject treated of being the temptation of the man denominated Noah. In a general sense this passage relates both to the temptation of that man, and to the total <term>vastation</term> <note>a state of spiritual stripping away or depletion of old, corrupted states</note> of those of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> who were reduced to this state; wherefore *for as yet seven days* means not only the beginning of the temptation, but also the end of the <term>vastation</term>. The reason of this signification is, that *seven* is a holy number, as was said and shown above, (verse 2 of the present chapter, and chap. iv. 15, 24; also n. 84—87,) and has reference both to the Lord’s advent into the world, and to his coming to glory, meaning specifically every advent of the Lord. Now every advent of the Lord is, at the same time, the beginning to those who are regenerated, and the end to those who are vastated. The reason why *forty days* signifies the duration of temptation <note>spiritual trial or struggle</note> is, as previously stated, because the Lord allowed himself to be tempted by the devil for *forty days*. Since everything in the Word <note>the Bible</note> was representative of Him, when the angels had a concept of temptation, it was represented in the world of spirits by worldly things. This follows the common law of angelic ideas: as they descend into the world of spirits, they become fixed and are shown through symbols—in this case, by the number *forty*, because the Lord was tempted for *forty days*. To the Lord, and to those in the angelic heaven, the present and the future are one; what is to come is seen as present, as if it had already happened. For this reason, the number *forty* came to symbolize temptations and <term>vastations</term> <note>the process of being "emptied" of old errors or selfish habits to make room for new life</note> in the representative Church. These facts cannot yet be fully understood, however, because we do not yet understand how the influence of the angelic heaven flows into the world of spirits.

731. The phrase *I will destroy every substance which I have made from off the faces of the ground* signifies the clearing away of man’s <term>proprium</term> <note>the "self" or ego; the parts of a person that feel independent from God</note>. This happens when the self is, in a sense, <term>vivified</term> <note>brought to spiritual life</note>, as is clear from our earlier notes on the <term>proprium</term>. The human "self" is entirely made of what is evil and false; as long as it remains active, a person is in a state of spiritual death. However, when a person undergoes spiritual trials, that selfhood is broken up—or, to put it another way, it is loosened and softened by truths and goodness from the Lord. In this way, it is <term>vivified</term> and appears as if it were no longer there. When the text says *I will destroy*, it means the "self" ceases to show itself and is no longer harmful; it is never actually *destroyed* in reality, but remains still and quiet. 

In this regard, the <term>proprium</term> can be compared to the colors black and white. When these are hit by rays of light in various ways, they are transformed into beautiful colors—like blue, yellow, and purple. Through their arrangement, as seen in flowers, different forms of beauty and loveliness are displayed; yet, these colors still fundamentally relate to the black and white they came from. 

Because this passage also describes the final <term>vastation</term> of those who belonged to the Most Ancient Church <note>the symbolic name for the earliest, most celestial state of humanity</note>, the phrase *I will destroy every substance which I have made from off the faces of the ground* also refers to those who perished, as seen in verse 23. The "substance" mentioned refers to every human being, every "vessel" capable of holding heavenly seeds, or every member of the church. This is why, in both this verse and the 23rd, the word *ground* is used; it represents a person of the church in whom goodness and truth are planted. In those represented by Noah, these qualities grew successfully as evils and falsehoods were separated. However, in the <term>antidiluvians</term> <note>those living before the flood</note> who perished, these spiritual seeds were choked out by weeds.

732. Verse 5. *And Noah did according unto all that Jehovah commanded him*, signifies, as before, that it was so done. Intellectual things regard those of the will as other and distinct from themselves; whilst the voluntary things regard those belonging to the understanding as united to or as one with themselves, for the understanding is from the will; and this is the reason of its being there twice said that Noah did as he was commanded, but here only once, and also why the Lord is there called *God*, but here *Jehovah*.

733. Verse 6. *And Noah was a son of six hundred years, and a flood of waters was caused upon the earth*. By Noah's being a son of six hundred years, is denoted his first state of <term>temptation</term> <note>in this context, "temptation" refers to a spiritual trial or crisis that leads to growth</note>; and by *a flood of waters being caused upon the earth*, the commencement of that temptation.

734. The subject now treated of, however, from verse 6 to 11, is his temptation, and that indeed in its first state, thus at its commencement; and, as every one may perceive, there again occurs a repetition, it being said that *Noah was a son of six hundred years when the flood was caused upon the earth*, and in verse 11, that this event occurred *in the six hundredth year of his life, in the second month, and on the seventeenth day of the month*. It is also written both in the 7th and 13th verses, that *Noah entered into the ark with his sons and their wives*, and in the 8th and 9th verses, as well as from the 14th to the 16th, that *beasts entered into the ark to Noah*; whence it is again evident that the same words are repeated. He who abides in the <term>literal sense</term> <note>the surface-level historical story</note> only must regard these as reiterated statements of certain historical facts; whilst, since it is the Word of the Lord, there cannot be a single superfluous or unnecessary expression, and thus no repetition without a difference of <term>signification</term> <note>internal symbolic meaning</note>. The present passage, as has been previously remarked, describes his first temptation, or that of the understanding, and afterwards his temptation as to what appertains to the will, these succeeding each other in the regenerate man. 735. The reason why temptation as to the understanding, or as to the <term>falses</term> <note>Specific false ideas or misconceptions regarding the truth</note> in which man is principled, is light, is because every human mind is influenced by the fallacies of the senses, which, as they necessarily obtain admission, must therefore also admit of being easily dispersed. Thus all who take the Word literally where it is spoken according to man's apprehension, and consequently according to the fallacies of his senses, notwithstanding their errors, readily suffer themselves to be instructed, if they have believed them in simplicity, and because they are so stated in the Word of the Lord. In like manner, he who believes in simplicity that he is able to do good of himself, and that he will receive a reward in another life if he is good from himself, easily admits of being taught that the good which he does is from the Lord, and that he, out of mercy, freely dispenses reward. Hence when such persons enter into temptation as to things intellectual, or as to these fallacies, they can only be mildly tempted, and this, which is the first temptation, and indeed scarcely appears like one, is the subject now treated of. The reason of this derivation is, that in the combat of temptation, the holy principle of faith is present, and also that the *six days of labor and combat look forward to the holy seventh.* <note>The "holy seventh" refers to the Sabbath, representing a state of peace after spiritual struggle.</note>

**738.** Noah is here called a *son of six hundred years*, because, as we have previously seen, *a son* signifies <term>intellectual truth</term> <note>Truth as understood by the mind or intellect, rather than felt by the heart</note>. **739.** By a *flood of waters* is signified the commencement of temptation, as is evident from the present passage relating to a temptation as to things intellectual, which always precedes, and is comparatively slight, as has been just observed. Hence it is called a *flood of waters*, and not simply *a flood*, as in the 17th verse; for *waters* primarily signify the spiritual things of man, or the intellectual things of faith, and also their opposites, or <term>falses</term> <note>Latin: *falsa*; technical term for false principles, errors, or delusions that attack the mind</note>, as might be confirmed by numerous citations from the Word. That a *flood of waters* or an <term>inundation</term> <note>A symbolic term for being overwhelmed by false ideas or spiritual trials</note>, represents temptation, appears from what was stated at the beginning of the chapter, and also from Ezekiel: "Thus saith the Lord God, I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury, and there shall be an *overflowing shower* in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it: So will I break down the wall which ye have daubed with untempered [mortar]," (xiii. 13, 14.) Here a *stormy wind* and an *overflowing shower* signify the desolation of what is false, and a *wall daubed with untempered [mortar]* a fiction bearing the semblance of truth. So in Isaiah: "Thou [Jehovah] hast been a refuge from the *inundation*, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as an *inundation* against the wall," (xxv. 4;) in which passage an *inundation* denotes temptation as to intellectual things, and it is distinguished from temptation as to what belongs to the will, which is called *heat*. Again, in the same prophet: "Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, as an *inundation* of hail, a destroying storm, a *flood of mighty waters overflowing*," (xxviii. 2;) where the degrees of temptation are described. Again: "When thou passest through the *waters*, I will be with thee; and through the *rivers*, they shall not overflow thee: when thou goest through the *fire*, thou shalt not be burned, neither shall the flame kindle upon thee," (xliii. 2;) where *waters* and *rivers* represent falses and <term>phantasies</term> <note>Delusions or misleading mental images</note>, and *fire* and *flame*, evils and...

**741.** Noah's entering into the ark from before the waters of the flood, denotes his being protected, as may be made to appear plainly to every one. Temptations are the combats of evil spirits with the angels attendant upon man; for evil spirits excite all the depraved inclinations and thoughts which a man has had from infancy, thus both his evils and <term>falses</term> <note>A technical term used here to describe specific false ideas, errors, or misconceptions of the mind.</note>, and condemn him, nothing being more delightful to them than this; indeed, the very essential delight of their life consists herein; but the Lord, by his angels, protects man, and restrains the evil spirits from transgressing their limits, and inundating him with a more powerful influence than he is capable of sustaining.

By truths and goods then, notwithstanding they are here called *sons and wives*, are signified those possessed by the man named Noah, and by which he was protected; for such is the most ancient style of the Word, that, although it is connected as an historical relation, it contains within its bosom <term>celestial arcana</term> <note>original: "arcana coelestia"; deep, hidden spiritual secrets or mysteries of heaven.</note>.

**751.** As the subject here is the <term>temptation</term> <note>In this context, "temptation" refers to a deep spiritual struggle or crisis of character, rather than just a simple urge to do something wrong.</note> of the man of the new church called Noah, and since the nature of such a trial is understood by few (if any), because so few people today experience these spiritual struggles—and those who do often believe the suffering comes from within themselves—I am permitted to briefly explain the matter. 

During these times, malicious spirits stir up the memory of all the <term>falses</term> <note>Incorrect beliefs or delusions that lead the mind astray.</note> and evils a person has thought or done since childhood, acting in an incredibly cunning and spiteful way. The angels, however, who are present with the person, bring forth their good qualities and truths to defend them. This inner conflict, being felt and recognized by the individual, causes remorse and the stings of conscience. 

There are two kinds of temptation: one affecting the **understanding** (the intellect) and the other affecting the **will** (the heart). When a person’s intellect is tested, malicious spirits bring up the evil actions they have committed—signified here by the ***unclean beasts***—to accuse and condemn them. At the same time, the spirits take the person's good actions—represented by the ***clean beasts***—and twist them through a thousand tricks. They also target the person's thoughts, denoted by the ***fowl***, and everything represented by ***every thing which creepeth upon the ground***. This kind of trial is relatively light and is felt only as a memory of these things and a certain resulting anxiety. 

However, when a person is tested in their **will**, it is not just their past actions and thoughts that are stirred up. Instead, evil <term>genii</term> <note>A specific class of malicious spirits that target a person's deepest desires and emotions rather than their logical thoughts.</note>—for that is what these types of spirits are called—inflame the person with the same filthy lusts and selfish desires they are already prone to. They carry on the fight using the person’s own <term>cupidity</term> <note>Strong, often selfish, desires or greed.</note>. They do this so secretly and maliciously that it is almost impossible to realize the spirits are behind it; they blend into the person's own impure affections, instantly turning a love for what is good and true into a love for what is evil and false. Consequently, the person cannot help but feel that this is coming from their own self. This form of temptation is most severe and is felt as internal agony and a tormenting fire. Many experiences have confirmed this description to me, and have shown me when this spiritual "flooding" occurs, as well as its origin and nature; by the Lord's mercy, these details will be shared at length later.

**752.** Verse 10. *And it was till seven days, and the waters of the flood were upon the earth.* By these words, as mentioned before, the beginning of the spiritual trial is signified.

**753.** Seven days represent the beginning of a <term>temptation</term> <note>In this context, a spiritual struggle where one's beliefs or character are tested.</note>, as was previously explained in the commentary on verse four. This current passage connects to what came before: this specific trial is one of the **understanding** (the intellect or logic). Because it is the primary or starting phase of the trial, it is described this way. Since it is a struggle of the intellect, it is symbolized here—as it was in verse 7—by the ***waters of a flood*** (called a ***flood of waters*** in verse 6). As previously shown, water is a fitting symbol for this kind of intellectual trial.

**754. Verse 11.** *In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day were all the fountains of the great abyss disrupted, and the cataracts of heaven were opened.* The mention of the **six hundredth year**, the **second month**, and the **seventeenth day** signifies a new stage of spiritual struggle. The "disruption of all the fountains of the great abyss" represents a severe trial of the **will** (the heart or desires), while the "opening of the cataracts of heaven" represents a severe trial of **intellectual things** (the thoughts).

**755.** The ***six hundredth year, second month, and seventeenth day*** indicates a different state of trial, following the sequence established earlier. From verse 6 until now, the text focused on the first stage of trial, which involves the intellect. Now, it shifts to a different kind of struggle—one involving the **will**. 

This is why **Noah's age** is mentioned twice: first, he was called a "son of six hundred years," and now it is specified that he was in the **six hundredth year, the second month, and the seventeenth day** of his life when the flood occurred. It may seem impossible to believe that the specific years, months, and days of Noah's life actually refer to states of spiritual struggle within the human heart. However, as mentioned before, this was the style of writing and speaking used by the <note>The author refers to a legendary "Most Ancient Church" or prehistoric humanity that communicated through symbols and correspondences rather than literal history.</note> **most ancient people**. They found great joy in using times and names to create a narrative that looked like history but actually contained deep wisdom. 

We have already seen (in verse 6) that **six hundred years** refers to the first stage of trial; it has the same meaning here. To show that this is now a *different* stage of the struggle, the **months and days** are added. The specific number of the month—the **second**—is significant because the number **two** refers to conflict. This was seen in verse 2 of this chapter, where **two** carried the same meaning as **six**: it represents labor, struggle, and dispersion. The number **seventeen**, meanwhile, symbolizes both the beginning and the end of the struggle, because it is made of **seven** and **ten**. Consequently, what use would there be in knowing the year of Noah's life, and the month and the day when the deluge took place, unless some *heavenly arcanum* was involved in it? And who cannot see that the phrase *all the fountains of the great abyss being disrupted, and the cataracts of heaven opened* is language suited to the prophetic style of speaking? Not to mention other considerations of a similar kind.

## Section 782
The subject treated so far, from verse 11 onward, has been the church as it was preserved among those called "Noah." What follows is a description of its state, which is first explained here. The specific quality of that church's state is described later; every single verse—indeed, every single expression—involves some specific state of being. Furthermore, as the state of the church is about to be described, what was said just before is repeated here, and in fact, it is repeated twice: *they that entered in, entered in male and female, of all flesh*, which in the verse immediately preceding was expressed as: *And they entered in unto Noah into the ark, two by two, of all flesh.* This repetition in <term>the Word</term> <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> indicates that a different state is being discussed; otherwise, as would be obvious to anyone, the repetition would be completely unnecessary.

## Section 783
From this it appears that *those which entered in* signify the things present within the person of the church. Also, their being *male and female, of all flesh* denotes that he possessed truths and goods of every kind; for male and female represent truths and goods, as was shown above. *As God commanded* signifies his preparation to receive what has been spoken of here, as was also demonstrated previously; for "to command," when spoken of the Lord, means to prepare and to act.

## Section 784
*Jehovah shut him in* signifies that man no longer had the same direct communication with heaven as was enjoyed by the man of the <term>celestial church</term>. <note>The "celestial church" refers to the "Most Ancient Church," a metaphorical era of humanity characterized by a heart-centered, direct connection to the Divine.</note> This becomes clear when it is understood that in the Most Ancient Church, people enjoyed internal communication with heaven, and thus through heaven with the Lord. They were <term>principled in love</term> <note>To be "principled in love" means that love for God was the primary rule and motivation of their lives.</note> toward the Lord. All who are in love toward the Lord are like angels, with the only difference being that they are clothed with a material body. Their interiors—their inner spiritual minds—were opened and remained open directly from the Lord. 

It was, however, different with this new church <note>Represented by Noah and his family.</note>, which was not characterized by direct love toward the Lord, but by faith, and through faith by <term>charity toward the neighbor</term>. <note>While the earlier people loved God directly, this new group practiced "charity," or active kindness toward others, as their path to the Divine.</note> Consequently, they could not enjoy internal communication with heaven like the most ancient people, but only external communication. Since it would require a long explanation to describe the specific nature of both these modes of communication, we will simply observe that every person—even the wicked—has communication with heaven through attending angels. The difference lies in the degree, the closeness, or the remoteness of that connection; without it, a person could not possibly exist. The degrees of communication...

# GENESIS [CHAPTER VII]

...at such times present with man; and the meaning of the present passage is similar, except that there is now no temptation denoted, and therefore it is here simply called *the flood*, and not a *flood of waters*. <note>In the author's symbolic system, a "flood of waters" specifically refers to a trial or temptation, whereas "the flood" here refers more generally to the state of the transition between the two "Churches" or spiritual eras.</note>

**788.** *By the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth*, the nature of its fluctuation is denoted, and by *the waters were strengthened, and were greatly increased upon the earth, and the ark went upon the faces of the waters*, is meant that its fluctuations thus increased. This cannot be seen clearly unless the state of this church, called "Noah," be first shown. Noah was not the Ancient Church itself, but, as it were, its parent or seed, as was before observed; Noah, along with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, constituting the Ancient Church, which immediately succeeded the Most Ancient. <note>The "Most Ancient Church" represents the era of original spiritual integrity (Eden), while the "Ancient Church" (represented by Noah) represents the new beginning after that integrity was lost.</note> Every man of the church denominated Noah was of the descent of the Most Ancient Church, and consequently in a similar state regarding hereditary evil <note>The concept that spiritual inclinations and character traits are passed down through generations.</note> with those who perished; and all who were in such a state could not be regenerated and made spiritual in the same way as those who do not have the same kind of hereditary condition. The quality of this hereditary condition was shown above (number 310), but in order to give a clearer idea of this subject, it may be helpful to offer the following observations. 

Those who are of the seed of Jacob—such as the Jews—cannot be regenerated like the Gentiles; there being inherent in them a principle contrary to faith, not only in consequence of principles received from infancy and afterwards confirmed, but also in consequence of hereditary disposition. The fact of this may appear, in some degree, from the consideration that they are of a different <term>genius</term> <note>In this context, "genius" refers to an innate nature, disposition, or character shared by a group.</note>, and even of different manners and features from all other people, from whom they may easily be distinguished, all which they derive hereditarily. This is also true as to their "interiors" <note>The inner spiritual or psychological states of a person, of which their outward appearance is a reflection.</note>, of which external manners and features are the types; therefore, also, converted Jews fluctuate more than any other people between what is true and what is false. This was the case with the first men of the church who are called Noah, because they were of the stock and seed of the Most Ancient people. 

These are the fluctuations which are described here, and later in the further account of Noah, where it is said that he was *a man of the ground, and he planted a vineyard, and drank of the wine and was drunken, so that he lay uncovered in the midst of his tent* (Genesis 9:20, 21). That the men denominated "Noah" were few in number was made evident to me from the circumstance of the man of that church being represented in the world of spirits <note>An intermediate state between heaven and hell where spirits are prepared for their final destination.</note> as a tall and slender person, clothed in white, in a confined chamber. These were, however, the persons who possessed and preserved amongst them the <term>doctrinals of faith</term> <note>The organized teachings and principles that define a religious belief system.</note>.

### 788—790. GENESIS

...spiritual. <note>Completing the sentence from the previous page regarding the inability of certain people to be made spiritual without divine intervention.</note>

**788.** The text states that the *waters increased, and bare up the ark; then, and it was lifted up above the earth;* afterwards, *and the waters were strengthened, and were greatly increased upon the earth;* and lastly, *and the ark went upon the faces of the waters.* These phrases describe the various stages of the ark's fluctuation. To describe every specific degree of these fluctuations would be both tedious and unnecessary; it is enough to know that they are being detailed here.

**789.** However, it is useful to explain what is meant by *the ark's being lifted up above the earth* and *going upon the surface of the waters.* This cannot be understood by anyone unless they are first taught how a person is kept away from evils and falsities. Since this is an <term>arcanum</term> <note>original: "arcanum"; a sacred or hidden spiritual secret.</note>, we will briefly explain it. Human nature is generally so depraved that if the Lord did not hold back even those who are being "regenerated" <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or improvement.</note> from their own evils and false beliefs, they would throw themselves headlong into hell. In fact, the moment a person is left entirely to their own devices, they rush toward hell impulsively. This has been shown to me through much experience, and it was also represented by the "horse" mentioned earlier (sections 187, 188). 

This "holding back" from evil and falsity is actually an elevation. By being "lifted up," a person is able to look down on those negative things, perceiving them to be beneath them. By the Lord's divine mercy, more will be said about this elevation later; for now, it is enough to understand that this is what is signified by *the ark’s being lifted up above the earth, and going upon the surface of the waters.*

**790.** In these verses, *Waters* signify *falsities* <note>original: "falsa"; often translated in older texts as "falses."</note>. This can be seen from the passages of the Word <note>The Bible or Holy Scripture.</note> quoted in the introduction to this chapter, and also in the 6th verse, which mentions a *flood* or *inundation of waters.* It was shown there that *inundations of waters* represent desolation and spiritual trials (temptations). These imply the presence of falsities, because desolations and trials are essentially "floods of falsehoods" stirred up by evil spirits. 

The reason *waters* signify falsities in this context is that, in a general sense, *waters* in the Bible signify things that are spiritual—that is, things relating to the intellect, the reason, and <term>scientific</term> knowledge <note>original: "scientificum"; in this historical context, it refers to "factual knowledge" or things learned through the senses and memory.</note>. Because they represent these things, they also represent their opposites. Every falsity is a type of "fact" or "knowledge" and mimics rational and intellectual thought because it is a subject of our thinking. 

That *waters* refer to spiritual things is clear from many biblical passages; however, that they also signify falsities can be confirmed by the following examples:

> "This people refuses the *waters of Shiloah* which flow softly; therefore, behold, the Lord brings up upon them the *waters of the river*, strong and many; and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks." (Isaiah 8:6, 7).

In this passage, *waters flowing softly* signify spiritual truths, while *waters strong and many* signify falsities. Again, in the same prophet: 

> "Woe to the land shadowing with wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia <note>original: "Cush"; the Hebrew term for the region of the Upper Nile.</note>; that sends messengers..."

It defines "waters" in the biblical sense as representing both spiritual truths and, in the context of the flood, overwhelming falsities.</summary>

793. The **antediluvians** <note>Those who lived "before the flood" (from the Latin *ante*, meaning before, and *diluvium*, meaning flood).</note> who perished constitute the subject of the remainder of the present chapter, as may appear from every particular of the description. Those who are in the **internal sense** <note>A deeper, spiritual meaning within the literal words of the Bible.</note> of the Word can, even from a single expression, immediately discover the matter under consideration, and still more readily can they discern it from several expressions associated together. When a new subject is taken up, either other words are immediately employed, or the same words are connected in a different mode. The reason of this is, that some expressions are peculiar to **spiritual** things, and others to **celestial** things; or what amounts to the same, some are exclusively employed in reference to the **understanding** <note>The "spiritual" part of a person, dealing with truth and thoughts.</note>, and others to the **will** <note>The "celestial" part of a person, dealing with love and intentions.</note>. The word *desolation*, for example, belongs to spiritual things, and *vastation* <note>original: "vastatio"; a technical term for the process where a person is stripped of their previous beliefs or loves, often used here to describe the total depletion of good in the heart.</note> to celestial things: *city* has relation to spiritual, and *mountains* to celestial things; and so in all other instances. The like is true in regard to the connecting together of expressions; and what must needs appear surprising to every one, in the **Hebrew tongue** these are often distinguishable by the sound; for in whatever appertains to the class of spiritual things, the first three vowels <note>The vowels *a*, *e*, and *i*.</note> commonly prevail, whilst in those relating to the celestial class, the two last <note>The vowels *o* and *u*.</note> are most frequently met with. Hence it is known that in the present verse a different subject is entered upon, as is indeed evident from the repetition spoken of above, it being here again said, *and the waters were strengthened very greatly upon the earth*, although the same remark had been made in the preceding verse. What follows corroborates this statement.

794. Persuasions of what is false increase immensely when men immerse truths in their lusts, or cause them to favor self-love and the love of the world; for they thus pervert truths, and by a thousand methods force them to agreement with their desires; and hence how common it is for him who imbibes or frames to himself a false principle to confirm it by many a <term>scientific</term> <note>original: "scientificum"; in this historical context, it refers to a specific piece of factual knowledge or "science" stored in the memory.</note> of which he is in possession, nay, even by the Holy Word itself! Is there a single heresy which has not originated in its authors imbibing the principles of what is false, and in this manner confirming them, forcing into agreement whatever does not favor their principles, and by various strained explanations compelling the...

# GENESIS. [Chap. vii.]

...most discordant facts into assent? For example; where it is a received principle that faith saves without the **goods of charity** <note>In this context, "goods of charity" refers to the outward acts of kindness and the inward intentions of love that should accompany religious belief.</note>, do we not find that the abettors of such a tenet can compose an entire system of doctrine from the Word in favor thereof, without ever regarding, or even attending to, or so much as seeing, what the Lord has said, *that the tree is known by its fruit, and whatsoever tree doth not bring forth good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire?* (Matthew 7:16—20; 12:33.) 

What is more pleasing than for a man to live according to the flesh, and yet be saved, if so be he only knows what is true, although he does not at all practise what is good? Every desire which a man favors forms the life of his **will**, and every principle or persuasion of what is false forms the life of his **understanding**, and these lives make a one when the truths or doctrinals of faith are immersed in lust. Every man thus forms to himself, as it were, his own soul, and his life after death is fixed accordingly. Wherefore nothing is of more importance to man than to know what is true; for when he has obtained this knowledge in such a manner that it cannot be perverted, then it will never be so immersed in lusts as to produce these deadly effects. What ought to be more dear to man than his life to eternity? If he destroy his soul during the life of the body, does he not destroy it for ever?

795. By *all the high mountains were covered which were under the whole heaven*, is meant that all the goods of charity were extinguished, as is evident from the **signification** <note>The symbolic or spiritual meaning behind a literal word in the Bible.</note> of *mountains* amongst the most ancient people. *Mountains* with them represented the Lord, in consequence of their worshipping him upon *mountains*, because these are the highest parts of the earth. On this account *mountains* denoted **celestial affections** <note>Deep, heavenly feelings of love toward God and others.</note>, which they also regarded as the highest, consequently love and charity, and thus the goods of love and charity, which are celestial. 

In an opposite sense, those who are high-minded are called *mountains* in the Word, and thus a mountain denotes self-love itself. The <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>Swedenborg uses this term to describe the first "age" of humanity—a state of innocence and direct connection with the Divine before the spiritual "fall."</note> is also signified in the Word by mountains, in consequence of their elevation above the earth, and being, as it were, nearer to heaven. That *mountains* represent the Lord, and all celestial things thence derived, or the goods of love and charity, is manifest from the following passages of the Word, from which also their particular signification may be recognized, since all the expressions of the Word, both general and particular, have a sense according to the subject to which they are applied. Thus we read in David: "The *mountains* shall bring peace—and the *hills* in righteousness," (Psalm 72:3); where *mountains* denote love towards the Lord, and *hills* neighborly love, such as prevailed in the <term>Most Ancient Church</term>, which, in consequence of being **principled** <note>To be "principled in" something means to have one's character and actions fundamentally rooted in that specific value or belief.</note> in such love and charity, is therefore represented in the Word by *mountains* and *hills*.

813. That these words signify the last term of the Most Ancient Church, and *a hundred and fifty*, a limit which is both last and first, cannot indeed be so well confirmed by citations from the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used here for the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, as the more simple numbers which frequently occur. The multiplication of a few, as that of a *half*, a *fourth*, or a *tenth* part, diminishes the amount of the product, so that at length it is next to nothing, and consequently represents the end or last term. This number occurs with a similar meaning in the following chapter (viii. 3), where it is said, *After the end of the hundred and fifty days, the waters were abated*. Numbers in the Word are to be understood altogether abstractedly from the sense of the letter, being—as we have previously asserted and demonstrated—inserted only to carry on the historical series which is in the literal sense. Thus, where the number *seven* occurs, it denotes what is holy, altogether irrespective of the times and measures to which it happens to be joined; for the angels who perceive the internal sense of the Word, do not know any thing of time and measure, and still less of the number by which it is expressed, and yet they fully understand the word when read by man: wherefore, when any number occurs, they form no idea of it as a number, but perceive instead all that it represents. Thus in the present instance, they recognize in the number *a hundred and fifty* the last term of the Most Ancient Church, and in the following chapter (verse 3), the first commencement of the ancient or new church.

This is owing to their direful natures, and to the phantasies <note>In this context, "phantasies" refers to distorted spiritual perceptions or hallucinations arising from an evil heart.</note> thence derived; for, from this hell such a stench actually exhales, as that when it is opened, which is seldom done, and then only for a little while, no spirits can remain in its vicinity, in consequence of the stench. Some <term>genii</term> <note>The author distinguishes between "spirits" (those who act from thought) and "genii" (those who act from hidden, deep-seated desires or the will).</note>, or rather furies, being let out thence, that I might become acquainted with their quality, so infected the surrounding sphere with a poisonous and pestilential exhalation, that the spirits about me could not remain, and my stomach became at the same time so much affected as to occasion vomiting. On manifesting themselves, an infant was first seen, having a not unhandsome countenance, and carrying a concealed dagger, and him they sent to me, bearing in his hand a vessel: from these representatives <note>Symbolic visions or manifestations that reveal the true inner character of a spirit.</note> I became aware that their purpose was to commit murder, either by dagger or poison, under an appearance of innocence. Their bodies were bare, and of the blackest hue, and they were presently sent back into their cadaverous hell, when I had an opportunity of observing the mode in which they descended. They proceeded towards the left, in the plane of the left temple, and this to a considerable distance, before sinking down; and, when they began to fall, they first entered into a fire which now presented itself, then into a fiery smoke, resembling that of a furnace, and presently beneath that furnace, and towards its front, to a place where there were several very dark caverns tending downward. In the way they were continually meditating and contriving mischiefs, without any provocation, and especially against the innocent: during their descent through the fire, they uttered many lamentations. To distinguish them when sent forth, that it may be known whence they come, and what is their nature, they have a kind of ring, to which are affixed what appear sharp brazen points, which they press with their hands, and twist about. This mark denotes their quality, and is a token of their being bound.*

# GENESIS [Chapter 7]

*...of these serpents and the pain they produce are felt as clearly as if they were real. Such things are intensely felt by spirits because these sensations are as suited to their spiritual life as physical objects are to those living in a body. In the meantime, they live in terrible phantasies <note>In this context, "phantasies" refers to vivid, waking hallucinations or delusions that the spirit believes to be entirely real.</note> and remain in this state for ages, until they no longer know that they were ever human; for the life of hatred and revenge they have built through constant indulgence cannot be extinguished any other way.*

816. *Since there are countless types of hatred and revenge, and even more numerous sub-species—and because no two kinds share the exact same hell—it is impossible to give a full account of every one. I will therefore speak only of those I have seen as clearly as daylight—indeed, in a light clearer than day, perceived through my internal sight <note>This "internal sight" refers to a unique state where the author’s spiritual consciousness was opened, allowing him to interact with the afterlife while still living in the world.</note>, because by the Lord’s divine mercy, I am permitted to be present among spirits. A certain person came to me who appeared to be of noble rank. At his first approach, he suggested through deceptive gestures that he had many things he wished to share, asking me if I was a Christian. When I answered that I was, he said he was of the same religion and wished to be alone with me to say something that others must not hear. However, I replied that in a spiritual state of existence, people cannot be alone in the way men assume they are in the physical world, and that many spirits were already present. He nevertheless came closer and stood behind me, near the back of my head. I immediately perceived that he was an assassin. While he was there, I felt a sharp sensation like a stroke through the heart, and soon after another in the brain—strikes that would have easily killed a man. But because I was protected by the Lord, I feared nothing. I do not know what spiritual "art" or technique he used. Supposing that I was dead, he said to other spirits nearby that he had just come from a man he had murdered by giving him a mortal wound from behind. He boasted that he had the skill to strike so expertly that no one would notice until they fell down dead, and that everyone would believe he was innocent. From this, I realized he was recently deceased and had been a professional assassin in the natural world. The punishment for such people is dreadful; after enduring hellish torments for many ages, they eventually take on a most detestable and monstrous appearance—a ghastly face that looks more like lurid tow <note>original: "stupa lurida" — "Tow" refers to the coarse, fibrous part of flax. The description suggests a face that is pale, sickly, and lacks the smooth, solid quality of human skin, looking instead like a bundle of yellowish, frayed fibers.</note> than a human face. In this way, they cast off everything human until everyone who sees them is so horrified that they are forced to wander like wild beasts in dark places.*

*...dig a hole in the ground, similar to a grave for the interring of a corpse: hence a suspicion arose that he had committed some act of murder during his life in the body. Immediately afterwards there appeared a bier covered with black cloth, and presently one rising from the bier came to me, and in an affecting tone informed me that he was dead, and was of opinion he had been poisoned by that man, adding that he thought this at the hour of death, but was still ignorant whether or not his suspicion was well grounded. The wicked spirit, on hearing this, confessed that he was guilty of the murder. After confession followed punishment. He was twice rolled in the dirty hole which he had dug, until both his face and body were made as black as an Egyptian mummy <note>In the 18th century, mummies were often viewed in Europe as objects of morbid fascination, characterized by their blackened, shriveled appearance—symbolizing here the spiritual corruption of the murderer.</note>, and thus he was carried on high and presented to the view of spirits and angels, whilst this cry was uttered, "What a devil!" His whole frame then became frigid <note>Coldness in this context symbolizes the total absence of "spiritual warmth" or love.</note>, and he was in this state cast into hell amongst the cold infernals.*

818. *Beneath the back parts* <note>original: *sub natibus*, literally "under the buttocks." In the author’s visions, different regions of the spiritual world correspond to parts of the "Grand Man" or universal human form; regions "lower" or "beneath" usually signify more external or baser corruptions.</note> *there is a dreadful hell, where the inhabitants seem to strike at each other with knives, aiming them, like furies, at each other’s breasts; but at the instant of giving the blow, the knife is always taken away from them. This hell was opened, to the end that I might see the nature of mortal hatred, but only in a small degree, on account of their dreadful cruelties.*

819. *There is a capacious stagnant lake towards the left in a plane with the lower parts of the body, whose length is greater than its breadth. About its front bank there appear to the neighboring inhabitants monsters of serpents such as frequent stagnant lakes, breathing a pestilent exhalation. On the left bank, a little further, are those who eat human flesh, and devour each other, [and who are seen] with their teeth sticking in one another’s shoulders. Still towards the left, but at a greater distance, there are seen great fishes and large sea-monsters, which devour men and then vomit them up again. And yet more remotely, or on the opposite bank, there appear some horribly deformed faces, particularly those of old women, running to and fro like mad persons, so monstrous that it is impossible to describe them. On the right bank dwell those who endeavor to kill each other with frightful instruments of various kinds, according to the terrible animosities of their hearts: the midst of the lake is everywhere black like a bog or morass. Sometimes I have seen spirits brought to this lake, and on expressing my surprise, have been informed by some who came from thence, that those spirits were such as had indulged in deadly hatred against their neighbor, which burst forth as often as occasion offered, and that in this they perceived their greatest delight, nothing being more agreeable to them than to accuse their neighbors of crimes...*

820. *Those who during their life in the world have practised robbery, and such as have been pirates, are delighted with fetid and stinking urine above all other liquids, and they appear to themselves to have their habitations in the midst of them, and likewise in stagnant lakes of a disagreeable odor. A certain robber approached me, gnashing his teeth, the noise of which was as plainly heard as if it had proceeded from a man, an astonishing circumstance, since those* <term>spirits</term> <note>Spirits here refers to people who have recently died and are in the intermediate state between heaven and hell.</note> *have no teeth. 821. *There are some* <term>spirits</term> *who present outwardly a fair aspect, and upright life, so that none would suspect their integrity. They study by every method to put on such an appearance, for the sake of being advanced to honors, and of enriching themselves without the loss of reputation. Wherefore, what they do, they do covertly, using others as instruments for obtaining, by deceitful artifices, the property of their neighbors, without any regard to the distress of the families whom they hereby reduce to indigence. They would themselves be personal agents in this villany, without any remorse of conscience, could they only escape public notice, and are, of course, equally guilty as if they were so. These are secret robbers, and the kind of hatred peculiar to them is conjoined with haughtiness, greediness of gain, unmercifulness, and deceit. Such persons are in another life desirous of being deemed guiltless, insisting that they have done no evil, because it had never been discovered; and in order to clear themselves from every imputation of guilt, they strip off their clothes, and show themselves naked, thus testifying their innocence.* <note>Nakedness in this spiritual vision symbolizes an attempt to show that one has "nothing to hide," though here it is a desperate and false performance.</note> *During their examination, it is clearly evident, both from their every expression, and every idea of thought, what sort of* <term>spirits</term> *they are, although this is unknown to themselves. These* <term>spirits</term> *are, in the other life, ready to destroy such of their companions as offend them, without the slightest remorse; they carry moreover in their hands an axe and a hammer, and seem to have another spirit with them, whom they strike as he stoops down, but they are cautious of shedding blood, because they are fearful of death. It is not in their power to cast these instruments out of their hands, although they attempt it with all their might, to prevent the barbarity of their dispositions from being apparent to* <term>spirits</term> *and angels. They reside at an intermediate distance between the two feet in front.* <note>The author organizes the spiritual world according to the "Grand Man" (the *Maximus Homo*); regions associated with the feet generally relate to things that are very grounded, external, or "natural" rather than spiritual.</note>

822. *There is one kind of hatred towards the neighbor, which finds its delight in doing injuries, and in annoying every one, and the more mischief it occasions the better is it pleased. Many of the lowest of the people are of this character; but there are also persons of higher rank, whose disposition is similar, although they are outwardly better behaved, in consequence of the superiority of their education, and the apprehension they entertain of legal punishment. After death, the upper part of the body of these* <term>spirits</term> <note>Spirits: people who have died and are now living in the intermediate spiritual realm before their final state is determined.</note> *appears naked, and their hair dishevelled: they annoy one another by rushing forward and placing the palms of their hands on each other's shoulders, when leaping over their heads, they quickly return to the assault and beat one another grievously. Those who are better behaved, of whom we were last speaking, act in a similar manner, but to save appearances, they first salute each other, and then going round, make their assault behind, striking with their fists; when, however, they see each other in front, they again proffer their salutations, and passing round again make their assault behind: they are seen at some distance to the left, in a middle altitude.* <note>Middle altitude: in the author's spiritual geography, the position of a spirit (above, below, left, or right) indicates their specific internal state and character.</note>

823. *Whatever a man has done, or even thought, in the life of the body, returns successively in the other life. When feelings of enmity, hatred, and deceit recur, the persons against whom they have been indulged, and whose injury has been clandestinely contrived, are also presented, and that immediately, as will, by the divine mercy of the Lord, be more fully described hereafter. It is, in consequence of a perception of the thoughts of all being communicated in the other life, that those entertained against others appear openly, the most lamentable states being induced when the hidden feelings of enmity burst forth.* <note>The author explains that in the spiritual world, one's private thoughts are no longer hidden but are "broadcast" or perceived by others, making hypocrisy impossible.</note>

With the wicked, all their evil deeds and thoughts thus vividly return; but with the good, it is not so, all their states of goodness, friendship, and love, recurring with the greatest possible delight and happiness.

# GENESIS.

## CHAPTER THE EIGHTH.

### CONTINUATION RESPECTING THE HELLS.

->**OF THE HELLS OF THOSE WHO HAVE PASSED THEIR LIVES IN ADULTERIES AND LASCIVIOUSNESS, AND, ALSO, OF THE HELLS OF THE DECEITFUL, AND OF CRAFTY WOMEN.**<-

<margin>The reader is requested to observe that the author is describing the location of these spiritual societies based on how they correspond to the different parts of the human body.</margin>

824. *UNDER the heel<gloss>The "heel" here refers to a specific spiritual location that corresponds to the lowest or most external parts of human life.</gloss> of the right foot is the hell inhabited by those who have taken delight both in cruelty and in adulteries, finding in these things the greatest satisfaction of their lives. It is a surprising fact that those who were cruel during their life in the body were also adulterers more than anyone else; they reside in that hell, where they practice cruelties through the most wicked inventions. By using their phantasies,<note>In this context, "phantasies" refers to the ability of spirits to create vivid, sensory illusions or mental projections that seem entirely real to those experiencing them.</note> they create vessels and instruments like pestles and mortars—such as those used for crushing herbs—with which they crush and torture anyone they can. They also construct broad axes, similar to those used by executioners, and a type of awl or drill with which they cruelly torment one another, not to mention many other horrific practices. In that hell are some of the Jews who in former times treated the non-Jewish people so barbarously. Today, that hell is growing, fueled especially by those from the so-called Christian world who have placed their chief delight in adultery, as these individuals are for the most part also cruel. Sometimes their delight is transformed into the stench of human waste, which pours out abundantly when the hell is opened; when this is sensed in the world of spirits,<note>The "world of spirits" is the intermediate realm where people first go after death before transitioning to heaven or hell.</note> it immediately causes a person to feel faint, as I have experienced. This foul smell sometimes prevails and sometimes ceases in these hells, for the delight they felt in adultery is what changes into this smell. In time, when they have completed their allotted period in these conditions, they are left alone and sit in torment, becoming like deformed skeletons, though they continue to live.*

825. *In the plane of the soles of the feet, some distance forward, there is a hell called Gehennah<note>original: "Gehennah." This term derives from the Hebrew "Ge-Hinnom" (Valley of Hinnom), a site outside Jerusalem that came to symbolize a place of fire and purification or punishment.</note> inhabited by immodest women who placed their entire delight in adultery. These women considered such acts not only lawful but even respectable, and they lured the guiltless and innocent into these practices by using various false appearances of good character and social standing. *...visible in that hell a kind of fiery appearance, such as is often seen shining in the air from a great fire; and it is attended also with heat, which it was given me to feel by the warmth thence communicated to my face; and a stench exhales thence similar to that arising from burnt bones and hair. This hell is sometimes changed into dreadful serpents, which bite the inhabitants, who desire death, but cannot die. Some of the women being liberated thence, mentioned, on coming to me, that it is burning hot there, but that when they are allowed to approach any society of good spirits, their heat becomes changed into intense cold, and at such times they experience in themselves an alternation of heat and cold, passing from one extreme to the other, and being thereby miserably tortured. Nevertheless there are intervals during which they are in the excitement of their fiery lust; but their states become changed in the manner described.*

826. *There have been some persons of both sexes from that part of the world called Christendom, who, during their life in the body have regarded adulteries as not only lawful, but even holy, thus considering what they have impiously denominated community of wives as sacred. I observed that these were sent to Gehennah <gloss>Gehennah is a biblical term for a place of fiery punishment or destruction</gloss>, but when they came thither, a change took place; the fiery appearance of Gehennah, which is of a reddish cast, becoming on their arrival whitish, and it was perceived that they could not agree together. That wicked band was therefore separated, and conveyed to the region behind, thus, as it were, into another world, where they had to be immersed in stagnant lakes, and thence passed to a new Gehennah appointed for them. There was heard in Gehennah an indescribable kind of hissing, the hissing or murmur of Gehennah being duller than that of the spirits who had defiled holiness by adulteries.*

827. *Those who ensnare by pretending a regard for <term>conjugial love</term><note>The author uses the specific term "conjugial" (from Latin *conjugialis*) rather than "conjugal" to describe a spiritual, heavenly union between spouses, rather than a merely physical or legal one.</note>, and for love towards children, behaving themselves in such a manner that a husband has no suspicion but that they are chaste, innocent, and friendly, and who, under these and various other pretences, commit adultery with the greater security, are in a hell beneath the buttocks <term>[sub natibus]</term>, amongst the filthiest excrements, and, because they rank with the treacherous, become <term>vastated</term><note>In this context, "vastation" refers to a process in the spiritual world where a person's external pretenses or borrowed virtues are stripped away, leaving only the bare reality of their internal character.</note> to such a degree as to be like mere bones. Such persons do not even know what conscience is. I have conversed with them, and they are surprised that any one should have a conscience, and should say that adulteries are contrary to it. They were informed that it is as impossible for such unconscientious adulterers to come into heaven as for a fish to live in air, or a bird in ether, because on the instant of their approach, they would feel, as it were, suffocated, their adulterous delight becoming changed into a most offensive stench; and further, that they must needs be thrust down into hell, and become finally like bony substances, possessing scarcely any vitality, because they have acquired to themselves...*

*a life so wicked, that, on losing it, there remains almost nothing of life truly human.*

828. *Those who desire nothing more than to deflower virgins—specifically those who find their greatest delight in the "spoils" of virginity without any regard for marriage or children—suffer the most severe punishment in the afterlife. Once they have satisfied their lusts, they often feel a deep hatred for their victims and abandon them to a life of prostitution. Because their earthly life was lived in total opposition to all natural, spiritual, and heavenly order, they are seen as enemies of <term>conjugal love</term> <note>From the Latin 'amor conjugialis,' referring to a spiritually perfected marriage union that Swedenborg believes is the foundation of heaven.</note>. They are also enemies of innocence, which they wound and destroy by seducing those who might have otherwise entered into a holy marriage. Since the holiness of heaven is built upon the foundations of marriage and innocence, those who destroy these things are essentially <term>interiorly homicides</term> <note>Swedenborg argues that destroying someone's spiritual capacity for love and innocence is a form of "murder" (homicide) within the soul, even if no physical body is killed.</note>. In the spiritual world, these people appear to themselves to be riding a wild, raging horse that tosses them high into the air. They fall back down in terror, fearing for their lives. Afterwards, they seem to crawl under the belly of the horse and enter it through its rear. They then suddenly find themselves inside the belly of a filthy harlot, who transforms into a great dragon; there they remain trapped in torment. This punishment repeats many times over hundreds or even thousands of years, until they are filled with genuine horror at their own past desires. I have also been told that the children of such parents are often more prone to evil than others because they inherit a <term>hereditary constitution</term> <note>The idea that a parent's spiritual state or dominant character traits could be passed down to their children as a biological or spiritual predisposition.</note> from the father's nature. Consequently, children are rarely born from such fleeting connections, and if they are, they often do not live long.*

829. *Those who constantly dwell on lewd and lascivious thoughts during their physical life—even turning holy conversations into something obscene—carry this habit into the next life. This is especially true for those who continued this behavior into middle and old age, when they could no longer blame youthful impulses. In the spiritual world, thoughts are visible and shared; these individuals' thoughts are sometimes turned into obscene visual representations that offend other spirits. As a punishment, they are laid out horizontally in front of the spirits they have offended and are spun around rapidly like a roll of fabric from left to right. Then they are turned and spun in a different direction, and then a third, either naked or half-naked depending on the nature of their lewdness, until they are overcome with shame. They are later rolled by their head and feet in a hinging motion, which causes great pain through the resistance of two opposing forces—one pulling them in a circle and the other pulling them backward—and*

When this is completed, they have permission granted them to withdraw from the sight of spirits, and then a sense of shame is instilled into them; nevertheless they are still not without temptations to continue the same evil practices, but, so long as they are in a state of shame and grief, they are careful of yielding to them. This punishment was seen at some distance towards the front.*

829. *There are also boys, youths, and young men, who, in consequence of the impetuosity of youth, have conceived wicked and pernicious principles, supposing that wives, and especially such as are young and beautiful, ought not to be confined to their husbands, but to be free to themselves and their like, the husband remaining only as the head of the family, and the educator of the children. These are distinguished in the other life by their boyish tone of voice, and reside at some height backwards. Such amongst them as have confirmed themselves in these principles, and in a practice conformable thereto, are miserably tormented in another world, by having their joints put out and in alternately, which is effected by spirits, who have the art to excite in others a <term>phantasy</term> <note>In Swedenborg's theology, 'phantasy' is not merely an imagination, but a vivid, sensory experience in the spiritual world that feels entirely real to the spirit experiencing it.</note> as if they were still in the body, and at the same time a sense of bodily pain. By these contortions and retortions, and the struggles they make in opposition to them, they are so lacerated as to seem to themselves torn into minute fragments, with exceeding great pain; and this punishment is repeated, until being struck with horror at their principles, they desist from such thoughts.*

830. *Those who deceive others by artful dissimulation, making a show of friendliness in the countenance and discourse, whilst they conceal inwardly the poison of treacherous enmity, and thus allure with a design to destroy, are in a hell more terrible than that of others, and indeed more terrible than the hell of murderers. They appear to themselves to be living amongst serpents, and the more pernicious their stratagems have been, so much the more dreadful, poisonous, and numerous do the serpents, which encompass and torment them, appear. They know no other than that these serpents are real, inasmuch as they occasion similar pains and torments, which possibly few will believe, although it is a certain fact. These are they who purposely or with premeditation exercise deceit, and therein experience the delight of their life.* <note>Swedenborg often ranks deceit as the ultimate evil because it destroys the internal spiritual connection between people, whereas physical violence only affects the external body.</note> *The punishments of the deceitful are various, according to the nature of the deceit of each. In general they are not tolerated in societies, but are expelled; for whatever any spirit thinks is immediately known and perceived by neighboring spirits, and consequently every species of deceit is recognized. Hence at length such deceitful spirits sit down in solitude, being expelled from all society, and then they appear with their faces dilated, so as to be four or five times the breadth of an ordinary face, with a broad fleshy cap, of a whitish color, upon their heads, like images of* <note>The "dilated face" and "fleshy cap" are symbolic appearances in the spirit world, representing how the spirit’s inner falsehood has distorted their spiritual form.</note>

### 831.
There are some of the female sex, who have lived in the indulgence of their inclinations, regarding only themselves and the world, and making the all of life and its delight to consist in external decorum, in consequence of which they have been particularly esteemed in polished society. They have thus, by practice, acquired the talent of insinuating themselves into the good graces of others, by specious pretences and a fair exterior, for the purpose of gaining an ascendancy over them; and hence their life has been one of simulation and deceit. They used to frequent churches like other people, but for no other end than to appear upright and pious; being moreover destitute of conscience, and exceedingly prone to wickedness and adulteries, when able to conceal them. 

Such persons in another life think as they did here, knowing not what conscience is, and making a mock of those who speak of it; they enter into the affections of others by a pretended honesty, piety, compassion, and innocence, which with them are the means of deceiving; and whenever external restraints are removed, they plunge into the most wicked and obscene practices. These are they who, in the other world, become enchantresses or sorceresses, of whom there are some denominated <term>sirens</term> <note>In this context, 'sirens' refers to spirits who use beautiful appearances and voices to lure others into spiritual harm, mirroring the Greek myth but focused on psychological manipulation.</note>, who become expert in arts unknown on earth; and are like sponges, imbibing all wicked artifices, from being of such a genius as readily to practise them. 

The artifices unknown here, which they learn in the spiritual world, are these:
*   They can speak as if from a different place to that in which they are, the voice being heard as if proceeding from good spirits elsewhere. 
*   They can be, as it were, present with several persons at the same time, thus persuading others that they are present everywhere, and they speak like several together, and in various places at the same moment. 
*   They have the power of averting the <term>influx</term> <note>The 'influx' refers to the spiritual energy or influence flowing from the divine or from higher angelic realms into lower spirits and humans.</note> from good spirits, yea, even that of angelic spirits, perverting it instantly by curious methods in favor of themselves. 
*   They can assume another’s likeness by ideas which they conceive and fashion to themselves; and can inspire every one with an affection for them, by insinuating themselves into the real state of another’s affection. 
*   They can suddenly withdraw themselves out of sight, and become invisible. 
*   They have the power of representing to the view of spirits a bright flame encompassing the head, and this, which is an angelic token, to several at the same moment. 
*   They can feign innocence by various methods, even by representing infants whom they kiss; they also excite others, whom they hate, to murder them, because

# THE CONTENTS.

832. The subject, following its regular order, is the man of the new church, who is called <term>Noah</term>; specifically, it describes his state after <term>temptation</term> <note>In this context, temptation refers to a period of internal spiritual struggle or trial.</note>, leading up to his <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new.</note>.
833. His first state after this trial, and his fluctuation between what is true and what is false until truths begin to appear, is discussed from verse 1 to 5.
834. His second state consists of three parts: first, when the truths of faith do not yet exist; next, when they are joined with <term>charity</term> <note>A term used here to mean selfless love and goodwill toward others.</note>; and finally, when the good results of that charity shine forth, in verses 6 to 14.
835. His third state is when he begins to act and think from a place of charity; this is the first stage of a person being "regenerated," in verses 15 to 19.
836. His fourth state is when he acts and thinks from charity as a settled habit; this is the second stage of being regenerated, in verses 20 and 21.
837. Finally, the new church, which is established in place of the former one, is described in verses 21 and 22.

---

# THE INTERNAL SENSE.

838. In the two preceding chapters, the new church called *Noah*, or the person belonging to that church, was discussed. This included his preparation to receive faith (and through faith, charity), his trials, and his protection when the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The symbolic name for the earliest state of human spirituality, which the author describes as having fallen away prior to the "flood."</note> perished. What follows here is his state after those trials, described in the exact order in which it occurs for everyone who undergoes spiritual rebirth. The Word of the Lord is written so that even when it speaks of one person, it actually refers to all people and every individual, with differences based on each person's character; this is the <term>universal sense</term> <note>The idea that the Bible contains deep, spiritual meanings that apply to the human soul generally, rather than just historical events.</note> of the Word.

839. Verse 1. *And God remembered Noah, and every wild beast, and every beast, which was with him in the ark; and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters assuaged.* By the phrase *God remembered*, it signifies the end of the trial and the start of a renewal. By *Noah*, it means, as before, the man of the <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>The spiritual state of humanity that followed the "flood," characterized by a new way of connecting with the Divine through conscience and instruction.</note>. *Every wild beast, and every beast which was with him in the ark*, represents everything that this person possessed spiritually. *God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters assuaged*, represents the process of bringing all parts of the person's mind and life back into their proper order.

So long as temptation continues, man supposes the Lord to be absent, because being disturbed by evil <term>genii</term> <note>original: "genii"; referring to spiritual influences or spirits that affect a person's inner state and thoughts.</note>, to such a degree as sometimes to be reduced to a state of despair, he can scarcely believe that any God exists, although the Lord is then more intimately present than he can ever conceive. When, however, temptation ceases, then he receives consolation, and begins to believe that the Lord is present ; and this being the case here, *God is said to remember*, to denote the end of his temptation, and the beginning of his renovation. The word *God* is here used, and not *Jehovah*, because as yet man was in a state antecedent to that of <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new.</note> ; but when he becomes regenerate, then mention is made of *Jehovah*, as at the end of this chapter, verses 20, 21. The reason of this is, because faith was not yet conjoined with <term>charity</term> <note>A term for selfless love and goodwill; here, faith alone is seen as a preliminary state.</note>, for man is first said to be regenerate when he acts from charity. In charity Jehovah is present, but not so in faith prior to its conjunction with charity. Charity is the very <term>being</term> <note>original: "esse"; the innermost essence or life-force.</note> and life of man in the other world ; and as it is Jehovah who is <term>being</term> <note>original: "esse"</note> itself and life itself, so before man is, and lives, *Jehovah* cannot be said to be with him, but God.

841. By *Noah* is signified, as before, the man of the <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>The second great period of spiritual history, following the "Most Ancient Church" (the era of Adam).</note> ; and by *every wild beast*, and *every beast which was with him in the ark*, every thing which belonged to him, as is demonstrated from what was previously stated respecting *Noah*, and the signification of *wild beast*, and *beast*. The term *wild beast* is taken in a two-fold sense in the <term>Word</term> <note>A common term for the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, denoting both those things in man which are alive, and those which are dead. It denotes what is alive, because its correlative in the Hebrew tongue signifies a living thing ; and in consequence of the most ancient people, in their humiliation, acknowledging themselves to be as wild beasts, this word became also a type of what is dead in man. In the present passage, by *wild beasts* are represented both what is alive and what is dead in one complex ; for, as is customary with man after temptation, the living and the dead, or the things of the Lord, and those of man's <term>self-nature</term> <note>original: "proprium"; that which belongs to the human ego or selfhood, often viewed as the source of selfish impulses.</note>, appear so confused that he scarcely knows what is true and good ; the Lord then, however, reduces and disposes all things in order, as will be subsequently shown. That a *wild beast* signifies what is alive in man, may be seen in the preceding chapter (vii.), verse 14, and in the present chapter, verses 17 and 19 ; that they also represent things which are dead in man, is evident from what was observed above respecting *wild beasts* and *beasts*, n. 45, 46, 142, 143, 246.
