All spirits, both good and bad, are compared and likened to *wind*, and in the original tongue <note>Referring to the Hebrew language.</note> both spirits and winds are expressed by the same word. In <term>temptations</term> <note>Internal spiritual struggles where a person feels overwhelmed by negative thoughts or doubts.</note>—which are here symbolized by *the waters that assuaged*, as was shown above—evil spirits cause an inundation, in consequence of entering by <term>influx</term> <note>The process by which spiritual forces flow into a person's mind and feelings.</note> in great multitudes with their <term>phantasies</term> <note>Distorted, false, or harmful mental images and beliefs projected by spirits.</note>, and exciting similar phantasies in man; and when these spirits or their phantasies are dispersed, it is said in the Word to be done by a *wind*, and indeed by an *east wind*. 

Every man individually is similarly circumstanced during temptation and when the commotions or waters of temptation cease, as man in general, as has been given me to know by repeated experience; for evil spirits in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>An intermediate realm between heaven and hell where spirits are prepared for their final destination.</note> sometimes associate themselves in troops, and thereby excite disturbances until they are dispersed by other bands of spirits generally coming from the right, consequently from the eastern quarter, who strike such fear and terror into them, that they think of nothing but how they can escape. Thus those who had associated themselves are dispersed into all quarters, and thereby the societies of spirits formed for evil purposes are dissolved. The troops of spirits who disperse them are called the *east wind*; and there are also innumerable other methods of dispersion, denominated *east winds*, of which, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said hereafter. 

When evil spirits are thus dispersed, the state of commotion and turbulence is succeeded by serenity, or silence, as is also the case with man when tempted; for during that state he is in the midst of such a band of spirits, but when they are driven away or dispersed, there follows, as it were a calm, which is the commencement of the disposal of all things into order. Before reducing any thing into a state of order, it is most usual to bring the whole into a kind of confused mass, or chaos as it were, for the purpose of disjoining what do not well cohere together, and when they are disunited, then the Lord disposes them into order. This process may be compared with what is observable in nature, where all things, both in general and particular, are first reduced to a kind of confused mass before being disposed or arranged regularly. Thus, for instance, unless there were storms in the atmosphere, to dissipate whatever is <term>heterogeneous</term> <note>Elements that are different in kind or do not belong together; mismatched parts.</note>, the air could never become serene, but would be rendered pestiferous by the accumulation of unwholesome vapors. So in like manner in the human body, unless every part of the blood, as well what is heterogeneous as what is <term>homogeneous</term> <note>Elements that are of the same kind or belong together; harmonious parts.</note>, did continuously and successively flow together into one heart, to be there commingled, there would ensue a fatal coagulation of the liquids, which would render it impossible for the particular component parts to be distinctly disposed to their respective uses. That *wind*, and especially that the *east wind*, signifies the dispersion of <term>falses</term> <note>A term used here to describe false beliefs, errors, or delusions that cloud the mind.</note> and evils, or, what is the same, of evil spirits and <term>genii</term> <note>A specific class of evil spirits that influence a person's emotions and hidden desires.</note>, and afterwards an arranging into order, is evident from the Word; as from Isaiah: “Thou shalt disperse them, and the *wind* shall carry them away, and the *whirlwind* shall dissipate them, and thou shalt rejoice in Jehovah, and glory in the Holy One of Israel,” (xli. 16.) Similar also was the representation of the *east wind* by which the Red Sea was dried up, that the children of Israel might pass over, as described in Exodus: “Jehovah caused the Red Sea to go back, by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry, and the waters were divided,” (xiv. 21.) The signification of *the waters of the Red Sea* was similar to that of the waters of the flood in the present passage, as is evident from this consideration, that the Egyptians, by whom are represented the wicked, were drowned therein, whilst the children of Israel, who are typical of the regenerate, as *Noah* is here, passed over. By *the Red Sea*, as by the flood, is denoted condemnation also, and temptation; consequently *by the east wind* is signified the dissipation of the waters or evils of condemnation, or temptation, as is evident from the song of Moses after they had passed over, (Exod. xv. 1—19;) and from Isaiah: “Jehovah shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea, and with his mighty wind shall he shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dry-shod. ### 843—846.] GENESIS. 311

*fountains of the abyss* denoting evils of the <term>will</term> <note>In this context, the "will" refers to the seat of human desires and intentions.</note>; the *cataracts of the heaven*, <term>falses</term> <note>A technical term for false beliefs or intellectual errors that distort a person's perspective.</note> of the understanding; and *rain*, temptation in general.

844. From this to the sixth verse it treats of the first state of the man of this church subsequent to temptation; and what is said in the present verse signifies the cessation of temptation. His temptation, both as to the things of the will and as to those of the understanding, has been previously spoken of; and its termination as to voluntary things is here meant by *the fountains of the abyss being stopped*; and its cessation as to the understanding, by *the cataracts of heaven being stopped*. That these expressions have such a signification, was asserted and demonstrated in the preceding chapter, verse 11; and that *rain* denotes temptation itself was also shown, verse 12, of the same chapter, wherefore there is no need to dwell longer on the subject.

845. The reason why *the fountains of the abyss* signify temptation as to the things of the will, and *the cataracts of heaven* temptation in reference to those of the understanding, is, that it is the will of man which is influenced by hell, and not the intellectual principle, unless it be immersed in <term>lusts</term> <note>Intense, disordered desires that originate in the self-centered will.</note> which are of the will. Evils, which belong to the will, are what condemn man and sink him down to hell, and falses only so far as they become conjoined with evils, when one follows the other. This may be proved by numerous instances of those who, being in falses, are yet saved: as is the case with many amongst the gentiles, who have lived in natural charity and in mercy, and with numbers of Christians who have believed in simplicity of heart. Their ignorance and simplicity are their excuse, because in them there may be innocence; but it is otherwise with those who have confirmed themselves in falses, and have thus contracted such a life of the false, as to refuse and oppose all truth, since this life must necessarily be <term>vastated</term> <note>A process of spiritual clearing where false ideas are stripped away so that a person can be open to the truth.</note> before any thing of truth and thereby of good can be <term>inseminated</term> <note>Planted like a seed in the mind or soul.</note>. It is, however, still worse with those who from <term>cupidity</term> <note>A strong, often selfish desire or greed.</note> have confirmed themselves in falses, so that falses and lusts constitute one life; for these are they who sink themselves down into hell. This is the cause of temptation as to voluntary things being signified by *the fountains of the abyss*, which are the hells, and temptation as to intellectual things by *the cataracts of heaven*, which are the clouds, from which comes rain.

846. Verse 3. *And the waters receded from off the earth, in going and returning; and after the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters were abated.* By *the waters receded from off the earth, in going and returning*, are signified fluctuations between the true and the false; and by *the waters abating after the end of the hundred and fifty days*, the cessation of temptations. *A hundred and fifty days* signify here, as above, a <term>terminus</term> <note>original: "terminus"; a boundary, limit, or concluding point.</note>

It highlights that salvation is possible for those in intellectual error if their hearts are well-intentioned, whereas confirmed evil in the will leads to spiritual ruin.</summary>

By *the waters receded from off the earth*, are signified *fluctuations between the true and the false*, as is evident from the previous statement that the waters of the flood, or inundations, with respect to Noah, denote <term>temptations</term> <note>In this context, temptation refers to an internal spiritual struggle where a person's values and beliefs are tested.</note>; for as it here treats of the first state after <term>temptation</term>, *the waters receding in going and returning* can represent nothing else than fluctuation between truths and falses. The nature of this fluctuation, however, can only be known after man becomes acquainted with the nature of <term>temptation</term>, for such as the <term>temptation</term> is, such is the fluctuation succeeding to it. When the <term>temptation</term> is <term>celestial</term> <note>Celestial refers to the highest level of spiritual life, centered on love for the Divine.</note>, then the fluctuation is between good and evil; when it is <term>spiritual</term> <note>Spiritual refers to the level of the mind concerned with truth, logic, and neighborly charity.</note>, between the true and the false; and when it is <term>natural</term> <note>Natural refers to the lowest level of the mind, dealing with worldly matters and physical desires.</note>, the fluctuation is between what agrees with and what is contrary to his natural <term>desires</term> <note>original Latin: "cupiditates", referring to disordered cravings or lusts of the lower self.</note>. There are several kinds of <term>temptations</term>, which in general may be divided into the <term>celestial</term>, <term>spiritual</term>, and <term>natural</term>, and these ought never to be confounded with each other. <term>Celestial temptations</term> can have no place except with those who are principled in love towards the Lord; and <term>spiritual</term> with those only who are in charity towards their neighbor. <term>Natural temptations</term> are altogether distinct from these, and are not indeed truly <term>temptations</term>, but merely anxieties arising from the assault of <term>natural</term> loves, in consequence of misfortunes, diseases, or a depraved condition of the blood and other fluids of the body. From this short account it may, in some degree, be seen that <term>temptation</term> is anguish and anxiety occasioned by whatever opposes or resists any particular kind of love. Thus with those who are in love towards the Lord, whatever assaults this love produces an inmost torture, which is <term>celestial temptation</term>; also with such as are in love towards the neighbor, or charity, whatever assaults this love occasions torment of conscience, and this is <term>spiritual temptation</term>. With those who are merely <term>natural</term>, what they frequently call <term>temptations</term>, and the pangs of conscience, are not truly so, but only anxieties arising from the assault of their loves, as when they foresee and are sensible of the loss of honor, the good things of the world, reputation, pleasures, bodily life, and the like; nevertheless these troubles are wont to be productive of some good. <term>Temptations</term> are moreover experienced by such as are principled in natural charity, and consequently by all kinds of heretics, gentiles, and idolaters, arising from every assault on the life of the faith which they cherish. These straitnesses <note>Difficulties or narrow passages of the mind.</note>, however, bear only a faint resemblance to <term>spiritual temptations</term>.

### 847—851.] GENESIS. 313

<insert>Regenera</insert>tion has as its goal that a person may receive *new life*, or rather that they may receive *life* itself. From being "no man," they may become a truly human being; from being *dead*, they may be made *living*. Therefore, when their former life—which is merely animal—is destroyed through **spiritual trials** <note>original: "temptations"; in this context, these are internal struggles where one's values and beliefs are tested.</note>, it is inevitable that they will waver between what is true and what is false. Truth belongs to the *new life*, while falsity belongs to the old; and unless that former life is dismantled and this period of wavering occurs, it is impossible for any spiritual seed to be planted, because there is no ground for it. 

**848.** When all of this is accomplished, however, the person hardly knows what is true and good, or even if such things as "truth" exist at all. For example, when reflecting on the good deeds of charity—commonly called "good works"—they might wonder if they can do them on their own or not. They might also feel that they deserve credit for whatever they do by their own power. In this state, they are in such obscurity and darkness that when they are told no one can do good from themselves or from their own **selfhood** <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium"; a technical term for the human ego or the sense of self that feels independent of the Divine.</note>, and even less can anyone claim merit—for all good is from the Lord and all merit is His alone—they are completely astonished. They feel the same way about all other truths of faith. Yet, despite the great obscurity and darkness of the mind, it becomes noticeably, though gradually, enlightened. 

**Spiritual rebirth** <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of being spiritually made new.</note> is accurately illustrated by a human birth as an infant. An infant's life is at first very obscure; the baby knows almost nothing and receives only general impressions from the objects around them. These impressions, however, become more distinct as specific ideas are introduced, which then lead to even more specific ones. In this way, general notions are filled in with individual details, and the person learns not only that things exist, but also understands their nature and quality. This is how it is for everyone emerging from a spiritual trial. The state of those in the next life who, having been stuck in errors, are **cleansed** <term>vastated</term> <note>original: "vastated"; a spiritual process of purging or clearing away false beliefs to prepare a soul for heaven.</note>, is quite similar. This state is called *fluctuation* (or wavering), and is described here by the biblical phrase: *the waters receding in going and returning*.

849. From this, it clearly follows that by *the waters abated at the end of a hundred and fifty days* is meant the end of these trials. That *a hundred and fifty days* signifies a **limit** <term>terminus</term> <note>original: "terminus"; a boundary or conclusion.</note> is clear from what was said about this number in the previous chapter (verse 24); consequently, it represents the conclusion of the period of wavering and the start of a new life.

**865.** By *sending forth a raven, and it went forth, going to and fro*, it is meant that falsehoods were still causing a disturbance, as is clear from the meaning of a *raven* and of *going to and fro*, which will be discussed more later. In this state, falsehoods are constantly causing trouble, so it resembles the morning twilight, where some of the darkness of night still remains.

Falsities, with the spiritual man, and especially before his <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or being made new by God.</note>, are like the dense spots of a cloud. The reason is, because he can know nothing of the truth of faith, except by what is revealed in the Word, where every thing is stated in a general way; and general truths are but as the spots of a cloud, for every single general truth comprehends in it thousands and thousands of particulars, and each particular thousands and thousands of individual truths, all general truths being illustrated by the individual facts which constitute particulars. These specific truths are never therefore revealed to man, because they are both indescribable and inconceivable, and consequently can neither be acknowledged nor believed in, as being contrary to the fallacies of the senses in which man is born, and which he does not easily permit to be destroyed. 

It is, however, altogether otherwise with the <term>celestial man</term> <note>A person who is guided by love and a direct, intuitive perception of what is true and good.</note>, who possesses *perception* from the Lord; for in him particular truths, and the individual facts of which they are composed, are capable of being insinuated. For example, a true marriage is that of one man with one wife; this is representative of the celestial marriage, and is consequently admissive of heavenly happiness, which a marriage of one man with several wives is not. Now the <term>spiritual man</term> <note>A person who is guided by the intellect and obedience to the rules and truths they have learned from scripture.</note>, who knows this to be true from the Word of the Lord, acquiesces in it, and hence admits as a point of conscience, that marriage with more wives than one is a sin, but he knows no more; whilst the celestial man perceives a thousand particular truths, confirming the general truth, so that marriage with several wives excites his abhorrence. As the spiritual man is only acquainted with general truths, and has his conscience formed from these, and as the general truths of the Word are accommodated to the fallacies of the senses, it is evident that innumerable falsities, which cannot be dispersed, will adjoin and insuinate themselves into them;—it is these falsities which are here signified by *the raven which went forth going to and fro.*

**866.** A *raven* signifies falsities, as is demonstrable from what was said and shown above concerning *birds* in general, as denoting intellectual, rational, and scientific truths, and also their opposites, which are reasonings and falses. Both these are described in the Word by various species of *birds*; intellectual truths by those which are gentle, beautiful, and clean, and falses by the ravenous, ugly, and unclean, varying according to the specific truth or falsity. Gross and dense falsities are typified by *owls* and *ravens*; by *owls*, because they live in the darkness of night, and by *ravens*, because they are of a black color; as in Isaiah: "The *owl* also, and the *raven* shall dwell in it," (xxxiv. 11;) speaking of the Jewish Church as being the habitation of mere falsities, represented by the *owl* and the *raven*.

<summary>This page explains the symbolic meaning of the raven in Noah's ark as the lingering false thoughts that haunt a person during spiritual growth. It highlights the difference between the 'spiritual' person, who follows general rules, and the 'celestial' person, who intuitively understands the deeper reasons for those rules.</summary>

## 866—868.] GENESIS

867. *Going to and fro* denotes that such was their state, as is evident from the nature of the falsities with man, when in his first and second state after temptation, for they then fly about as it were, so as to *go forth and return*. This is for the reason mentioned above, man at that time being necessarily only in the knowledge of the most general truths, into which there is an influx of the phantasies <note>In this context, "phantasies" refers to illusory or deceptive thoughts arising from the physical senses and worldly desires.</note> arising from corporeal, sensual, and worldly ideas, which are opposed to the truths of faith.

868. *The drying up of the waters from off the faces of the earth*, signifies the apparent dissipation of falsities, as is manifest from the state of man when regenerated. It is universally believed in the present day that evils and falsities in man are entirely separated and abolished during regeneration, so that when he becomes regenerate, nothing of the evil or falsity remains, but that he is clean and righteous, like one washed and purified with water. This notion is, however, utterly erroneous; for not a single evil or falsity can be so shaken off as to be abolished; but whatever has been hereditarily derived in infancy, or acquired by man's own act and deed, remains; so that man, notwithstanding his being regenerate, is altogether evil and false, as is vividly perceived by souls after death. The truth of this fact may appear sufficiently evident from the consideration, that there is nothing good and true in man except from the Lord, and that all evil and falsity are from <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium." A technical term meaning "what is one's own." It refers to the human ego or selfhood, which the author argues is inherently inclined toward evil.</note>, hence that every man, and every spirit, yea, and every angel, if left for a single moment to himself, would rush spontaneously into hell; wherefore also it is said, in the Word, that *the heavens are not pure*. <note>A reference to the Book of Job 15:15.</note> This the angels acknowledge, and whosoever refuses to acknowledge it cannot dwell with them, for it is the mercy of the Lord alone which delivers them; yea, which draws and keeps them out of hell, lest they should precipitate themselves thither of their own accord. The angels perceive manifestly that they are thus kept by the Lord from falling into hell, and it is also evident in some degree to good spirits; but evil spirits, like evil men, do not believe it, although it has been often proved to them experimentally, as will be shown, by the divine mercy of the Lord, in a future part of this work. Since therefore the state of man is such, that not a single evil or falsity can be so entirely separated as to be completely abolished, because his proper life consists in the evil and the false, the Lord, out of his divine mercy, whilst regenerating man, so overcomes his evils and falses by temptations, that they appear as it were dead, although they are not really so, being only subdued, to prevent their resisting the goods and truths which are from the Lord. At the same time also, the Lord, by means of temptations, confers on man a new faculty of receiving goods and truths, by gifting him with ideas and affec-

869. **Verse 8.** *And he sent forth a dove from himself to see if the waters were abated from off the faces of the ground.* By a dove, the truths and goods of faith in one about to be regenerated are denoted. From the words *earth* and *ground alone*, their signification in the **internal sense** <note>In this context, the "internal sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning hidden beneath the literal words of the Bible.</note> may be seen, not only here, but in all other parts of **the Word** <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note>. By *ground*, in a universal sense, is meant the church, and hence, as a consequence, the man of the church also; for, as has been previously stated, every individual man of the church is himself a church.

873\. Verse 9. *And the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot; and she returned to him into the ark, because the waters were on the faces of the whole earth: and he put forth his hand and took her and pulled her in unto himself into the ark.* By the *dove’s finding no rest for the sole of her foot*, is signified that nothing of the good and truth of faith could as yet take root; and by her *returning to him into the ark*, the appearance of goodness and truth as the offspring of faith with him. *Because the waters were on the faces of the whole earth*, signifies that falsities still overflowed; *his putting forth his hand* represents his own ability; and *his taking her, and pulling her in unto himself into the ark*, that he did what was good and thought what was true of himself.

874\. Here is described the first state of **regeneration** <note>The process of being spiritually "reborn" or transformed by divine influence.</note> of the man of this church after temptation, one which is common to all who become regenerate, in which they imagine they do good and think what is true from themselves, the Lord permitting them so to believe in consequence of the extreme obscurity of their perceptions. In reality, however, all the good they do, and all the truth they think, whilst influenced by such a false idea, is not the good and truth of faith; for whatsoever a man brings forth from himself cannot be good, since it proceeds from an impure and unclean fountain, whence no good can ever emanate. In such a state men think of their own merit and righteousness, and some are even led to despise others in comparison with themselves, as the Lord teaches (Luke xviii. 9—14), whilst others fall into other errors and evils; for, in this state, a man’s own lusts commingle themselves with what he thinks and does, which thus appears outwardly as if it were good, when yet within it is defiled; wherefore the good which he then does is not the good of faith. It is similar with regard to the truth which he thinks; so that although it may be most true, whilst he remains in <term>proprium<note>original: "proprium" — a Latin term referring to a person's "selfhood" or "own-ness"; the inherent nature of a human being which, without divine influence, is considered to be focused only on the self.</note></term>, being in itself indeed a truth of faith, still the good of faith is not in it; and all truth, in order that it may be the truth of faith, ought to have in it the good of faith from the Lord, when it first becomes both good and true.

875\. By the *dove’s finding no rest for the sole of her foot*, is meant that nothing of the good and truth of faith could as yet take root, as is evident from a *dove’s* signifying the truth of faith, and from *rest for the sole of the foot*, meaning to take root. # 873 — 876.] GENESIS. 323

overflow; but, how this happened cannot be known, unless the mode in which the **regeneration** <note>The process of being spiritually "reborn" or transformed by divine influence.</note> of the spiritual man is effected be first understood. With this man, the **knowledges of faith** <note>The specific facts, teachings, and truths learned from sacred texts.</note> collected from the Word of the Lord, or from doctrines derived from it—which the **Ancient Church** <note>According to this text, the "Ancient Church" was a spiritual era that followed the "Most Ancient Church"; it relied on learning truth rather than direct intuition.</note> had from what was revealed to the **Most Ancient Church**—required to be implanted in the memory, so that his intellectual mind might be instructed by them.

Now, as long as **falsities** <note>In this context, falsities are incorrect beliefs or distorted spiritual perceptions that "flood" the mind.</note> overflow, it is impossible for the truths of faith to take root, no matter how they are sown; they remain only on the surface or in the memory. Nor *can the ground* be fitted to receive them until, as was observed before, the falsities are so entirely cleared away that they no longer appear. Real *ground* is prepared in the intellectual mind of this man, and when it is ready, the good of **charity** <note>Love in action; the selfless desire to do good for others.</note> is introduced into it by the Lord. From this, a **conscience** is formed, from which the man afterwards acts—or rather, it is the means by which the Lord produces the good and truth of faith.

In this way, the Lord distinguishes the intellectual things of this man from those that belong to his **will** <note>The "will" represents the seat of a person's core desires and intentions, which in this theology are considered naturally corrupted in modern humans.</note>, so that they are in no way united. For if they were united, the man would necessarily perish forever. In the man of the **Most Ancient Church**, as with the celestial angels, the things of the will and the things of the intellect made a single whole. However, neither with the man of this church, nor with the spiritual man, are they united, even though it may seem as if the good of charity he performs comes from his own will. This is merely an appearance and a fallacy.

All the good of charity that he does belongs to the Lord alone, acting not through the man's will, but through his conscience. If the Lord were to leave him to act from his own will in the slightest degree, he would do evil instead of good, driven by motives of hatred, revenge, and cruelty. The same applies to the truth that the spiritual man thinks and speaks; if it did not come from conscience—and thus from the good of the Lord—he could no more think or speak what is true than the **diabolical crew** <note>A reference to malevolent spirits who attempt to deceive by appearing virtuous.</note> can when they **disguise themselves as angels of light** <note>original: "feign themselves angels of light"; an allusion to the biblical warning in 2 Corinthians 11:14.</note>, as is clearly seen in the **other life** <note>The spiritual world or the afterlife.</note>. 

This explains the method of regeneration and the nature of the spiritual man’s rebirth: it consists of a separation of the **intellectual principle** from the **will principle** by means of the conscience, which the Lord forms in the understanding. Because of this conscience, whatever the man does seems to come from his own will, even though it is actually from the Lord.

876\. By the dove **returning to him in the ark**, the text represents the appearance of goodness and truth as the results of faith within him, as is clear from what has been said and what follows. To *return to the ark* does *not*, in the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the scripture as opposed to the literal story.</note>, signify *freedom*. Instead, freedom is represented by being sent out from the ark and *not* returning. This is clear from verse 12, where it says that *he sent forth the dove, and she returned not again unto him any more*; and also from verses 15 and 16.

## GENESIS [Chapter 8]

16, in which it is stated, that, *Noah was commanded to go forth of the ark*; and from verse 18, where it is said, that *he went forth*. The *ark* signifies his state before **regeneration** <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or transformed by Divine influence.</note>; and, whilst in that state, he was in captivity and prison, blocked up on all sides by evils and **falses** <note>Distorted or incorrect spiritual beliefs.</note>, or by the waters of the flood: wherefore by *the dove’s* returning to him into the ark, is signified that *goodness and truth*, understood by *the dove* came back again to him. Whatever good a man supposes he does of himself, this returns to him, because he regards himself, or does it that it may be seen before the world, or in the sight of angels, or that he may merit heaven, or be the greatest in heaven, such motives being in the **selfhood** <note>original: "proprium"—the human ego or the sense of self that believes it acts independently of God.</note> and in every idea thereof, although it appears in its external form to be the good and truth of faith. The genuine good and truth of faith is inwardly good and true, entering by **spiritual flow** <note>original: "influx"—the process by which life and truth from God enter the human mind.</note> from the inmost, that is, through the most interior principles of man from the Lord: but when it is grounded in **selfhood** <note>original: "proprium"</note>, or merit, then the interiors are defiled and the exteriors appear clean; like a filthy harlot, with a beautiful countenance; or an **Ethiopian**, or rather, an **Egyptian mummy**, clad in a white garment.

877. *Waters on the faces of the earth* signify falsities were still overflowing, as is manifest from the signification of the *waters of a flood*, being falsities, as was shown above; and consequently from the very words themselves.

878. *To put forth his hand* represents his own ability, and *taking her, and pulling her in to himself into the ark*, that he did what was good, and thought what was true, from himself, as is demonstrated from the signification of the hand, as denoting power, consequently here, his own proper power; for *to put forth the hand, take the dove, and pull her in unto himself*, is to apply and attribute to himself the truth, understood by *the dove*. By the hand is signified ability, power, and confidence, as is demonstrable from many passages in the **Word** <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note>; as from Isaiah: “*I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria,—for he saith, by the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent,*” (x. 12, 13;) where *hand* manifestly denotes man’s proper power, to which he attributes what he thinks and does, and which is the cause of his being punished. Again, in the same prophet: “*He [Moab] shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth [his hands] to swim; and he shall bring down their pride, together with the spoils of their hands,*” (xxv. 11;) where the hand is self-ability, grounded in inordinate self-consequence, thus in pride. Again, “*Their inhabitants were short of hand, they were dismayed and confounded,*” (xxxvii. 27:) to *be short of hand* is to be powerless. Again: “*Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?*” (xlv. 9:) to have no hands signifies to have no ability.

So in Ezekiel: “The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled,” (vii. 27;) where hands denote powers. In Micah: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds; when the morning is light they practise it, because their hand is their god,” (ii. 1;) the *hand* here represents self-ability, in which they confide as in their god. So in Zechariah: “Woe to the idol shepherd that forsaketh the flock! the sword shall be upon his *arm*, and upon the eye of his right hand; his *arm* shall be clean dried up, and the eye of his right hand shall be utterly darkened,” (xi. 17.) Since *hands* typify power, therefore man’s evils and **falses** <note>Spiritual errors or distorted beliefs that lead one away from truth.</note> are in all parts of the Word called *works of their hands*; evils being from the **selfhood** <note>original: "proprium"—the natural human ego or the sense of self that feels independent of Divine influence.</note> of his will, and falses from that of his understanding. That they actually proceed thence, is sufficiently evident from man’s **selfhood** <note>original: "proprium"</note> being nothing but evil and the false, as may be seen above, n. 39, 41, 141, 150, 154, 210, 215. As in a general sense *hands* denote power, therefore they are often in the Word attributed to Jehovah or the Lord; and in that case by *hands*, in the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and historical accounts.</note>, is understood **omnipotence** <note>The quality of having unlimited or very great power, specifically the all-encompassing power of God.</note>; as in Isaiah: 

> “Jehovah, thy *hand* is lifted up,” (xxvi. 11;) 

referring to the divine ability. Again, in the same prophet: 

> “Jehovah shall stretch out his *hand*, all are consumed,” (xxxi. 3;) 

speaking of the divine power. Again: 

> “Concerning the work of my *hands* command ye me;—my hands have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded,” (xlv. 11, 12;) 

signifying divine power. The **regenerate** <note>Those who have undergone a spiritual rebirth or transformation of character.</note> are frequently called, in the Word, “*the work of the hands of Jehovah*.” Again: 

> “My hand hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my *right hand* hath spanned the heavens,” (xlviii. 13;) 

where *hand* and *right hand* denote omnipotence. Again: 

> “Is my *hand* shortened at all that it cannot redeem, or have I no power to deliver?” (l. 2;) 

alluding to the divine power. So in Jeremiah: 

> “Thou hast brought forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched-out *arm*,” (xxxii. 21;) 

signifying divine power, which, at verse 17, is called *power*, although in this verse *hand*. It is frequently said, that by “a strong hand, and a stretched-out arm,” the people of Israel were brought forth out of Egypt. In Ezekiel:

"*Moses stretched forth his hand—and there was a thick darkness,*" (Exod. x. 22.) "*Moses stretched out his hand over the [Red] sea, and the Lord—made the sea dry,*" (Exod. xiv. 21.) However, because the raising and extending of the hand represented divine power, it was established as a <term>representative</term> <note>In this context, a "representative" is a physical act or object that serves as a visible symbol for a spiritual reality, allowing that spiritual influence to act on the material world.</note> in the <term>Jewish Church</term> <note>This term refers to the ancient Israelite religious system, which the author describes as being built upon symbolic rituals and external laws.</note>. 

A similar case was the representation of <term>Joshua</term>'s stretching out his spear, about which it is written, "*Jehovah said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward <term>Ai</term>, for I will give it into thy hand. From these examples, the nature of "representatives"—which formed the <term>externals</term> <note>The outward rituals and literal histories of the Bible, as distinguished from their deeper spiritual meanings.</note> of the Jewish Church—becomes clear. It can be seen that the <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible, viewed here as a sacred text containing hidden layers of divine truth.</note> contains accounts which, in their literal sense, do not seem to represent the Lord or his kingdom (such as the stretching out of a hand). The true meaning of these events cannot be understood as long as the mind stays only on the historical stories of the literal text. 

This fact also shows how the Jews lost the true understanding of the <term>Word</term> and their own religious rites when they focused entirely on outward ceremonies. They wrongly attributed power to the *rod of Moses* and the *spear of Joshua*, which actually had no more power than any other piece of wood. However, because these objects represented the Lord's <term>Omnipotence</term> <note>The all-encompassing, infinite power of God.</note>—and because this symbolic meaning was recognized in heaven when they stretched out their hands or rods by command—miracles and signs were performed through them. 

The same principle applies to what is written about <term>Moses</term> on the hilltop: when he lifted his hands, Joshua’s army won, but when he lowered them, the enemy won; therefore, "*they stayed up his hands,*" (Exod. xvii. 9, 11, 12.) This is also true of the ritual of laying on of hands to consecrate someone, such as when the people did this to the Levites (Numb. viii. 9, 10, 12), or when Moses appointed Joshua as his successor (Numb. xxvii. 18, 23) to confer power. This is the origin of modern ceremonies of <term>inauguration</term> <note>The formal act of ordaining or placing someone into a sacred office.</note> and <term>benediction</term> <note>A formal blessing.</note> through the <term>imposition of hands</term> <note>The ritual of placing hands on a person's head to symbolize the transfer of authority or the bestowing of a blessing.</note>.

The third state is described by *the dove's not returning*, by *Noah's removing the covering of the ark*, and, lastly, by *his going forth of the ark*, because *the faces of the ground were dry, and the earth was dried*.

891. From this, it follows that the phrase *the dove returned not again unto him any more* signifies a state of freedom. This is also clear because the dove (representing the truth of faith), along with the other birds, animals, and Noah himself, were no longer kept inside the ark because of the floodwaters. As long as Noah remained in the ark, he was in a state of slavery, or captivity and imprisonment, being tossed about by the waters of the flood—which represent <term>falsities</term> <note>In this context, "falsities" or "falses" are the deceptive thoughts and mistaken beliefs that overwhelm a person’s mind during times of spiritual trial.</note>. This state of imprisonment and temptation was described in the previous chapter, where the waters increased and lifted the ark, and then prevailed as the ark drifted on the surface of the deep. His state of liberty is described in the upcoming verses (15–18) of this chapter. This freedom is shown not only by *Noah going out of the ark*, but also by everyone with him leaving as well. This process begins with the departure of the dove—that is, the truth of faith that grows out of goodness. All true freedom comes from the "good of faith," which is essentially the love of what is good.

892. When a person becomes <term>regenerate</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of spiritual rebirth or "re-making," where a person moves from being driven by selfish impulses to being guided by divine love and truth.</note>, they enter a state of liberty for the first time. Before this, they were in slavery. A person is a slave as long as they are ruled by <term>cupidities</term> <note>original: "cupiditates" — these are selfish cravings, lusts, or intense worldly desires that pull a person away from spiritual health.</note> and falsities. They are only at liberty when governed by an affection for what is good and true. 

A person never realizes they are in a state of servitude as long as they remain in it; they only begin to recognize it when they first enter a state of liberty. While someone is a slave—meaning, as long as selfish cravings and false ideas rule them—they actually imagine themselves to be free. This is a total delusion. Because they are carried away by the delight of their cravings and the pleasures they get from them—which are the things they love—the experience feels agreeable, and so they think they are free. 

Anyone who is guided by a specific love or passion thinks they are free as long as they follow where it leads. But the truth is, at those times, such a person is swept along by a torrent of <term>diabolical spirits</term> who hurry them away. The person imagines this is the highest form of liberty. They believe that if they were deprived of these desires, their life would be miserable and hardly worth living. They fall into this belief not just because they don't know any other kind of life, but also because of a common misconception: they have been told that no one can enter heaven except through misery, poverty, and giving up all pleasure. This is a false idea. I have learned through much experience—which, by the Lord's mercy, I will share later—that this is not the case. A person never enters a true state of liberty, where they are guided by the love of goodness and truth from the Lord, until they have undergone regeneration. It is only in this state that they are finally able to know and perceive...

## 893. Verse 13. 

*And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the beginning, in the first of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth; and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and he saw, and behold the faces of the ground were dry.* 

By *its coming to pass in the six hundredth and first year*, is signified the **ultimate terminus** <term>ultimate terminus: the final boundary or end point of a specific spiritual stage</term>, and by *in the beginning, in the first of the month*, the first terminus <note>The "first terminus" refers to the starting point of a new spiritual state.</note>. *The waters being dried up from off the earth*, signifies that **falsities** did not then appear; *Noah's removing the covering of the ark, and seeing*, represents the light of the truths of faith, which he acknowledged and believed in, when falses had been removed; and *the faces of the ground being dried*, signifies **regeneration** <note>Regeneration is the process of being spiritually reborn or "re-made" by the Lord.</note>.

By *it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year* is signified the **ultimate terminus**, as is evident from the signification of *six hundred* given in the preceding chapter (verse 6, n. 737), as denoting a beginning. In that particular passage, it meant the beginning of a temptation; here, the termination of that temptation is designated by the same number after an entire year had passed. Therefore, it occurred at the end of a year, which is why it is added that it happened *in the beginning, in the first of the month*, denoting the first boundary of a new state. Every entire period is marked in the Word <note>Swedenborg refers to the Bible as "the Word."</note> either by *a day, a week, a month, or a year*, even although the actual duration of that period might be *a hundred or a thousand years*. This is similar to the days mentioned in the first chapter of Genesis, which denote periods of the **regeneration** of the man of the **Most Ancient Church** <term>Most Ancient Church: Swedenborg’s term for the very first era of humanity, which he describes as having a direct, celestial perception of God.</term>. *A day* and *a year* have no other signification in the **internal sense** <term>internal sense: the hidden, spiritual meaning within the literal stories of the Bible</term> than...

# GENESIS. [CHAPTER 8.]

898. **"And behold, the faces of the ground were dry,"** signifies **regeneration** <note>In this theology, "regeneration" is the process of being spiritually reborn or transformed from a worldly person into a heavenly one.</note>, as is proved by the meaning of **"ground,"** which has been explained many times before as representing the person who belongs to the church. The **"faces of the ground"** are said to be **"dry"** when falsities <note>In this context, "falsities" are incorrect beliefs or distorted perspectives that cloud spiritual understanding.</note> are no longer visible.

899. Verse 14. **"In the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dried."** The **"second month"** represents every state that comes before regeneration; the **"seven and twentieth day"** represents what is holy; and the **"earth being dried"** signifies that the person was now regenerate. These words mark the end of everything that happened before and the beginning of what follows.

900. The **"second month"** signifies every state prior to regeneration, which is clear from the meaning of the number **"two"** in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>. **"Two"** means the same as **"six,"** which represents the struggle and labor that must happen before a person is reborn; therefore, in this passage, it represents every state before a person’s regeneration. Periods of time—whether long or short—are usually divided in the Word into **"threes"** or **"sevens,"** and are called days, weeks, months, years, or ages. The numbers **"three"** and **"seven"** are holy, while **"two"** and **"six,"** which come before them, are not holy, but are instead **profane** <note>The term "profane" here does not mean "irreverent" in the modern sense, but rather "common" or "worldly," referring to the state of struggle before something is made sacred.</note> by comparison, as was shown previously in section 720. **"Three"** and **"seven"** are also considered sacred and cannot be changed because they both refer to the **last judgment** <note>The "last judgment" is described here not just as an end-of-the-world event, but as a personal spiritual milestone—the moment the Lord "arrives" in a person's heart or the moment of death.</note>, which is said to happen on the **"third"** or **"seventh"** day. The last judgment for every individual is the coming of the Lord, both in a general and a specific sense. Thus, the Lord’s arrival in the world was the last judgment; it will be the last judgment when He comes again in glory; it is the last judgment when He comes to each person individually; and it is also the last judgment for everyone when they die. This last judgment is the **"third"** and the **"seventh"** day, which is sacred to those who have lived well, but the opposite for those who have lived poorly. Therefore, these days are used to describe both those who are condemned to death and those who are granted life. Consequently, they signify what is not holy for those who are condemned, and what is holy for those who are granted life. The numbers **"two"** or **"six,"** which come before, refer generally to the entire state that came before. This, then, is the meaning of the numbers **"two"** and **"six,"** which is specifically defined by the subject they are describing, as can be seen even more clearly from what follows regarding the number **"twenty-seven."**

901. The **"seven and twentieth day"** denotes what is holy. This can be proven by the fact that it is the result of the number **"three"** multiplied by itself twice; for three multiplied by itself is **"nine,"** and nine multiplied by three is **"twenty-seven,"** making **"three"** the ruling number. In this way, the **Most Ancient people** <note>The "Most Ancient people" refers to the earliest, most spiritually pure human civilization described in these writings, who lived before the time of the Flood and understood the world through symbols.</note> calculated their numbers, understanding them as representing spiritual things.

only. That *three* has the same meaning as *seven*, is evident from what was just now observed, and the mystical reason of it is, that the Lord rose again on the *third* day, for the Lord's resurrection includes whatever is holy, and the resurrection of all. <note>The author links the holiness of the number three to the Resurrection, suggesting that "three" symbolizes a completed process or a new beginning in a holy state.</note> Hence in the Jewish church this number was made representative <note>A "representative" is an outward ritual or object that serves as a physical symbol for a deeper spiritual reality.</note>, and is in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> holy, as it is also in heaven, where there are no numbers, but instead of *three* and *seven* the general holy idea of the Lord's resurrection and advent. <note>In this theological framework, angels do not think in quantities but in the spiritual qualities those numbers represent.</note> That *three* and *seven* represent what is sacred, is plain from the following passages in the Word:

"He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean *seven days*. He shall purify himself with it on the *third day*, and on the *seventh day* he shall be clean; but if he purify not himself the *third day*, then the *seventh day* he shall not be clean.—Whosoever toucheth one that is slain with a sword—or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean *seven days*.—And a clean [person] shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the *third day*, and on the *seventh day*; and on the *seventh day* he shall purify himself and wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at even," (Numbers 19:11, 12, 16, 19.)

These things are representative, or these externals signify something internal, as is very evident; as that a *person should be unclean who touched a dead body, one slain with a sword, the bone of a man, or a grave*, all of which, in the *internal sense* <note>The "internal sense" is the hidden spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</note>, denote what are properly man's own <note>The phrase "properly man's own" (often called the *proprium*) refers to the human ego or self-centered nature, which the author considers spiritually "dead" or "profane" when separated from God.</note>, which are dead and profane; thus the *third* and the *seventh day* are also representative, signifying what is holy, because on them the *unclean were purified, and thereby made clean*. In like manner it is written of those who returned from the battle against the Midianites: "Abide ye without the camp *seven days*, whosoever hath killed a soul, and whosoever hath touched any slain; purify yourselves—on the *third day*, and on the *seventh day*," (Numbers 31:19.)

If this were a mere ritual only, the *third* and *seventh* days not representing and signifying what is holy, or expiation <note>Expiation refers to the act of making amends or being cleansed from spiritual wrongdoing.</note>, it would be like something dead, and destitute of motive, or as a cause without an end, or as a something separate from its cause, and this from its end, consequently as in no degree divine. That the *third day* was representative, and thus significative of what is holy, appears evidently from the coming of the Lord on Mount Sinai, concerning which it is written, "Jehovah said unto Moses, Go unto the people, and sanctify them to-day and to-morrow, and let them wash their clothes, and be ready against the *third day*; for on the *third day* Jehovah will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai," (Exodus 19:10, 11, also 15, 16.) The presence of the Lord with man first exists when he loves his neighbor; for the Lord is in love, and so far as man is in love the Lord is present with him; and in the degree in which the Lord is present, he speaks with man. ->### 918--920. GENESIS.<-

This communication was the **perception** <note>Perception: An intuitive, immediate understanding of spiritual truth that comes directly from the heart, rather than through logic or study.</note> of which so much has been said above; and being thus angelic, they were also **internal men** <note>Internal men: People whose primary focus and awareness are centered on spiritual and heavenly realities rather than just physical or material ones.</note>; sensible, indeed, of the external objects relating to their bodies and the world, but not caring for them; perceiving in all the objects of sense something divine and celestial. Thus, for example, when looking upon any high mountain, they were impressed with no idea of it as a mountain, but with a sense of its height, and from this they had a perception of heaven and the Lord. Hence it came to pass that the Lord was said to dwell on high, and he himself was called the Highest and Most Exalted, and the worship of the Lord was subsequently solemnized on mountains. 

It was similar in other instances: thus, when they recognized the presence of morning, they had no idea of it as the commencing day, but as the celestial morning, the day-dawn in the mind; hence the Lord was called the *Morning*, the *East* <note>original: *Oriens*</note>, and the *Day-spring* <note>original: *Aurora*</note>. In like manner, when they beheld a tree, with its fruit and leaves, they did not attend to them, but saw in them as it were man represented, the *fruit* denoting his love and charity, and the *leaves* his faith; hence also the man of the church was not only compared to a tree and a paradise, and the things in man to *fruit* and *leaves*, but they were likewise so denominated. 

Such are those who are in celestial and angelic ideas. Every one may perceive the fact, that all particular impressions—those derived from the objects of the senses, such as affect the eye or the ear—have relation to one's common prevailing ideas. This relation is so strong that the objects themselves are not even noticed, except so far as they coincide with the general idea. Thus if the mind be joyful, whatever is heard or seen appears smiling and happy; but if it be affected with sorrow, then whatever is heard or seen appears sad and painful. So also it is in other instances; for the general affection flowing into **particulars** <note>original: *singulars*; the specific, individual details of a person's life or thoughts.</note> modifies them into accordance with itself, while contrary impressions are ignored, as though they were either absent or did not exist. 

This was the state of the man of the **Most Ancient Church** <note>Most Ancient Church: A term for the earliest era of humanity (symbolized by Adam), described here as having a natural, direct connection to spiritual realities.</note>: whatever he saw with his eyes gave rise to some celestial idea, and thus with him all things, both in general and in particular, were filled with life. Hence it may appear that his divine worship was exclusively internal, and in no respect external. When, however, the church was on the decline—as with his posterity—and when their perception or communication with heaven began to cease, then another state of things commenced. Men no longer perceived from the objects of sense what was celestial, but what was worldly, and this in proportion to the diminution of their perception; until at length, in the last posterity immediately preceding the flood, they recognized nothing in sensible objects but what was worldly, corporeal, and terrestrial. ### 925.
**Jehovah's smelling an odor of rest** means that worship derived from that state was *grateful* to the Lord, and that it was worship from <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is the active love for one's neighbor and the primary motivation for good actions.</note> and the faith of charity, signified by a *whole burnt-offering*, as was stated in the verse immediately preceding. It is said *he smelled an odor of rest from the burnt-offerings* (Exodus 29:18, 25, 41; Leviticus 1:9, 13, 17; 23:13, 18; Numbers 28:6, 8, 13; 29:2, 6, 8, 13, 36; and from other sacrifices, Leviticus 2:2, 9; 6:8—15; 8:21, 28; Numbers 15:3, 7, 10, 14); which are said to be *made by fire*, for *an odor of rest to Jehovah*, to denote that they proceeded from love and charity; *fire*, in the Word, and what is kindled with *fire*, when predicated of the Lord, signifies love. *Bread* has a similar signification, wherefore also representative worship by whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices is called *the bread of the offering made by fire unto Jehovah, for an odor of rest* (Leviticus 3:11, 16). 

That *an odor* signifies what is grateful and acceptable—and thus, in the <term>Jewish Church</term> <note>The religious system of the Old Testament based on symbolic rituals and representative acts.</note>, was also representative of what is grateful and is attributed to Jehovah, or the Lord—is because the good of charity and the truth of faith grounded in charity correspond to delightful and sweet *odors*. The existence and nature of this <term>correspondence</term> <note>The spiritual law that natural things in the world reflect and act in unison with spiritual realities.</note> are proved by the *spheres* in the heavens of spirits and angels. In heaven there are spheres of love and of faith which are manifestly perceived. They are of such a nature that when a good spirit or angel, or a society of good spirits or angels, approaches, their quality as to love and faith is instantly perceived whenever it seems good to the Lord. This can be felt even from a distance, although more particularly as they become present. This may appear incredible, but it is nonetheless most true, for such is the communication and perception which prevail in the next life; and hence, when it so pleases the Lord, there is no necessity for much examination to discover the quality of a soul or spirit, since this may be known the instant of its approach. To these spiritual spheres, the odors of the world correspond, as is evident from the fact that the spheres of...

## 929.
Hence then it appears that by *neither will I again smite every thing living, as I have done*, is meant that man would be no longer capable of so destroying himself; for when man is <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of spiritual transformation or "regeneration."</note>, he is then withheld from the evil and the false which are with him, and in this state perceives no other but that he does what is good and thinks what is true. This is, however, a mere appearance or fallacy, owing to his being so powerfully restrained, and thus kept from self-destruction; for were the hold on him at all remitted, and he left to himself, he would rush headlong into evil and falsity.

## 930.
*Verse* 22. *For during all the days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, shall not cease.* 

For *during all the days of the earth*, signifies in all time; *seed-time and harvest* the man about to be regenerated, and the church thence derived; and *cold and heat*, the state of the regenerate man, as to the reception of faith and <term>charity</term> <note>Charity here refers to active love and goodwill toward others.</note>, *cold* denoting the absence, and *heat* the presence, of faith and charity. *Summer and winter* signify the state of the regenerate man as to his new <term>voluntary things</term> <note>This refers to the "will" (the Latin "voluntarius")—the seat of human desires and intentions.</note>—the changes of which resemble those of summer and winter—*day and night*, the state of the same, that is, of the regenerate man, as to intellectual things, the mutations of which are similar to those of *day and night*; *shall not cease*, means that this shall be the case for ever.

## 931.
*For during all the days of the earth*, means all time, as is evident from the signification of a *day*, which represents time (as seen in sections 23, 487, 488, 493); and thus in the present passage *the days of the earth* are so long as there is earth, or inhabitant upon it. The earth begins to cease to be inhabited when there is no longer any church; for when this occurs there is no longer any communication existing between man and heaven, on the cessation of which every inhabitant perishes. The church, as was observed, is like the heart and lungs in man, and so long as these continue sound, man has life. The same holds true of the church in reference to the <term>Greatest Man</term> <note>original: "Maximus Homo." This is a foundational concept in this system of thought, suggesting that the entire heaven is organized in the form of a single human being, with the Church acting as its vital organs.</note>, which is the universal heaven; wherefore it is here said, *during all the days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease*. For the last judgment of every "church" occurs when it is <term>vastated</term> <note>A term meaning "emptied" or "devastated" of all true faith and love.</note>, or when there is no longer any faith left within it. 

It was the last judgment of the *Most Ancient Church* <note>The earliest era of humanity described symbolically in the beginning of Genesis.</note> when it *perished* among the generation immediately preceding the flood. It was the last judgment of the *Jewish Church* when the Lord came into the world, and there will also be a last judgment when He shall come again in glory. This is not because the earth and the universe will then perish, but because the church will then reach its end. 

Under these circumstances, a new church is always raised up by the Lord—just as the Ancient Church was raised at the time of the flood, and the early church of the gentiles at the time of the Lord's first coming. This will also occur when the Lord comes again in glory, which is what is meant by the formation of a "new heaven and a new earth."<gloss>Notably, this work was first published in Latin in 1749; the author describes the spiritual event of the Last Judgment as occurring later, in 1757.</gloss> 

The same process takes place with every <term>regenerate person</term> <note>Someone undergoing a spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note> who becomes a member of the church, or a "church" in miniature. Their <term>internal man</term> <note>The inner, spiritual part of a person's mind.</note>, when it is re-created, is called a "new heaven," and their <term>external man</term> <note>The outer, natural part of a person's mind and behavior.</note> is called a "new earth." Furthermore, the last judgment for each individual is the time of their death; for then they are judged according to the things done in the body, either to spiritual death or to eternal life. That nothing else is meant by the expressions *consummation of the age*, *the end of days*, and *the last judgment*—and consequently that they do not mean the destruction of the visible world—is very clear from the Lord's words in Luke:

> "In that *night* there shall be two [men] in one bed, the one shall be *taken* and the other *left*. Two [women] shall be grinding together, the one shall be *taken* and the other *left*. Two [men] shall be in the field, the one shall be *taken* and the other *left.*" (Luke 17:34–36)

Here the "last time" is called *night*, because there is no faith due to the absence of love (charity). And since some are said to be "left" behind, it is plain that the physical world *will not then be destroyed*.

The Word of the Lord itself, and its influence toward spiritual growth, is also compared to a *harvest*. Indeed, this is obvious to everyone, as these metaphors are familiar in common language. This passage deals generally with *every* person, informing us that "seed" (spiritual truth) will never cease to be sown in them by the Lord, whether they are within or *outside* the formal church—that is, whether they have been made acquainted with the Word of the Lord or not. This occurs to every one during his <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth, where a person is gradually changed from being self-centered to being led by God.</note>, and indeed continues to occur with him so long as he is undergoing this process; for man cannot be otherwise regenerated—that is, from being dead be made alive—because, as has been previously stated, his will is altogether corrupt, and thus separated from the new will which he receives from the Lord, and which is of the Lord, and not of man. Hence then it may be seen what is here signified by *cold* and *heat*. That such is the fact, every regenerate person may know experimentally, for whilst he is under the influence of corporeal and worldly things, he is absent and remote from internal things, so that he not only thinks nothing about them, but even feels in himself as it were *cold* towards them; when, however, things corporeal and worldly are quiescent, then he is in faith and charity. It may also be known by experience that these states are alternate; for when corporeal and worldly thoughts begin to overflow, and are desirous to gain the dominion, then the regenerate person comes into straitness and temptations, until he is reduced to such a state, that the external man becomes obsequious to the internal, which never occurs until it is quiescent, and as it were annihilated. The last posterity of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The earliest era of humanity described in Genesis; in this context, they represent a state where the heart and mind were inseparable.</note> could not be regenerated, because, as was observed, their intellectual and voluntary principles constituted one mind, in consequence of which intellectual things could not be separated from those of the will, so that they might be alternately under the influence of celestial and spiritual, and of corporeal and worldly thoughts. Thus with them there prevailed a perpetual *cold* as to celestial things, and a continual *heat* as to their <term>cupidities</term> <note>Selfish or worldly desires and lusts.</note>, so that no alternation could possibly take place.

So in Daniel: "The <term>Ancient of Days</term> <note>A title for God used in the Book of Daniel, representing His eternal nature.</note> did sit—his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as *burning fire*. A fiery stream issued and came forth before him; thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him," (7:9, 10:) where *fire* denotes the Lord's love. 

In Zechariah: "For I, saith Jehovah, will be unto her a wall of *fire* round about," (2:5;) speaking of the New Jerusalem. So in David: "Who maketh his angels spirits, his ministers a *flaming fire*," (Psalm 104:4;) a *flaming fire* denotes the <term>celestial-spiritual principle</term> <note>The state where a person's life is guided by truth that is deeply rooted in love.</note>. Inasmuch as *fire* signified love, it was also made a representative of the Lord, as appears from the *fire* on the altar of the whole burnt-offering, which represented the mercy of the Lord, and of which it is said, "it shall not be put out," (Leviticus 6:12, 13.) Therefore before Aaron entered into the <term>mercy-seat</term> <note>The gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant, representing the presence of God and the place of atonement.</note>, he was directed to offer incense, taking *fire* from off the altar of the <term>whole burnt-offering</term> <note>original: "holocaust"; an ancient sacrifice where the entire animal was consumed by fire as a symbol of total devotion.</note>, (Leviticus 16:12—14;) and in order to show that such worship was acceptable to the Lord, *fire* was sent down from heaven, and consumed the holocaust, (Leviticus 9:24.) By *fire* also in the Word is signified self-love and the lust thereof, with which heavenly love cannot agree, wherefore also the two sons of Aaron were consumed by *fire*, because they burnt incense with *strange fire*, (Leviticus 10:1, 2;) *strange fire* being all self-love and the love of the world, and every lust arising from them. Heavenly love, moreover, appears no other to the wicked than

935. *And summer and winter signify* the state of the <term>regenerate<note>In this context, "regenerate" refers to a person who has undergone a spiritual rebirth or internal transformation to live a life of faith and charity.</note></term> man as to the renewed <insert>affections</insert> of his will, the changes of which resemble those of *summer and winter*, as is evident from what has been said respecting *cold and heat*. The mutations of those about to be regenerated are likened to *cold and heat*, but the alternations of such as are regenerate to *summer and winter*. That the former passage treated of a person about to be regenerated, and the present relates to one already regenerated, may be seen from this consideration, that in the former instance *cold* is first named, and then *heat*, whereas here *summer* is first mentioned, and afterwards *winter*. The reason is, that the man who is being regenerated commences in a state of *coldness*, or of no faith and charity, but when he is regenerated then he begins from charity. That the regenerate man undergoes changes from states of no charity to those of some charity, may appear clearly from this, that every one, even the regenerate, is nothing but evil, and that all good is of the Lord alone, consequently he must necessarily undergo changes, being at one time as it were in *summer*, or in charity, and at another in *winter*, or in no charity. These alternations are for this end, that man may be more and more perfected, and thus rendered more and more happy. Similar mutations take place in the regenerate man, not only during his life in the body but also when he comes into the other world, for without changes resembling as it were those of *summer and winter* as to the will, and of *day and night* as to the understanding, he can never be perfected and rendered happier. These changes, however, in another life are like those of *summer and winter* in the temperate zones, and of *day and night* in the season of spring. These states are also described in the prophets by the terms *summer and winter* and *day and night*; as in Zechariah: "And it shall be in that day, living waters shall go out from Jerusalem, part of them towards the eastern sea, and part of them towards the hinder sea; in summer and in winter shall it be" (14:8); speaking of the <term>New Jerusalem<note>A symbolic term for a new spiritual era or the "Lord's kingdom," characterized by a direct connection with the divine.</note></term>, or the Lord’s kingdom in heaven and on earth, or of the states of both, called *summer and winter*. So in David: "The day is thine, the night also is thine, thou hast prepared the light and the sun. Thou hast set all the borders of the earth; thou hast made summer and winter" (Psalm 74:16, 17).

936. *Day and night* signify the state of the <term>regenerate<note>A person who has undergone a spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note></term> man in regard to intellectual matters. The changes in his understanding resemble the transition between *day and night*, as evidenced by what has been stated. *Summer and winter*, because of their difference in heat and cold, are applied to matters of the will (the heart), as they function in a similar way. *Day and night*, however, are used for the intellect because it undergoes variations comparable to light and darkness. As this is self-evident, there is no need to prove it by quoting similar passages from the <term>Word<note>original: "Verbum"; refers to the Holy Scriptures or Bible.</note></term>.

937. From this, it is clear what the <term>Word</term> of the Lord is in its internal sense. Looking only at the literal words, it seems to speak only of *seed-time and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night*. However, all these terms contain within them <term>arcana<note>original: "arcana"; spiritual secrets or hidden deeper meanings.</note></term> of the Ancient or spiritual church. The words themselves, in their literal sense, provide a natural container for these ideas. They act as the outermost vessels for so many important heavenly <term>arcana</term> that it is impossible to describe even a ten-thousandth part of them. Angels, guided by the Lord, see the entire process of spiritual rebirth within these common words about earthly things. They see the various states of those who are being transformed, while a person reading the text might hardly notice anything at all.

Their thoughts—which greed has made dense and earthly—transform into terrifying <term>phantasies<note>Illusionary or distorted mental realities experienced in the spiritual world.</note></term>. 946. *I have conversed with spirits regarding the fact that few people are likely to believe that such and so many <term>states<gloss>In this context, "states" refers to the internal conditions, environments, or stages of existence that the soul experiences after death.</gloss></term> exist in the next life. This is because people have only a very general and obscure idea of the nature of life after death—an idea that is almost nonexistent—and they have convinced themselves of this by observing that a soul or spirit is invisible to the physical eye. Furthermore, the "learned"—even though they claim the soul or spirit exists—actually believe even less than the uneducated. This is because they stick to artificial expressions and technical terms which tend to cloud, or even extinguish, the understanding of things; they are also often immersed in selfish and worldly goals, rarely considering the public good or heaven. The spirits I spoke with were very surprised that this is the case with humans, who are so well aware that even nature, in all its kingdoms, presents so many various and wonderful complexities of which they are ignorant. For example, it would fill a volume just to list the amazing and unheard-of details of the internal structure of the human ear, which everyone admits exists. Yet, if a fact is stated about the spiritual world, from which everything in nature derives its existence, hardly anyone believes it. This is because of the pre-conceived and fixed opinion that something is nothing if it cannot be seen.*

947. *Those who are deceitful, and seek to secure every thing to themselves by deceitful contrivances, and who have confirmed themselves in such habits by their success during the life of the body, appear to themselves to dwell towards the left in a very large <term>tun<gloss>A "tun" is a very large cask or barrel for holding liquids; here it describes a confined, vat-like spiritual environment.</gloss></term>, denominated the infernal tun, over which there is a covering, and on its outside a small globe on a pyramidal base, which they actually suppose to be the universe under their inspection and government. Such amongst them as have craftily persecuted the innocent, dwell therein for ages—I was informed that some had remained there already during twenty ages <note>The author uses "ages" to denote vast, indefinite periods of spiritual time.</note>—and when they are let out, they entertain the <term>phantasy<gloss>A persistent, visionary delusion that the spirit believes is physical reality.</gloss></term>, that the universe is a kind of globe, which they walk around, and trample under foot—believing themselves to be its gods. I have sometimes seen and conversed with them concerning their phantasy, but having acquired such a nature during their abode in the world, they could not be withdrawn from it. I repeatedly perceived also, with what subtle <term>sophistry<gloss>The use of clever but false arguments, especially to deceive others.</gloss></term> they could pervert the thoughts, turning them in an instant in a different direction, and substituting others with such incredible craftiness that it could scarcely be recognized as their doing. In consequence of this, these spirits are never admitted to men, for they infuse their poison so secretly and clandestinely that it is impossible to perceive it.*

948. *There is also to the left another tun, as it appears to them, in which reside certain spirits, who in the life of the body supposed when they did evil they were doing good, and vice versâ, consequently who put good in the place of evil. Still, however, they seem to themselves to be awake, and on the recovery of their rationality they are restored to themselves, and become as other spirits.*
