The state to which those who dwell there, and who have dealt fraudulently, are at length reduced, was shown to me, as seen in the broad light of day. Their countenances are worse than those of the dead, being of a livid color and cadaverous appearance, and horribly wrinkled, in consequence of their being always tormented by anxiety.*

950. *There was a <term>phalanx<gloss>A compact body or organized group of spirits, often moving or acting in unison.</gloss></term> of spirits rising from the side of <term>Gehennah<gloss>A term for hell, derived from the Valley of Hinnom; here it refers to a specific region of spiritual punishment for those who hate the Divine.</gloss></term> to a considerable height in front, from whose sphere it was evident that they had no regard for the Lord, and despised all divine worship, for the quality of spirits may be perceived by their spheres alone on their first approach. Their speech was <term>undulatory<gloss>Moving with a wavy, vibrating motion; here it suggests a lack of spiritual stability or harmony.</gloss></term>. One of them, uttering some scandal against the Lord, was in consequence instantly cast down towards one side of Gehennah. From the front they ascended over the head, hoping to find some with whom they might join themselves for the purpose of subduing others; but they were stopped by the way, and given to understand that unless they desisted it would be to their own detriment, so they halted, and thus became visible. Their faces were black, and they had about the head a white bandage, denoting that they regard divine worship, and consequently the Word of the Lord, as dark matters—useful only to keep the vulgar under the restraints of conscience. Their residence is near Gehennah, where are flying but not poisonous dragons, whence this place is called the <term>habitation of dragons<gloss>A biblical reference to a desolate or chaotic spiritual state; here it is a specific region for those who are proud but not necessarily malicious.</gloss></term>;—as they are not, however, deceitful, their hell is less grievous. These spirits also ascribe all things to themselves and their own prudence, and boast that they are afraid of no one; but it was shown them that a mere hiss suffices to excite their alarm and put them to flight; for, a hissing noise being heard, they were so terrified that they thought all hell was rising up to fetch them away, and the heroes suddenly discovered all the fearfulness of women.*

951. *Those who whilst here have fancied themselves saints, are in the <term>lower earth<gloss>A region in the spiritual world between heaven and hell where certain spirits undergo a process of clarification or realization.</gloss></term> before the left foot, where they occasionally appear to themselves to have a shining countenance—owing to the idea of their own sanctity. At length it comes to pass, that they are seized with the greatest desire of ascending into heaven, which they suppose to be on high; this desire becomes increased, and is changed more and more into anxiety, which grows upon them immensely, until they acknowledge that they are no saints. When taken away from thence, it is given them to be sensible of their own <term>stench<gloss>In the spiritual world, one's inner character is perceived as a physical odor; here, the "stench" is the reality of their hidden selfishness.</gloss></term>, which is indeed most offensive.*

952. *A certain spirit having assumed in the world an appearance of sanctity, to gain the esteem of men, and thereby <term>merit<gloss>The belief that one can "earn" a place in heaven through outward deeds rather than inner transformation.</gloss></term> heaven, supposed himself holy, and stated that he had led a pious...*

When he was asked if he had actually done any good for others or performed any acts of charity, or even wanted to, he replied that he did not know what "works of charity" meant, only that he had lived a holy life. Because his primary goal was actually personal power—viewing others as worthless compared to himself, especially since he considered himself a saint—his appearance changed. At first, he appeared in a human form that was white down to the waist, but he soon shifted into a dark blue, and finally to black. Because he desired to rule over others while looking down on them, he became even darker than those he despised. The state of those who wish to be the "greatest" in heaven is described further back in sections 450 and 452.*

953. *While being led through some of the dwellings of the first heaven, I saw a vast sea in the distance. It was surging with massive waves, and its borders reached further than I could see. I was told that people who chased worldly status and were obsessed only with gaining fame—without caring if they used honest or dishonest means—are gripped by <term>phantasies<gloss>In this context, "phantasies" refer to vivid, inescapable spiritual hallucinations that reflect a person's inner state or earthly obsessions.</gloss></term> like this. They see a sea such as this and live in constant terror of drowning in it.*

954. *The obsessions that dominate a person's life in the body are transformed in the afterlife into corresponding experiences. For example, those who were violent and heartless on earth find those vices turned into an incredible degree of cruelty. They seem to themselves to murder and torture every companion they meet in various ways, and they find their highest pleasure in these acts. Those who were bloodthirsty take delight in torturing spirits until they see blood—or what appears to be blood—for their <term>phantasy<gloss>The mental projection or "waking dream" of a spirit that feels entirely real to them.</gloss></term> makes it look real to them. At the sight of this blood, they feel a deep, dark satisfaction. The delusions of the greedy or avaricious make them believe they are infested with mice and similar vermin, depending on the specific nature of their greed. Those who lived only for physical pleasures, making them the sole purpose of life—their "heaven"—find their greatest satisfaction living in <note>original: "latrinis," translated here as "privies" or outhouses</note> privies, which they perceive as pleasant places. Some live in stinking, urine-filled lakes, while others live in muddy bogs, and so on.*

955. *There are also many different kinds of punishment with which the wicked are severely tormented in the next life. They tend to rush into these punishments as they return to their own filthy <term>lusts<gloss>Intense, disordered selfish desires that drive the spirit's behavior.</gloss></term>. Through these experiences, they eventually feel shame, terror, and horror regarding their behavior, and they eventually stop. These punishments are of various...*

*...kinds, but consist in general of laceration, cutting to pieces, punishments under veils, and many others.*

*956. Those who, being addicted to revenge, fancy themselves greater than everybody else, esteeming others as nothing in respect to themselves, are punished by laceration, which is thus effected. They are bedaubed all over the body and face, so that there are scarcely any traces of a human figure left. The face looks like a thick round cake, the arms resemble coarse garments, which being stretched out are set in motion on high, and turned constantly towards heaven, whilst the nature of their offence is publicly proclaimed; and this is continued till they are most intimately touched with shame, and are thus compelled in a suppliant manner to beg forgiveness, and submit to authority. Afterwards they are conveyed to a miry lake, near the filthy Jerusalem <note>In Swedenborg’s visions, "Jerusalem" often represents the Church or a religious state; a "filthy Jerusalem" refers to a corrupted or hypocritical religious environment in the spiritual world.</note>, and are plunged and tumbled therein, until they are all covered with mud; and this is repeated until such lust for revenge is taken away. In this lake there are malicious women belonging to the province of the <term>Urinary Bladder<note>original: "Vesica Urinatoria." Swedenborg’s "Grand Man" theory suggests that the entire spiritual world corresponds to the anatomy of the human body; certain regions represent the "excrementitious" or waste-filtering functions.</note></term>.*

*957. Those who in the life of the body have contracted a habit of speaking one thing and thinking another—especially if, under the mask of friendship, they have sought to obtain the wealth of others—wander about in another life, and wheresoever they come inquire whether they may abide there, saying that they are poor. On being received in any place, they covet all that they see in consequence of the lust that is in them; but as soon as their evil nature is discovered, they are punished and expelled, sometimes being miserably racked in different ways—according to the nature of the deceit and hypocrisy which they have contracted—some as to their whole body, others as to the feet, loins, breast, or head, and others only as to the region about the mouth. These torments consist of reciprocal reverberations <note>These are described as violent, back-and-forth shaking or vibrating movements that feel like being bounced between two surfaces.</note> of a nature not to be described, being violent collisions, and consequently stretching of parts, which make them fancy themselves torn into small pieces, struggling violently all the while. These rack-like punishments are of very various kinds, and are frequently repeated at intervals until the sufferers become affected with fear and horror at the thought of deceiving by false speeches—every succeeding punishment operates to the removal of something. The executioners declare they are so delighted with their office that they would like to exercise it to all eternity.*

*958. There are troops of spirits wandering about, of whom others are exceedingly afraid. They apply themselves to the lower part of the back, and torment by rapidly jerking and violently and audibly twisting the bodies of spirits into the form of a cone, having its apex <note>The pointed top or tip of the cone.</note> upward, and towards which they direct their chief force. Whosoever is let into this cone—and they are deceitful hypocrites who are punished in this way—especially if he be towards its top, is miserably racked in every joint.*

# GENESIS. [Chapter 9]

959. *One night on awaking, I heard some spirits about me, who were desirous to ensnare me in my sleep, and after a little while I had a dismal dream. On again awaking, I was much surprised to see suddenly present certain chastising spirits, who inflicted terrible punishment on those who had endeavored to ensnare me whilst asleep, by clothing them as it were with visible bodies, having corporeal senses <note>The term "corporeal senses" refers to the physical feelings of the body; here, spirits are made to feel physical pain as if they still had flesh.</note>, and then torturing them by violent collisions of the parts in all directions, attended with pangs owing to the struggles thereby occasioned. The chastising spirits desired to kill them if they could—they being principally the **sirens** <note>In this context, "sirens" are deceitful spirits who use charms or psychological manipulation to obsess and control others.</note> spoken of in section 831—and this added greatly to their violence. The punishment lasted a long while, extending to several troops about me; and what was surprising, all who had endeavored to ensnare me were discovered, notwithstanding they sought to conceal themselves; for being sirens, they endeavored by numerous contrivances to avoid punishment, but in vain. Sometimes they tried to escape by hiding themselves in the interior parts of nature <note>This suggests attempting to hide within the deeper, more subtle layers of the spiritual or psychological atmosphere.</note>; at others by pretending not to be the persons who had offended. Now they sought to transfer the punishment to others by transferring to them their own ideas; then they pretended that they were infants who were thus tortured, or good spirits, or angels, with a variety of other artifices—but all to no purpose. Wondering that they were so severely punished, I perceived that it was because their crime was of so enormous a kind, arising from the necessity there is that man should sleep in safety, since otherwise the human race must necessarily perish. I was also made aware that the same thing occurs, although man is ignorant of the fact, in reference to others, whom these spirits endeavor by their artifices to assault during sleep; for unless it be given to converse with spirits, being with them by internal sense <note>The "internal sense" is the spiritual capacity to perceive the world of spirits directly, rather than through physical eyes and ears.</note>, it is impossible to hear, and much more to see, such things, notwithstanding they happen alike to all. The Lord is particularly watchful over man during sleep.*

960. *There are certain deceitful spirits, who, whilst they lived in the body, practised secret artifices, and some of them, who, by a mischievous simulation assumed the semblance of angels with a view to deceive. Such spirits learn in the other world to withdraw themselves into the more subtile part of nature <note>A refined level of spiritual existence where they believe they are invisible to others.</note>, retiring from the observation of others, thinking thus to secure themselves from punishment. These, however, not only undergo racking pains like the others, according to the nature and heinousness of their deceit, but are also **cemented together** in such a way, that the more they desire to be loosened or separated from each other, so much the closer do they adhere. This punishment is attended with more intense torture, as answering to their deeper laid stratagems.*

961. *Some persons from habit, and others from a spirit of derision, accustom themselves to introduce texts of Holy Scripture*

962. *There is also a mode of punishment in which spirits are as it were torn asunder as to their thoughts, the interior thoughts being at war with the exterior. This is attended with interior torture.*

963. *The punishment of the veil is a very common one, and is effected in this manner. The offender, in consequence of the phantasies <note>In this context, "phantasies" refers to false or delusional sensory experiences in the spiritual world.</note> by which he is impressed, appears to himself to be under a veil, stretched out to a great distance, which is as it were a cohering cloud, condensed according to the culprit’s phantasy. Under this cloud the sufferers run here and there, with an exceedingly eager desire to make their escape, and with different velocities, until they are wearied out, this generally continuing for the space of an hour, more or less, and being attended with different degrees of torture according to the intensity of their desire to extricate themselves. The punishment of the veil is inflicted on those who, although they see the truth, are rendered by self-love unwilling to acknowledge it, and are angry to think that it is the truth. Some spirits have such anxiety and terror under the veil, that they despair of ever being set at liberty, as I was informed by one who had been let out.*

964. *There is also another kind of veil, in which the offender is enveloped as in a sheet, so that he seems to himself to be bound hand, foot, and body, and is at the same time impressed with a strong desire to extricate himself. This he imagines may be easily effected, as he is only wrapped up in a single fold, but, on making the attempt, the more he unfolds it, the longer it grows, until he is driven at last to despair.*

965. *What has been said may suffice concerning the hells and the punishments inflicted therein. Infernal torments are not, as some suppose, the stings of conscience <note>The author clarifies that those in hell cannot feel the "sting of conscience" because they have entirely discarded their conscience to get there.</note>, for those who are in hell have no conscience, and consequently cannot be so tormented, for such as have had conscience are amongst the blessed.*

966. *It is to be observed, that no one suffers any punishment and torture in another life on account of hereditary evils <note>Inherited tendencies toward selfishness or sin.</note>, but for the actual evils <note>Choices and actions made of one's own free will.</note> which he has himself committed.*

967. *When the wicked endure punishment, there are always angels present to regulate its degree, and alleviate the pains of the sufferers as much as may be. They cannot, however, remove them entirely, because such is the equilibrium <note>The fundamental spiritual law of balance, where every evil action carries its own necessary consequence or reaction.</note> of all things in another life, that evil punishes itself, and unless it were removed by punishments, the evil spirits must necessarily be kept in some*

968. *Some people have held the idea that the devil should never be spoken to, but should instead be shunned and avoided. However, such people are taught that no harm can come to those whom the Lord protects, even if they were surrounded by all the powers of hell both within and without—as I have learned through various and astonishing experiences. Eventually, I had no fear of speaking even with the very worst of the hellish company—this being allowed so that I might become acquainted with their nature. When some expressed surprise that I would converse with such wicked creatures, I informed them not only that such conversation caused me no harm, but also that the devils in the other world were once men. During their life here on earth, they lived in hatred, revenge, and adultery; many of them were even held in high respect and esteem at the time. Indeed, there are some among them whom I knew personally when they were in the body; for "the devil" is nothing more than a name for such a hellish crew. I stated further that while living in the body, every person has at least two spirits from hell and two angels from heaven accompanying them. With wicked people, the hellish spirits take control, but with good people, they are subdued and forced to serve. Consequently, it is an error to believe that any devils have existed since the beginning of creation other than those who were once men. Upon hearing this account, they were greatly amazed and confessed that they had held an entirely different opinion regarding the devil and his followers.*

969. *In so vast a kingdom—where all the souls of men have gathered since the beginning of creation, with nearly a million arriving weekly from this earth, each with a unique character and nature, and where there is a general communication of everyone’s ideas—everything must be continually organized, both in general and in every specific detail. Because of this, there must necessarily exist a countless number of circumstances that have never even occurred to the human mind. Since almost no one until now has had anything but a very vague idea of either heaven or hell, what has been said above will naturally seem strange and marvelous. This is especially true because spirits are generally thought to lack senses, even though they actually possess them more exquisitely than living men. In fact, evil spirits—using tricks unknown in our world—have the power to impose a sensory experience on others that feels almost physical, and is therefore much more blunt and heavy.*

970. *The nature of <term>vastations</term> <note>In this context, "vastation" refers to a process of purification or stripping away of external traits in the afterlife so that a spirit's outer appearance matches their inner essence.</note> will be considered at the conclusion of this chapter.*

# THE CONTENTS.

971. The state of the <term>regenerate man</term> <note>In this theological framework, a "regenerate man" is someone who has undergone a spiritual rebirth, allowing their inner spirit to be guided by divine truth rather than worldly desires.</note> now follows; and first of the dominion of the <term>internal man</term> <note>The "internal man" represents the higher, spiritual part of the human mind.</note> and the submission of the <term>external</term> <note>The "external man" refers to the natural, sensory, and physical aspects of a person.</note>.
972. All things belonging to the external man are subject and subservient to the internal, verses 1 to 3; but particular caution is necessary, lest man should immerse the goods and truths of faith in his lusts, or by goods and truths which are of the internal man confirm evils and falses <note>A technical term used here to describe false beliefs or "untruths" that arise from a person's selfish desires.</note>, which must of necessity condemn him to death, and punish him, verses 4 and 5, and thus destroy the <term>spiritual man</term>, or the image of God, with him, verse 6. This being prevented, all things will prosper with him, verse 7.

973. It next treats of the state of man after the flood, whom the Lord so formed that he might be present with him by means of charity <note>In this context, charity refers to an active love for one's neighbor and the practice of good deeds, rather than just donating money.</note>, and thus prevent his perishing like the last posterity of the *Most Ancient Church* <note>The "Most Ancient Church" refers to the earliest state of humanity (symbolized by Adam), which fell into total corruption before the flood.</note>, verses 8—11.

974. Afterwards the state of man subsequent to the deluge, who is in a capacity to receive charity, is described by *a bow in the cloud* <note>The rainbow.</note>, which he resembles, verses 12—17. The relation this *bow* has to the man of the church, or the <term>regenerate man</term> <note>One who has been spiritually reborn or transformed by divine truth.</note>, verses 12, 13 ;—to every man in general, verses 14, 15 ;—to the man who is in a capacity of being regenerated in particular, verse 16 ;—and consequently not only to man within but also to man without the church, verse 17.

975. It treats lastly of the Ancient Church in general; by *Shem*, there is understood internal worship <note>Sincere devotion from the heart.</note>, by *Japheth*, corresponding external worship <note>Outward religious practices that match the heart's intent.</note>, by *Ham*, faith separate from charity, and by *Canaan*, external worship separate from internal <note>Performing religious rituals without any actual love or spiritual substance.</note>,—from verse 19 to the end. This church, through the desire to investigate the truths of faith of itself, and by reasonings, first lapsed into errors and perverse opinions, verses 19—21. Those who are in external worship separate from internal, deride the doctrine of faith itself, in consequence of such errors and perverse opinions, verse 22 ; but such as are in internal worship, and in external thence derived, interpret such things to good, and excuse them, verse 23. Those who are in external worship separate from internal, are most vile, verses 24, 25 ; and still they may perform vile services in the church, verses 26, 27.

976. Lastly, the duration and state of the first Ancient Church are described by the years of Noah, verses 28, 29.

## THE INTERNAL SENSE.

977. Since it here treats of the <term>regenerate man</term>, it may be helpful to point out briefly his nature as compared with one who is not regenerate, so that the nature of both may be understood. With the regenerate man there is *joy* when he acts according to conscience, and anxiety when forced to do or think contrary to it; but it is not so with the unregenerate, for in many instances he does not know what conscience is, much less what it is to do any thing either according to or contrary to it, he doing only what

978. What the internal man is, and what the external, is known to few, if any, in the present day. It is generally supposed that they are one and the same, and the reason of this supposition is, because the generality of persons believe that they do what is good and think what is true of themselves, or from <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium". What the internal man is, and what the external, cannot be known, unless we are first aware that there is in every man a <term>celestial and spiritual principle</term> <note>These represent the highest levels of the soul, focused on love (celestial) and truth (spiritual).</note> corresponding with the angelic heaven, a <term>rational principle</term> <note>The "middle" part of the mind that uses logic and reason to bridge higher spiritual truths with lower worldly experiences.</note> corresponding with the heaven of angelic spirits, and an interior <term>sensual principle</term> <note>In this context, "sensual" refers to the outermost layer of the mind that deals with sensory information and worldly appearances, rather than "sensuality" in a modern physical sense.</note> corresponding with the heaven of spirits. Hence it was made manifest to me what constitutes the internal, and what the external man. The internal man is formed of what is celestial and spiritual; the interior or intermediate man, of what is rational; and the external man of sensual things, not belonging to the body, but derived from bodily things; and this is the case not only with man, but also with spirits. To speak in the language of the learned, these three, the internal, interior, and external man, are like *end, cause, and effect*; and it is well known that no *effect* can possibly be produced unless there be a cause, and that there is no cause without an *end*. *Effect, cause, and end*, are as distinct from each other as exterior, interior, and inmost. 

Strictly speaking, the sensual man—or he whose thought is grounded in sensual things—is the external man, and the spiritual and celestial man, the internal man, but the rational man is intermediate between the two—that by which the communication of the internal and external is effected. I am aware that few will apprehend these statements, in consequence of the generality of mankind living in external things, and making them the ground of their thoughts. Hence some regard themselves as like the brutes, believing that on the death of the body they shall die also, although they then first begin truly to live. 

After death, those who are good, at first live the sensual life in the world or heaven of spirits, afterwards the interior sensual life in the heaven of angelic spirits, and lastly the inmost sensual life in the angelic heaven, this angelic life being the life of the internal man, concerning which scarcely any thing can be said which is comprehensible by man. ### 979.] 
These observations on the state of the <term>regenerate man</term> <note>A person undergoing a process of spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note>, and on how the internal self flows into the external self, are provided as an introduction. ### 980.] 
**Verse 1. *And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful and multiply, and replenish the earth.*** *God blessed* signifies the presence and grace of the Lord; *Noah and his sons* signify the <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>According to the author, this refers to a specific era of spiritual history following the metaphorical "Flood," characterized by symbolic worship.</note>; *be fruitful* refers to the good works of charity; *and multiply* refers to the truths of faith, which were now to be increased; *by replenishing the earth* is signified the manifestation of these things in the external man.

### 981.] 
*God blessed* signifies the presence and grace of the Lord, as is evident from the meaning of the word *blessing*. To *bless*, in the Word <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible as a divine communication.</note>, means in a literal sense to enrich someone with every earthly and physical good. This is how the text is explained by those who stay only on the surface of the meaning—such as the ancient and modern Jews, and also many Christians today—who believe the divine *blessing* consists of riches, many possessions, and personal glory. 

To *bless* in the internal, spiritual sense, however, is to be enriched with all spiritual and heavenly goodness. This blessing can only be given by the Lord, and for that reason, it signifies His *presence* and *grace*, which naturally bring such spiritual goodness with them. The word *presence* is used because the Lord is present only where there is charity <note>In this context, "charity" means an active love for one's neighbor.</note>, and this passage concerns the reborn spiritual person who acts out of love. 

The Lord is indeed *present* with every person, but to the extent that a person moves away from love, that *presence*—so to speak—becomes more distant, or the Lord seems more remote. The reason why the text mentions *grace* rather than *mercy* is because "celestial" people <note>Those motivated by pure love.</note> never speak of *grace*, but only of *mercy*, while "spiritual" people <note>Those motivated by truth and intellect.</note> never mention *mercy*, but speak of *grace*. This way of speaking is based on the fact that celestial people acknowledge the human race to be nothing but filthiness—even, in itself, like waste and belonging to hell—and so they plead for the *mercy* of the Lord. Spiritual people, however, although they know human nature is like this, do not fully acknowledge it in the same way because they remain in their <term>own selfhood</term> <note>original: "proprium"; this refers to the human ego or the sense of "self" that desires to feel independent from the Divine.</note>, which they love. Therefore, they find it difficult to speak of *mercy*, but speak easily of *grace*.

### 982. 
By *Noah and his sons* is signified the <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>The spiritual era or state of humanity that followed the symbolic "Flood," characterized by a specific type of symbolic worship.</note>, as was stated and shown previously, and as is also clear from the text that follows.

### 983. 
*Be fruitful* signifies the good works of charity, and *multiply* signifies the truths of faith, which were now about to be increased. This is evident from the meaning of both expressions in the Word <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible.</note>, where *to be fruitful* (or to produce fruit) is constantly <term>predicated</term> <note>A technical term meaning "attributed to" or "spoken of."</note> of charity, and *to multiply* is predicated of faith, as was shown previously in sections 43 and 55. To further confirm this, we may look at the following passages from the Word:

“Turn, O backsliding children;—I will give you pastors according to mine heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and intelligence. And it shall be that ye shall be *multiplied and made fruitful in the earth*,” (Jeremiah 3:14—16). In this passage, *to multiply* clearly refers to growth in knowledge and intelligence—that is, in faith—while *to be made fruitful* relates to the good things of charity. This passage describes the planting of a church, where faith (multiplication) comes first. 

Again, in the same prophet: “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all lands whither I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds, and they shall *be fruitful and multiplied*,” (Jeremiah 23:3). This refers to a church that is already established; consequently, it is *fruitful* regarding the goods of charity and *multiplied* regarding the truths of faith. 

So also in the books of Moses: “Moreover I will look to you, and make you to be *fruitful* and I will make you to be *multiplied*, and establish my covenant with you,” (Leviticus 26:9). In the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note>, this speaks of the celestial church; therefore, *to be fruitful* is used for the goods of love and charity, and *to be multiplied* for the goods and truths of faith. 

In Zechariah: “I will redeem them, and they shall be *multiplied* as they have been *multiplied*,” (10:8). That *to be multiplied* here refers to the truths of faith is evident because it speaks of them being "redeemed." 

In Jeremiah: “The city shall be builded upon her own heap—and out of them shall proceed confession, and the voice of them that make merry, and I will cause them to be *multiplied*, and they shall not be diminished—their sons also shall be as aforetime,” (30:18—20). This speaks of the affections for truth and the truths of faith themselves. The affections are represented by *confession* and *the voice of them that make merry*, while the truths are represented by *being multiplied*. In this context, *sons* also represent truths.

### 984. 
*To replenish the earth* means to do so within the <term>external man</term> <note>The "external man" refers to the part of a person that interacts with the physical world—their senses, outward behaviors, and worldly memory.</note>. This is clear because, as demonstrated previously, the *earth* symbolizes the external man. Regarding the "goods of charity" and "truths of faith" in a person undergoing <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or transformation where a person moves from being self-centered to being led by divine love.</note>, these qualities are planted in the conscience through faith and hearing the Word. Consequently, they must first be stored in the memory, which belongs to the external man. When a person is reborn and the <term>internal man</term> <note>The higher, spiritual part of a person that is open to heaven and the Lord.</note> begins to act, the same process of *fructification and multiplication* occurs: the "goods of charity" express themselves in the desires of the external man, while the "truths of faith" increase and *multiply* within the memory. Any reborn person can recognize this process through the Word, through their own reason, and through <term>scientifics</term> <note>A technical term for factual knowledge or data gathered from the world.</note>, which further confirm their growth. This is the result of charity, with the Lord alone working through that charity.

### 985. 
Verse 2. *And let the fear of you and the dread of you be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every bird of heaven, to every thing which the ground causeth to creep forth, and to all the fishes of the sea; let them be given into your hands.* The *fear of you and the dread of you* signify the authority or dominion of the internal man—*fear* relates to "evils" and *dread* relates to <term>falses</term> <note>In this context, "falses" or "falsities" are incorrect beliefs or distortions of truth that lead a person away from spiritual goodness.</note>. The phrase *upon every beast of the earth* refers to the lusts or cravings belonging to the <term>animus</term> <note>Original Latin: *animus*. This refers to the lower or natural mind, which is the seat of emotions and worldly passions.</note>. The *bird of heaven* refers to the false ideas resulting from faulty reasoning. *To every thing which the ground causeth to creep forth* denotes the affections for what is good, while *to all the fishes of the sea* refers to <term>scientifics</term>. Finally, *let them be given into your hands* signifies that these things are now the possessions of the internal man, held within the external.

### 986. 
*The fear of you and the dread of you* signifies the dominion of the internal man, where *fear* refers to evils and *dread* to falsities. This can be seen in the state of a person being reborn. Before regeneration, a person’s cravings and false beliefs—which belong to the external man—usually dominate, leading to an inner struggle. Once reborn, however, the internal man takes charge of the external, ruling over its lusts and falsehoods. At this point, the person feels a *fear* of evil and a *dread* of falsehood, as both are contrary to their conscience; acting against conscience fills them with horror. However, it is not actually the internal man who feels this fear, but the external man. This is why the text says *let the fear of you... be upon every beast... and bird*, meaning upon the lusts (beasts) and the falsities (birds). While this fear and dread feel like they belong to the person themselves, they actually arise from a deeper cause. So in Ezekiel: "Upon his ruin shall every bird of heaven dwell, and every wild beast of the field shall be upon his branches," (31:13). In Daniel: "At length upon the bird of abominations shall be desolation," (9:27). In John: "Babylon... is become... the cage of every unclean and hateful bird," (Revelation 18:2). It is also frequently said in the prophets, that their carcasses should be given for meat to the *bird of heaven*, and to the beast of the earth (Jeremiah 7:33; 19:7; 34:20; Ezekiel 29:5; 39:4; Psalm 79:2; Isaiah 18:6); by which is signified that they should be destroyed by falsities, which are the *birds of heaven*, and by evils or lusts, which are the *beasts of the earth*.

989. Dominion over falsities, and dominion over evils, are regulated by similar laws, man of himself not being capable of exercising the least authority over what is false. Inasmuch as it here treats of the dominion of the <term>regenerate man</term> <note>A person undergoing a spiritual "rebirth" or transformation, moving from a self-centered life to one guided by divine love and wisdom.</note> over lusts (the *beast of the earth*) and over falsities (the *bird of heaven*), it is to be observed, that no one can say with any degree of propriety that he is regenerate unless he acknowledge and believe that <term>charity</term> <note>original: *caritas*; Here, charity does not just mean giving to the poor, but the internal feeling of love and goodwill toward others.</note> is the primary of his faith, be affected with love towards his neighbor, and be merciful and compassionate towards him—for his new will is formed from charity. By charity the Lord operates the good and thence the true, but not by faith without charity. There are some who exercise themselves in works of charity from a principle of obedience only—that is, because the Lord has so commanded, who nevertheless are not yet fully regenerate—such, however, are regenerated in another life, if they do not make righteousness to consist in mere external works.

990. By *every thing which the ground causeth to creep forth*, the affections of goodness are typified, as is evident both from what was previously said and from the signification of *ground*, out of which they are produced or *creep forth*; for it there treated of the evils and falsities over which the regenerate man should have dominion, although here of the <term>affections of goodness</term> <note>The internal desires or leanings toward what is morally and spiritually right.</note>, which would be given into his hands. It is evident from the signification of *ground*, out of which they are produced, or *creep forth*, because ground denotes the man of the church in general, and whatever is of the church, consequently, in this passage, all that is produced from the Lord in the external man.

993. **Verse 3. Every creeping thing** <note>original: "reptile"</note> **that lives shall be food** <note>original: "meat"</note> **for you; as the edible** <note>original: "esculent"</note> **vegetable of the herb, I have given it all to you.** *Every creeping thing that lives* signifies all pleasures that contain "good" (which is what is truly "alive"). *Shall be food for you* signifies the delight of those pleasures which people are meant to enjoy. *As the edible vegetable of the herb* refers to those things which are considered lowly or basic among delights. *I have given it all to you* signifies the enjoyment of these things because of their practical use.

994. *Every creeping thing that lives* denotes all pleasures in which there is good, for it is this "good" that constitutes life. This is clear from the meaning of "creeping thing" mentioned previously. In this context, all "clean" <note>In a biblical sense, "clean" refers to animals permitted for food or sacrifice, symbolizing pure or orderly affections.</note> beasts and birds are meant by the term "creeping things," as must be obvious to everyone, since the text says they are *given for food*. Strictly speaking, creeping things are the lowliest of all animals and are often considered "unclean," as seen in Leviticus 11:23, 29, and 30. However, in a broader sense—as used here—they refer to animals given for food. In this specific passage, they are called creeping things because they symbolize pleasures. 

Human affections (which, as previously noted, are represented in the Bible by clean beasts) are only perceived by a person through the pleasure they cause. Therefore, a person calls these affections "pleasures," and for this reason, they are called "creeping things" here. Pleasures are of two kinds: those of the will and those of the intellect. 

In a general sense, there are:
*   Pleasures arising from the possession of land, money, honors, and public office.
*   Pleasures of <term>conjugial love</term> <note>From the Latin *conjugialis*, referring to the spiritual and sacred love between a married couple.</note>, and of love toward infants and children.
*   Pleasures of friendship and social interaction.

There are also:
*   Pleasures of reading, writing, and acquiring knowledge and wisdom.
*   Pleasures of the senses: hearing (such as the delight found in music and singing); sight (from beautiful objects of many kinds); smell (from sweet odors); taste (from agreeable food and drink); and touch (resulting from many different delights).

These kinds of pleasures, because they are felt in the body, are called <term>corporeal pleasures</term> <note>Physical or bodily pleasures.</note>. However, in reality, no pleasure exists in the body that does not originate and survive from some "interior affection." Furthermore, no interior affection exists that does not originate and survive from one even more interior, which contains its purpose and end. 

While living in the body, a person is usually unaware of these deeper delights that flow in order from the "inmost" part of their being. Many hardly know these internal states exist, let alone that all outward pleasure is derived from them. However, since it is impossible for anything to exist in the external world unless it has an orderly connection with what is internal, these outward pleasures are actually <term>ultimate effects</term> <note>The final, outward expression of an internal spiritual cause.</note>. These interior things are not discovered while a person lives in the physical body, except...

Interior affections <note>In this context, "affections" refers to deep-seated emotional states or the inclinations of the soul.</note>, with their delights, show themselves in the world of spirits; such as are more interior, with their pleasantness, in the heaven of angelic spirits; and those which are more interior still, with their happiness, in the heaven of angels; for there are three heavens, one more interior, perfect, and happy than the other (as may be seen above, sections 459 and 684). This may be demonstrated to anyone from the consideration of the sense of vision and its pleasures, for unless there were interior sight, the eye could never see. Ocular vision derives its existence from interior sight, which is why man sees equally well after death—nay, much better than while living in the body—not indeed worldly and physical objects, but those of the other world. Hence those who were blind here see in another life equally well with those who were sharp-sighted; and hence also a man during sleep sees in his dreams as well as when he is awake; and by means of internal sight in the other world, I also have seen objects far more clearly than I do those which are here. 

Hence it is evident that external vision exists from interior vision, and this from vision still more interior, and so on; and it is similar with every other sense and pleasure. Pleasures are likewise called *reptiles* in other parts of the Word <note>"The Word" refers to the Bible.</note>, and a further distinction is made between those that are clean and those that are unclean—that is, between pleasures whose delights are living or heavenly, and those which are dead and hellish. Thus we read in Hosea:

Here the *wild beast of the field, the bird of the heavens, and the reptiles* signify such things in man as have been mentioned, as may appear from this consideration: that it there treats of a new church. In David:

> "Let the heavens and earth praise Him [Jehovah], the seas and every thing that creepeth therein." (Psalm 69:34)

*Seas and the creeping things therein* cannot praise Jehovah, but He may be praised by every thing in man signified by them.

That filthy pleasures also, which originate in the <term>proprium</term> <note>Proprium is a technical term referring to the "selfhood" or the ego—everything that a person feels belongs to themselves as opposed to what is received from the Divine.</note>, consequently in its defiled lusts, are likewise called *reptiles*, appears from Ezekiel: “So I went in and saw, and behold, every form of *reptile* and of *beast*—the abomination; and all the *idols* of the house of Israel, portrayed upon the wall round about,” (8:10.) Because *reptiles* typified these defiled affections, in the <term>representative church</term> <note>The "representative church" refers to the ancient Israelite system of worship, where physical objects and rituals were intended to symbolize spiritual and heavenly realities.</note>, they were accounted so unclean that it was not even lawful to touch them, and whosoever did so became unclean (Leviticus 5:2; 11:31–33; 22:5, 6).

### 996.
The *esculent vegetable* <note>An archaic term for an edible plant or garden herb.</note> signifies defiled delights, as is manifest from what has been previously stated. They are called *the esculent vegetable of the herb*, because they are only worldly and corporeal, or external, and, as was observed, the pleasures which are perceived in corporeal things or in ultimates <note>In this context, "ultimates" refers to the most outward or physical level of existence.</note> derive their origin from co-ordinated interior delights, and are respectively defiled; for every delight is of such a nature, that it becomes viler in proportion as it is external, and happier in the degree in which it is internal. 

Thus, as we have seen, in proportion as externals are evolved, or unswathed <note>Revealed or unfolded, as if removing outer layers to show what is inside.</note>, so much the more of amenity and happiness do their delights present, as must be very evident from this consideration, that the delight of man's pleasures whilst living in the body is vile compared with his delight after death, when he enters into the world of spirits; indeed, it is so vile that good spirits utterly despise them, nor would they desire to return to them even could they enjoy all that the world affords. 

But the delight of these good spirits likewise becomes vile when they are elevated by the Lord into the heaven of angelic spirits, for then they put off their interior delights, and enter upon such as are still more interior; and the same is true of the delight which angelic spirits enjoyed in their heaven, for this becomes vile when they are raised up by the Lord into the angelic or third heaven <note>The highest level of heaven in this theological system, characterized by pure love.</note>, where, in consequence of internal things living, and mutual love being felt by all, the happiness of its inhabitants is inexpressible, as may be seen in what is related of the nature of interior delight or happiness, n. 545. 

Hence it is evident what is meant by *as the esculent vegetable of the herb have I given it you*. Inasmuch as reptiles signify both the sensual and corporeal pleasures, of which the *esculent vegetable of the herb* is predicated, in the original tongue <note>Referring to the original Hebrew text of the Bible.</note> a word is here employed which means both any *esculent vegetable* and any *green thing*—*esculent vegetable* in reference to the pleasures arising from the <term>will-principle</term> <note>The faculty of the mind responsible for desires and intentions.</note> or the <term>celestial affections</term> <note>Deeply felt emotions related to the highest form of love for God.</note>, and *green thing* in reference to those of the <term>intellectual principle</term> <note>The faculty of the mind responsible for thought and understanding.</note> or the <term>spiritual affections</term> <note>Emotions related to the love of truth and the neighbor.</note>. ### 997.
*I have given it you all*, denotes the enjoyment on account of its use which is in meat <note>The word "meat" here is used in the older sense meaning "food" in general.</note>, as is evident from whatever is given for meat being of use. In reference to *use* it may be observed, that those who are in charity—that is, in love towards the neighbor, which imparts a living delight to their pleasure—look for the fruition of no pleasure except in the performance of *uses*; for charity is a nothing unless it manifest itself in the works of charity, since it consists in exercise or *use*. He who loves his neighbor as himself never perceives the delight of charity except in its exercise, wherefore a life of charity is a life of *uses*. Such is the life of the universal heaven; for the Lord’s kingdom, being a kingdom of mutual love, is a kingdom of *uses*; hence every pleasure derived from charity receives its delight from *use*, and the more exalted the *use*, so much the greater is the delight; and hence the angels receive happiness from the Lord according to the essence and quality of the *use* which they perform. So also it is with every pleasure, for the more distinguished its *use*, so much the greater its delight. Thus, for instance, conjugial love <note>term: conjugial love <gloss>A technical term for "marriage love," specifically referring to a spiritual and eternal union between two people.</gloss></note>, which is the seminary <note>The nursery or source from which something grows.</note> of human society, and from which is formed the Lord’s kingdom in the heavens, performs the most important of all *uses*, and is therefore attended with so great a delight, that, as was observed, it is heavenly happiness. It is similar with respect to other pleasures, with a difference, however, according to the excellence of their *uses*, which indeed are so numerous that it is scarcely possible to divide them into their several genera and species <note>Categories and types.</note>, although all of them regard the Lord’s kingdom or the Lord—some more nearly and directly, others more remotely and obliquely. Hence it may appear that all pleasures are allowed to man, but for the sake of *use* only, and that by virtue of their *use*, with a difference according to its degree, they participate in and live from heavenly felicity.

### 999.
<term>Flesh</term> <note>In the spiritual sense of the Word, "flesh" often represents the human will, particularly when it is focused on self-interest rather than God.</note> denotes the <term>voluntary principle</term> <note>The "voluntary principle" refers to the faculty of the human mind from which a person wills, desires, and chooses.</note> of man, as is evident from its specific signification in reference to man in a state of corruption. *Flesh*, in a general sense, denotes every man, but especially the corporeal man <note>The "corporeal man" is one who is focused entirely on bodily and worldly concerns.</note>, as may be seen above, n. 574; hence it signifies man's <term>proprium</term> <note>A technical term meaning one’s "own" or the "self"—the inherent nature of a person that feels independent of God.</note>, and consequently his will. His <term>voluntary principle</term>, or will, is only mere evil; wherefore *flesh*, when predicated of the man who is of such a quality, represents every lust, or every concupiscence <note>A strong, often selfish or disordered desire.</note>; for his will, as has been often previously shown, is nothing else but lust. Now as *flesh* had this signification, it was therefore represented by the *flesh* which the people lusted after in the wilderness, concerning which it is thus written in Moses: "The mixed multitude which was in the midst of it, *lusted a lust*, and the children of Israel also returned and wept, and said, Who shall give us *flesh* to eat?" (Numb. xi. 4.) Here *flesh* is plainly denominated a lust, for it is said they *lusted a lust*, and said, "Who shall give us *flesh* to eat?" It is also evident from the words which follow: "While the *flesh* was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of Jehovah was kindled against the people, and Jehovah smote the people with a very great plague, and he called the name of that place the graves of lust, because they there buried the people that *lusted*," (Numb. xi. 33, 34.) It must be plain to every one that such a plague would never have been inflicted on the people merely because they desired meat, since this is natural to men who have been long kept from eating it, as the people in the wilderness had been. There was, however, a more interior cause for such a plague, one of a spiritual nature, which was, that the people here spoken of were such as utterly to loathe what was signified and represented by <term>manna</term> <note>Manna represents heavenly bread, or the wisdom and goodness that come from God.</note>—as is manifest from the sixth verse of the same chapter—and that they desired only what was signified and represented by *flesh*, or the affections of self-will, which are of the nature of lusts, and in themselves excrementitious <note>Likened to waste products; things that have no spiritual life or value.</note> and profane. Now, as that church was a <term>representative church</term> <note>A church where external rituals and historical events were designed to mirror internal, spiritual realities.</note>, when these things came to be represented, the people were smitten with this great plague; for what was done to them was spiritually represented in heaven, where *manna* denotes what is celestial, and the *flesh* which was lusted after their defiled <term>voluntary principle</term>: hence their punishment was a consequence of their evil nature. From these and other passages in the Word it may be seen here that by *flesh* is signified what is of the will, and man's <term>voluntary principle</term>; and how defiled this is was shown at the second verse of this chapter, when treating of the beast of the earth.

### 1000.
**The soul** signifies life, as might be proved by numerous citations from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>. It is there used to denote life in general, as well what is internal, or the life of the internal man, as what is external, or the life of the external man. Now as it denotes all life, it necessarily signifies the life of the man of whom it is predicated, and it is here predicated of the life of the <term>regenerate man</term> <note>A person undergoing spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note>, which is distinct from that of his will; for, as was before observed, the new life which the regenerate spiritual man receives from the Lord is altogether separate from his <term>voluntary principle</term> or <term>proprium</term> <note>The "proprium" is the sense of self or ego that feels independent of God; in this theology, it is viewed as inherently selfish or "dead" without divine influence.</note>, or proper life, which is not life, although it is so called, but is death, inasmuch as it is infernal life. Here, therefore, *flesh with the soul thereof*, which they were not to eat, means *flesh together with its soul*, that is, they were not to commingle this new life, which is of the Lord, and the evil or <term>excrementitious life</term> <note>A strong term used to describe the "waste" or worthless nature of the unrefined human ego.</note>, which is of man—his voluntary principle or proprium.

### 1001.
**Blood** signifies <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is not just giving to the poor, but a fundamental spiritual love for others that flows from God.</note>, as may be abundantly shown; consequently it signifies the new voluntary principle which the regenerate spiritual man receives from the Lord. This new voluntary principle is the same as charity, inasmuch as the new will is formed of charity; for charity or love is the very essential or life of the will, since no one can with any degree of propriety say that he wills any thing, unless he has an affection for or loves it; when a person is said to think any thing, he does not will it, unless to will is present in his thought. This new will, which is of charity, is what is here typified by *blood*, and it is not man's but the Lord's in him; therefore being of the Lord, it is on no account to be commingled with the things of man's will, which, as was observed, are so defiled. This was the reason why in the <term>representative church</term> <note>The "representative church" refers to the era of ancient Israel, where physical rituals and laws were intended to represent deeper spiritual realities.</note> it was commanded that they should not *eat flesh with its soul, or the blood*, in other words, that they should not mingle them together. *Blood*, as signifying charity, represents what is holy, and *flesh*, as signifying man's voluntary principle, what is profane; and these two being distinct from, yea, contrary to each other, the eating of *blood* was therefore forbidden. To eat *flesh with blood* then was representative of <term>profanation</term> <note>The act of treating something sacred with irreverence or mixing it with worldly, selfish motives.</note> in heaven, or the mixture of what is holy with what is profane, which could not but strike the angels with horror; for at that time all things which existed with the man of the church were changed with the angels, according to their signification in the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal text.</note>, into corresponding spiritual representations. and still more so if he acknowledges, talks of, preaches, and persuades others respecting them, and yet lives in hatred, revenge, cruelty, rapine, and adultery, confirming himself in these vices by passages of the Word, which he perverts, and thereby immerses in his filthy affections. This it is to be guilty of ***profanation*** <note>In this context, profanation refers specifically to the act of knowing spiritual truths but living a life contrary to them, effectively mixing the sacred with the profane.</note>, and this is what especially occasions man’s spiritual death, as may appear from this consideration, that in another life things *profane* and holy are altogether separate, what is *profane* being in hell, and what is sacred in heaven. When a *profane* person, therefore, enters into the other world, holy and *profane* things adhere together in every idea of his thought as they did during the life of the body, so that he cannot produce a single holy idea but something *profane* is plainly seen adhering to it; such being the perception of ideas existing in another life. 

Thus there is *profanation* apparent in every particular of his thoughts, and as heaven abhors *profanation*, he must of necessity be thrust down into hell. Scarcely any one is acquainted with the nature of <term>ideas</term> <note>In this philosophical system, "ideas" are not just abstract thoughts, but are seen as living, composite structures that form the very substance of a spirit's mind.</note>, they being regarded as distinct or uncompounded. There are nevertheless, in every idea of thought, innumerable [others] conjoined in different ways, so as to constitute a certain form, and hence a vivid representation <note>original: *picta imago*, literally a "painted image"</note> of the man himself, which is fully perceived, yea, even visibly so in another life. 

Thus, for example, when the idea of any place occurs, whether it be a country, a city, or a house, then the form and image of all that he has ever done there is produced at the same time to the sight of spirits and angels. Or if the idea of a person occurs against whom a man has entertained hatred, then whatever he has thought, spoken, or done against him, is presented at the same moment. So it is also in reference to all other ideas; for as they come into existence, all and every thing which may have been conceived and impressed on the mind in relation to them is made manifest. 

Thus, when the idea of a marriage presents itself, then, if the man be an adulterer, all the filth and obscenity, even to the very thought of adultery, present themselves, and even the false notions by which he has confirmed himself in adulteries, whether derived from sensuality, or from reasonings, or from the Word, and the mode in which he has adulterated and perverted its truth, recur. The idea of one thing, moreover, flows into that of another, and infects it, as a drop of ink cast into water obscures the whole body of that fluid; whence the spirit is known by his ideas, and wonderful to relate, there is in each of them his image, or effigy, which, when rendered visible, is so deformed that it is horrible to behold. Hence the state and image of those in the other world who have profaned what is holy, may be seen. Such *profanation* is, however, by no means chargeable on those who have believed in simplicity what is contained in the Word, notwith

1009. Verse 6. *Whoso sheddeth man's blood in the man, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.* To shed man's blood in the man is to extinguish <term>charity</term> <note>While we often think of "charity" as giving to the poor, in this work it refers to the spiritual principle of loving one's neighbor from a place of goodness.</note>; "in the man" signifies that which is present with man. *Shall his blood be shed* signifies condemnation; and *for in the image of God made he man* signifies charity, which is the <term>image of God</term> <note>The "image of God" is seen here as the human capacity to reflect divine love through selfless action.</note>.

For the life of the Lord is charity, which is not in man—man being by himself altogether filthy and profane—but it is present *with* him.

This is what the Lord teaches in the Gospel of Matthew: "You have heard that it was said by them of old time, 'You shall not kill, and whoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment'; but I say to you, that whoever is *angry* with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment" (chapter 5, verses 21, 22). 

*To be angry* here signifies to turn away from charity, and consequently to be in a state of hatred, as may be seen above in section 357. He who indulges in hatred not only lacks charity, but also offers violence to it, or *sheds blood*. In hatred, there is actual murder; this is evident because someone who hates another desires nothing more earnestly than their death, and would destroy them if not held back by outward restraints like laws or fear. Therefore, the slaying of a brother and the *shedding of his blood* is spiritually equivalent to hatred, and that hatred dominates every single thought directed against that person. 

The same applies to <term>profanation</term> <note>Profanation is the act of treating something sacred with irreverence, or specifically, acknowledging spiritual truths while living a life of secret malice.</note>. He who profanes the Word not only feels enmity toward the truth but also extinguishes or destroys it. This is clearly seen in the other world <note>The "other world" refers to the spiritual realm or the afterlife.</note> among those who have been guilty of profanation. However upright, wise, or devout they may have appeared on the outside while living in the body, in the other world they harbor the most deadly hatred toward the Lord and all the goodness of love and truths of faith. This is because these divine things are the direct opposite of the hidden hatreds, thefts, and adulteries which they masked with a holy appearance and twisted to serve their own ends. "...the house of Israel that killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or that killeth it out of the camp, and bringeth it not unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, to offer an offering unto Jehovah, before the tabernacle of Jehovah, *blood shall be imputed unto that man, he hath shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people*,” (Leviticus 17:3, 4.) To sanctify in any other place than upon the altar, which was near the tabernacle, represented <term>profanation</term> <note>The act of treating something sacred with irreverence or contempt; here, it refers to performing holy rites outside of the God-ordained order.</note>; sacrifice being a sacred rite, when performed in the camp, or out of the camp, it became profaned.

1011. *Shall his blood be shed*, signifies his condemnation, as is manifest from what has been previously stated. The literal sense suggests the idea that the shedder of blood, or the murderer, should be punished with death; but the internal sense <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</note> is that he who bears hatred against his neighbor is by that very hatred condemned to death, or, in other words, to hell, as the Lord also teaches in Matthew: “Whosoever shall say to his brother, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire,” (5:22.) When <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is not merely giving to the poor, but the spiritual state of loving one's neighbor from a heart of goodness.</note> is extinguished, man is left to himself and his <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: "proprium." This refers to the human ego or the natural self that believes it is independent of God.</note>, being no longer governed by the Lord by means of internal bonds—which are of conscience—but by external bonds, which are of human law, and which man frames for himself that he may become rich and powerful. When those bonds, therefore, become loosened—as in the other world <note>The spiritual world or the afterlife.</note>—he plunges into every act of unleavened cruelty and obscenity, and consequently into his own condemnation. *That the shedder of blood should have his blood shed*, is a law of retaliation with which the ancients were well acquainted, and according to which they judged crimes and misdemeanors, as is demonstrable from many parts of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>. This law has its origin in the universal law, that no one should do to another what he would not wish another to do to him, (Matthew 7:12;) and also in this circumstance, that according to the general order which prevails in the other world, evil and falsity punish themselves, so that in them is formed their own punishment; every evil person running into that answering to his evil, as is here signified by the words, Whoso sheddeth blood, shall have his blood shed, that is, will fall headlong into condemnation.

1012. The literal sense of the words, *Whoso sheddeth man's blood in the man, his blood shall be shed*, is, that [thus it shall be done to him] who sheds another's blood; in the internal sense, however, it does not mean [the destruction] of another, but his own charity; wherefore it is also said, *the blood of man in the man*. Sometimes when the literal sense treats of two, the internal sense speaks of one only. The internal man is *man in the man*, therefore whosoever extinguishes charity—which is of the internal man, or rather the internal man himself—*his blood shall be shed*, that is, he is self-condemned.

# GENESIS. [CHAPTER 9]

1013. *For in the image of God made he man*, signifies <term>charity</term> <note>In these writings, "charity" is not just giving to the poor, but the spiritual state of loving one's neighbor and acting from a heart of goodness.</note>, which is the *image of God*, as follows of consequence. The subject treated of just above was charity, represented by blood, and that it should not be extinguished, was signified by the injunction, that blood ought not to be shed; now follows a declaration that *in the image of God made he man*, from which it is evident that *charity is the image of God*. 

It is scarcely known to any in the present day what is meant by the *image of God*; the common notion being that *God's image* was destroyed in the first man in whom it existed, whom they call Adam, and that it consisted of a certain integrity of which they are ignorant. It is true, there was integrity, for by Adam, or man, is meant the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>This refers to the very first era of human spiritual history, which the author describes as being in a state of direct, loving connection with the Divine.</note>, which was a <term>celestial man</term> <note>A "celestial" person is one who is motivated by pure love for the Lord, acting from the heart rather than just from rules or knowledge.</note>, and had perception, such as no church has since enjoyed, wherefore also it was a *likeness of the Lord*; a <term>likeness of the Lord</term> <note>original: "similitudo." A "likeness" represents a deeper, more internal union with God through the will and love, whereas an "image" is more a reflection through the intellect and neighborly love.</note> consisting in love towards him. 

After this church had, in process of time, perished, then the Lord created a new church, which was not a <term>celestial</term> but a <term>spiritual church</term> <note>A "spiritual" church or person is one who connects to God through the understanding of truth and the practice of neighborly love (charity), rather than through the direct, intuitive love of the "celestial" state.</note>; and not a *likeness* but *an image of the Lord*; *an image* denoting spiritual love, that is, neighborly love or charity, as was also shown above, numbers 50, 51. That this church, by virtue of spiritual love or charity, was *an image of the Lord*, appears from the present verse; and that charity itself *is an image of the Lord*, from its being said, *for in the image of God made he man*, signifying that charity itself made him such. 

That charity is an image of God, is most clearly evident from the very essence of love or charity; for nothing but love and charity can make a *likeness* or *an image* of any one; it being the essence of love and charity out of two to make as it were a one. When one person loves another as himself, yea more than himself, then he sees the other in himself, and himself in the other, as may be known to any one if he only attends to the nature of love, or to those who love mutually; for the will of the one is the will of the other, they being, as it were, interiorly conjoined, and only distinct from each other as to the body. Love towards the Lord makes man one with the Lord, as *a likeness*; and charity, or neighborly love, makes man one with the Lord, but as *an image*; *an image not being a likeness, but resembling it*. This oneness arising from love is thus described by the Lord himself in John:

> "I pray—that they all may be one, as thou, Father, [art] in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them, that they may be one, even as we are one, I in them, and thou in me," (17:20—23.)

This oneness is that <term>mystical union</term> <note>A term used by theologians to describe the spiritual joining of the human soul with the Divine.</note> spoken of by some which is effected by love alone. Again: 

> "Because I live ye shall live also. At that day ye shall know that I am in the Father, and ye in me, and I in you. He that hath my commandments and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.—If a man love me, he will keep my"

1019. Verse 8. *And God said to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying*, signifies the truth of what follows concerning the spiritual church, understood by Noah and his sons with him.

1020. ...no <term>knowledges</term> <note>original: *cognitiones*; here referring to specific spiritual facts or teachings learned from scripture.</note> of <term>faith</term> <note>The set of beliefs and the trust one has in the Divine.</note>, and being therefore altogether ignorant of the Lord, insisting that without <term>faith</term>, and a knowledge of the Lord, there is no <term>salvation</term> <note>The process of being saved from spiritual death and brought into a state of heavenly happiness.</note>; and thus condemning all who are out of the church. said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them—Ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. And behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last,” (Luke 13:23, 28—30.) By *Abraham, Isaac*, and *Jacob*, are here meant all who are <term>principled in love</term> <note>To be "principled in love" means that a person's entire life and character are motivated by genuine love for God and their neighbor, rather than by selfish rules.</note>, as has been previously demonstrated.

1033. We remarked that the gentiles are endowed with a conscience of what is right and good, according to their religious principles, and may here further observe, that conscience in general is either *true, spurious*, or *false*. A <term>true conscience</term> <note>A genuine internal sense of right and wrong that is built upon actual spiritual truths provided by the Divine.</note> is formed by the Lord from the <term>truths of faith</term> <note>These are the foundational spiritual principles or laws that a person accepts as true and uses to guide their life.</note> ; and when a man is endued with it, he becomes fearful of acting contrary to them, since he would thus act contrary to his conscience. This conscience can only be received by those who are in the truths of faith ; in consequence of which many in the Christian world cannot be receptive of it, because every one regards his own tenets as the truths of faith ; nevertheless all who are <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth where a person's character is transformed from selfish to selfless by the Divine.</note> receive *conscience* when they receive <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is the active love of one's neighbor and the desire to do what is good for others.</note>, for charity is the fundamental of conscience. A <term>spurious conscience</term> <note>An "off-shoot" or secondary form of conscience; it is sincere but based on traditions or upbringing rather than universal spiritual truths.</note> is that which is formed with the gentiles out of the religious principles in which they are born and educated, to act contrary to which is to act in opposition to conscience. When this conscience is founded on charity, mercy, and obedience, then they are in such a state as to be capable of receiving in the other world a *true conscience*, with which indeed they are endowed, because they love nothing better than the truth of faith. A <term>false conscience</term> is one formed not from internal but from external considerations, that is, not from charity but from self love and the love of the world. There are some persons who feel themselves acting contrary to conscience when acting in opposition to the love of their neighbor, and who at such times appear to themselves to be inwardly tormented. The reason of this is, however, because they perceive their own life, honor, reputation, wealth, or gain are endangered, and thus that they themselves are injured by it. Some receive hereditarily a tender-heartedness of this kind, and others acquire it by habit ; but it is a *false conscience*.

1034. *And all flesh shall not be cut off any more by the waters of a flood*, signifies that they should not again perish like the posterity of the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>According to the author, this refers to the very first era of humanity, which was characterized by a direct, intuitive connection to God that was eventually lost.</note>, as is evident from what was stated above respecting the <term>antediluvians</term> <note>Literally "those who lived before the flood."</note> who were thus destroyed at the deluge. It has been previously shown, n. 310, that this occurred in consequence of the latest descendants of the Most Ancient Church being of such a nature, that when their <term>will</term> <note>The part of the human mind that drives desires, intentions, and loves.</note> became corrupt their <term>intellectual principle</term> <note>The faculty of the mind used for reasoning, understanding, and logic.</note> fell into the same state, so that with them the latter could not be sepa <note>The word "separated" is continued on the next page.</note>
