for the sake of <term>conjunction</term> <note>A spiritual joining together, much like a marriage bond.</note>, so that the parties may live in mutual friendship or love; hence marriage is also called a **covenant**. This joining of the Lord with man is not possible except through love and <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, "charity" refers to the active practice of goodwill and loving one's neighbor, rather than just donating money.</note>; for the Lord is essential love and mercy. He desires to save everyone and, with a mighty arm, to draw them to heaven—that is, to Himself. 

From this, everyone can know and be convinced that it is impossible for anyone to be joined with the Lord except through that which He is—that is, unless a person becomes similar to Him, or "makes one" with Him. In other words, one must return the Lord's love and love their neighbor as themselves. This alone effects the joining, which is the very essence of a covenant; and when such a connection takes place, it follows clearly that the Lord is present. The Lord is indeed present with every person, but He is closer or more distant depending on how much—or how little—that person lives in love. 

Because a covenant is the Lord’s union with man through love—or what amounts to the same thing, the Lord’s presence with man in love and charity—it is therefore called in the Word a **covenant of peace**. This is because "peace" signifies the kingdom of the Lord, and His kingdom consists of mutual love, which is the only place where true peace exists. Thus it is written in Isaiah: 

> "The mountains shall depart and the hills be removed, but my mercy shall not depart from thee, neither shall the **covenant of my peace** <note>Original Latin: *foedus pacis*.</note> be removed, saith Jehovah that hath mercy on thee" (liv. 10); 

In this passage, "mercy" (which comes from love) is called the **covenant of peace**. Similarly, in Ezekiel: 

> "I will set up one shepherd over them, my servant David, and he shall feed them; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd—and I will make with them **a covenant of peace**" (xxxiv. 23, 25); 

Here, by **David**, the text clearly means the Lord <note>In spiritual interpretation, "David" often represents the Lord Jesus Christ as the Divine King or Shepherd.</note>. The Lord's presence with a <term>regenerate</term> <note>A "regenerate" person is one who has been spiritually reborn or transformed by following God's truths.</note> person is described here as "feeding them." Again, in the same prophet: 

> "David my servant shall be king over them, and they all shall have one shepherd. —Moreover I will make a **covenant of peace** with them, it shall be an **everlasting covenant** with them, and I will place them, and cause them to be multiplied, and will set **my sanctuary in the midst of them** for evermore. —And I will be **their God, and they shall be my people**" (xxxvii. 24, 26, 27). 

Here, likewise, **David** means the Lord; the **sanctuary in the midst of them** means love; and **being their God, and they his people** means the presence and joining of the Lord in love. This is called a **covenant of peace** and an **everlasting covenant**. 

In Malachi: 

> "Ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith Jehovah of hosts. **My covenant was with him of lives and of peace**, and I gave them to him with fear, and he shall fear me" (ii. 4, 5). 

In its highest sense, **Levi** <note>Levi was one of the sons of Jacob and the ancestor of the priestly tribe; symbolically, he represents the principle of love.</note> signifies the Lord, and consequently, it refers to any person who lives according to the principles of love and charity. A covenant, or conjunction, was not only effected by the laws or commandments of love, but also by the laws of society in the Jewish Church enacted by the Lord, which are called <term>testimonies</term>, and by the ceremonies which he enjoined, denominated <term>statutes</term>. All of these are said to belong to the covenant, because they relate to love and charity: hence it is written concerning Josiah, “The king stood upon a pillar, and *made a covenant before Jehovah, to walk after Jehovah, and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all the heart, and with all the soul, to perform the words of this covenant*,” (2 Kings 23:3.) 

Hence we see what a covenant is, and that it is internal; for the conjunction of the Lord with man is effected by internals, and not by externals separate from internals; externals are only types and <term>representatives</term> <note>Outward symbols or actions that mirror a deeper spiritual reality.</note> of what is internal, as the act of a man is a representative type of his thought and will, and as a work of charity is a representative type of the charity within, in the soul and mind. Thus all the ceremonies of the Jewish Church were types representative of the Lord, and consequently of love and charity, and of whatever is thence derived; and the covenant and conjunction are effected with the internals of man, external things being only what they are denominated—**tokens of the covenant**. That a covenant or conjunction takes place internally is plain from the Word; as from Jeremiah: “Behold the days are coming, saith Jehovah, that I will make a *new covenant* with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah; not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers—which my cove-

That externals do not constitute the covenant, unless what is internal be adjoined to them—so as that both together act as one and the same cause—but that they are <term>tokens of a covenant</term> <note>Visible signs or physical symbols that represent a deeper spiritual agreement.</note>, by which, as by representative types, the Lord might be kept in remembrance, appears from this consideration, that the sabbath and circumcision are called *tokens of the covenant*. 

That the sabbath is so called is evident from Moses: "*The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath, throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. For a similar reason blood is called the *blood of the covenant*, (Exod. xxiv. 7, 8;) and external rites more particularly were denominated *signs of the covenant*, because they were the mementos of the interior things which they signified, as were all the rites of the Jewish Church. 

Hence whatever suggested the remembrance of interior things was called a *sign*, as the binding of the first commandment on the hand and on the forehead in Moses: "*Thou shalt love Jehovah thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might; and these words—thou shalt bind for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be as <term>frontlets</term> <note>Small leather cases containing scriptural texts, traditionally worn on the forehead during prayer; also called phylacteries.</note> between thine eyes,*" (Deut. vi. 5, 6, 8; also xi. 13, 18.) Here the *hand*, as denoting power, represents the will—power being derived from the will—and *frontlets between the eyes* the understanding. 

Thus the *sign* was a memento of the first commandment, or of the sum of the law, that it might be continually in the will and in the thought, or, in other words, that the Lord and his love might be present in every desire and in every thought. Such is the presence of the Lord, and the mutual love derived from him, with the angels, the mode and nature of which will be more fully treated of, by the divine mercy of the Lord, in the following pages. So likewise here, where it is said, *This is the token of the covenant which I give between me and you. I have given my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of the covenant between me and the earth;* a token is no other than a symbol of the Lord's presence in <term>charity</term> <note>In this theological context, "charity" refers to active, spiritual love for one's neighbor, rather than just financial aid.</note>, thus it is a memento for man. Thus, for example, he who is of a haughty disposition, is haughty in every effort of his will, and in every particular idea of his thought. So, in like manner, a covetous person is influenced by covetousness; a hater of his neighbor, by hatred; a stupid man, by stupidity; and an insane one, by insanity; and this being the case, every man's quality is known in the other world, even from a single idea of thought. 1041. **Into the generations of the age**, signifies all who are created anew <note>This refers to the process of spiritual rebirth, or regeneration.</note> for ever, as is manifest from the signification of the **generations of the age**. Generations are the posterities derived from their predecessors and from their parents, as the age is what is perpetual. As it here treats of that which is regenerate, therefore by the **generations of the age** are meant those who are thence perpetually regenerated, or created anew; for every thing in the internal sense <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note> is predicated in reference to the subject treated of.

1042. **I have given my bow in the cloud**, signifies the state of the regenerate spiritual man, who is like a *rainbow*. It may appear surprising that a token of the covenant <note>A "covenant" is a spiritual agreement or conjunction between God and humanity.</note> in the Word should be a bow in the cloud, or a *rainbow*, since this is produced by the modification which the solar rays undergo when falling upon drops of rain, and, unlike the other signs of the covenant in the church, mentioned above, is a purely natural phenomenon. That it does, however, represent regeneration, and denote the state of the regenerate spiritual man, can only be known by those who are permitted to see, and thereby to know the reason of it. The spiritual angels, who have all been men of the spiritual church made regenerate, when presented to view in another life, have an appearance about the head like a *rainbow*; and as these *rainbows* agree perfectly with the state of the angels, their quality is hence discernible in heaven and the world of spirits. The cause of this rainbow-like appearance is, that their natural things corresponding with their spiritual present this appearance, it being a modification of spiritual light from the Lord in their natural things. It is these angels who are said to be born again *of water and the spirit*, whereas the celestial angels are regenerated *by fire*. It may be observed, that for the production of natural color there must necessarily be a ground which either absorbs or reflects the rays of light from the sun, or which is, in other words, either black or white. Now according to the various conditions of this ground as to absorbing or reflecting power, or, as it is termed, as to blackness or whiteness, is that modification of the inflowing rays of light, which gives rise to colors, some of which partake more or less of the obscure or black property, and others more or less of the shining or white property, and hence arises their diversity. So it is comparatively in spiritual things; for the obscurity resembles man’s <term>intellectual-proprium</term> <note>The "intellectual selfhood": the part of a person's identity shaped by their own thoughts and understanding, which can be prone to error or "the false."</note>, or *the false*; and the blackness his <term>voluntary-proprium</term> <note>The "voluntary selfhood": the part of a person's identity rooted in their own will and desires, which can be prone to selfish motives or "the evil."</note>, or *the evil*, which absorbs and extinguishes the rays of light. And the bright and white property is the *truth and good* which man thinks to do of himself, which reflects and rejects from itself the rays of light. These rays which fall thereon, and as it were modify them, are from the Lord—the

It is from the correspondence of natural things with spiritual, that when in the other world this is visible about the regenerate <note>Regeneration refers to the process of spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note> spiritual man, there is an appearance as of *a bow in a cloud*, the *bow* being a representation of what is spiritual in what is natural. The regenerate spiritual man has an intellectual <term>proprium (a sense of self or what belongs to the individual)</term>, into which the Lord insinuates innocence, charity, and mercy, and as these gifts are received by him, his *rainbow* when presented to view appears more beautiful in proportion as his *will-proprium* <note>The "will-proprium" refers to the person's natural, often selfish, desires and impulses.</note> is more removed, subdued, and reduced to obedience. The prophets also, whilst they were in the vision of God, saw an appearance as of a bow in a cloud; for we read in Ezekiel: "Above the expanse, which was over their heads [those of the cherubim], was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone,—and the likeness as the appearance of a man upon it. And I saw as it were the appearance of a burning coal, as the appearance of fire, round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward; and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about. As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Jehovah," (Ezekiel i. 26—28.) It must be manifest to every one, that it was the Lord who thus appeared, and also that by him was represented heaven, for he is heaven, or the All in All therein, and the man there spoken of. *The throne is heaven; the burning coal as the appearance of fire from the loins upward, the celestial principle of love; and the brightness of fire round about from the loins downward as the bow in the cloud, the celestial spiritual principle.* Thus the celestial heaven, or the heaven of the celestial angels, was represented from the loins upward, and the spiritual heaven, or the heaven of the spiritual angels, from the loins downward; for what is beneath the loins, through the feet to their very soles, in the <term>Greatest Man</term> <note>The "Greatest Man" (Latin: *Maximus Homo*) is a theological concept where the entirety of heaven is structured like a single human body, with different communities of angels corresponding to specific organs or limbs.</note> signifies natural things. Hence also it is evident, that what is natural in man—thus enlightened by spiritual light from the Lord—appears like *a bow in the cloud*. A similar appearance was also seen by John, (Rev. iv. 2, 3; x. 1.)

So also it is with the spiritual man; the obscure medium surrounding him—here called a cloud—being falsity, or, what is

This is a certain spiritual modification which can never be [fully] described, and unless the colors themselves and their mode of formation are perceived by man, I question whether it is possible to explain it to his understanding. 

The nature of this *cloud* with the <term>regenerate (spiritually reborn)</term> man, may be discovered from his state prior to that process. Man is <term>regenerated</term> by the means of what he conceives to be the truths of faith; for every one supposes his own religious beliefs to be true, and from this receives conscience; and after he has received conscience, to act contrary to what he is convinced are the truths of faith, is for him to act contrary to conscience. Such is every regenerate person: for many are regenerated by the Lord, of every religious opinion, and when they become so, they do not receive any immediate revelation, except what is breathed into them by the <term>Word (the Scriptures)</term> and the preaching of the Word. As, however, they receive charity <note>"Charity" here refers to active spiritual love for others.</note>, the Lord by it operates on their cloud, producing light similar to that caused by the sun's rays hitting a *cloud*, by which it is rendered more bright, and becomes varied with colors, and is thus rendered like a *rainbow*. In proportion, therefore, to the thinness of the *cloud*—that is, in proportion to the number of the truths of faith mixed with its other components—is *the bow beautiful*; and in proportion to its density—that is, to the fewness of the truths of faith of which it consists—is the beauty of the bow diminished;—innocence adds greatly to its beauty, by causing as it were a lively brightness in the colors. 

All the appearances of truth in which a man rests whilst he stays in the literal sense of the Word, are *clouds*, for the Word is expressed according to appearances, and when a man believes it in simplicity, and has charity, despite the fact he rests in appearances, this *cloud* is comparatively of little density. In this *cloud*, with the man who is within the church <note>The "church" refers to those who possess the Word (the Bible).</note>, conscience is formed by the Lord. All deficiencies of knowledge as to truth are also *clouds*, in which the man stays who is ignorant of the truths of faith of the Word in general, and especially of the Lord; and in this *cloud* conscience is formed by the Lord with the man who is out of the church; for in ignorance itself there may be innocence, and thereby charity. All falsities also are *clouds*, and these are the *thick clouds* accompanying both those who have a false conscience—spoken of above—and those who have no conscience. These are in general the *qualities of clouds*; and it may be observed in reference to their quantity, that there are with man clouds so large and so dense, that, were he aware of them, he would wonder how the rays of light from the Lord could ever pass...

Such are the *clouds* abiding with the <term>spiritual man (one who is guided by truths and conscience)</term>; but with the <term>celestial man (one who is guided by love and intuition)</term> they are not so large, because he is grounded in love towards the Lord. Because this love is implanted in his <term>voluntary principle (the faculty of the will)</term>, he does not receive conscience like the spiritual man, but rather the perception of goodness, and through that, the perception of truth from the Lord. 

When the will of man is capable of receiving the rays of celestial flame in this way, his <term>intellectual principle (the faculty of the understanding)</term> is enlightened as a result; for from love he knows and perceives all the truths of faith. In this case, his will is like a little sun, from which rays flow into his understanding. Such was the state of the people of the <term>Most Ancient Church (the earliest state of human innocence)</term>. 

When, however, man's will becomes altogether corrupt and hellish, a new will—which is conscience—is formed instead in his intellectual part. This occurred with the people of the <term>Ancient Church (the spiritual state following the decline of the first church)</term>, and indeed occurs with every <term>regenerate</term> person of the spiritual Church. In these cases, there is a dense *cloud*, because the person must necessarily learn what is true and good through study, having no internal perception of whether a thing is true or not. Here also there is a continual flow of the false, which creates the darkness of the *cloud*. This darkness comes from his "black" will—or rather, through that will from hell—which is why the understanding cannot be enlightened in the spiritual man in the same way it is in the celestial man. Hence, in this passage, a *cloud* signifies the relative obscurity of the light in which the spiritual man lives compared to the celestial man.

### 1044.
*And it shall be for a token of the covenant between me and the earth*, is an evidence of the Lord's presence in <term>charity (spiritual love in action)</term>, as can be shown from what was said above; and that *the earth* here signifies man's <term>selfhood (his inherent nature)</term> <note>original: "proprium"</note> is clear from the internal meaning and the sequence of the subjects discussed. 

It was previously stated, *This is the token of the covenant—between me and you, and every living soul which is with you*, which represents whatever is being reborn; but here the expression is changed to *it shall be for a token of the covenant between me and the earth*. From this change, and the repetition of the phrase *the token of the covenant*, it is plain that something else is signified. Here, *the earth* represents that which is neither reborn nor capable of being reborn: man's <term>voluntary selfhood (the inherent, selfish will)</term> <note>original: "voluntary proprium"</note>. The reborn man—in his intellectual part—belongs to the Lord, but in his will, he belongs to himself. These two principles are opposed to each other in the spiritual man. However, the will of man must necessarily exist despite its opposition; for all the obscurity in his understanding, and the density of his *cloud*, originates from that will.

Now in proportion as the Lord is present in heaven, is hell removed; for of himself man is in hell, but of the Lord he is in heaven; and he is continually elevated from the former into the latter, his hell being removed in the same proportion as he is elevated. The *token or sign*, therefore, of the Lord’s presence, is the removal of man’s will-<term>proprium</term>, which is effected by <term>temptations</term> <note>spiritual trials or inner conflicts</note>, and various other means of regeneration.

1045. The passages already explained regard the regenerate spiritual man, or the spiritual church, but what now follows relates to man in general. The man who is capable of being regenerated is subsequently specifically referred to.

1046. Verses 14, 15. *And it shall be in beclouding myself with a cloud over the earth, and the bow is seen in the cloud, that I will remember my covenant which is between me and you and every living soul in all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.* And it shall be in beclouding myself with a cloud over the earth, signifies, when by reason of man’s *voluntary-<term>proprium</term>*, the faith of charity does not appear; and the bow is seen in the cloud, although he is capable of being regenerated; that *I will remember my covenant which is between me and you*, signifies the Lord’s mercy, especially towards the regenerate, and those who are capable of regeneration; *and every living soul in all flesh*, is the whole human race. *And the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh*, signifies that man’s intellectual principle should not again be capable of imbibing such a persuasion as to cause it to perish like the posterity of the Most Ancient Church. These statements are general, and regard all men.

1047\. ***And it shall be in beclouding myself with a cloud over the earth***, signifies when the influence of man's ***<term>voluntary-proprium</term>*** <note>The "selfhood of the will," referring to the core of human desires and ego</note> prevents the faith of charity from appearing, as is evident from what was observed just before respecting ***the earth***, or man's ***voluntary-proprium***, being of such a nature as to be continually infusing into his intellectual part what is obscure, or false, by which it is ***beclouded***, and made to give birth to every falsity. This may be seen plainly enough from this consideration, that self-love and the love of the world, which are of man's will, are nothing but hatred, since in proportion as any one loves himself he hates his neighbor, and as these loves are utterly opposed to heavenly love, there must necessarily be a continual influx thence of what is contrary to mutual love, which in the intellectual principle becomes falsities, and hence the obscurity and darkness therein. The false beclouds the true, as a thick ***cloud*** does the light of the sun; and as the false and the true cannot abide together—any more than darkness and light—it hence manifestly follows that one must retire as the other approaches. Now as this takes place alternately, it is therefore here said, ***in the beclouding with a cloud the earth***, that is, when man's ***voluntary-proprium*** obscures the faith of charity, or the true and the good thence derived, and still more, the good and the true derived from it.

1048\. ***And the bow is seen in the cloud***, signifies although man is still capable of regeneration <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new</note>, as is evident from ***a bow in the cloud*** being a token or symbol of regeneration, as was previously demonstrated. With respect to ***the bow in the cloud***, it may be observed that man's quality—or that of the soul after the death of the body—is known immediately by the Lord; it is indeed known from eternity, and what it will be to eternity; but even the angels instantly perceive on the soul's first arrival into the other world what he is, in consequence of there being a kind of sphere <note>An "aura" or spiritual atmosphere emanating from a person's true character</note> exhaling as it were from his disposition, or from each particular of his mind. This sphere, wonderful as it may seem, is of such a nature, that it is thence perceived in what faith and what charity he is principled; for when it seems good unto the Lord, it becomes visible in the form of a bow;—but of this, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said hereafter. Hence it is evident that by ***the bow being seen in the cloud***, is here meant that man is capable of ***regeneration***.

1050\. ***And every living soul in all flesh*** is the whole human race, as is proved by the signification of the expressions. This germ of innocence, charity, and mercy, man receives from the Lord during infancy and childhood, as may be seen from the states of infants and children. What man then receives is treasured up within him, and is called in the Word the ***remnant*** or ***remains***, <note>These "remains" refer to the spiritual qualities of goodness and truth stored in a person's inner mind by God during childhood, which serve as the foundation for their later spiritual life.</note> which are of the Lord alone with man, and furnish him with the capacity of becoming truly man on his arrival at adult age; but more may be seen on this subject above, n. 468, 530, 560—563, 576. That the states of innocence, charity, and mercy, which man passed through during infancy and childhood, enable him to become a man, is evident from this consideration, that, unlike the brutes, he is not born into any exercise of life, but has all and every thing to learn, and what he learns become by use habitual, and thus as it were natural to him. He cannot even walk or speak unless he be taught, and so with all the other actions, which habit renders as it were natural to him. So it is also with states of innocence, charity, and mercy, with which he likewise becomes imbued in infancy, and unless these were present with him he would be far viler than the brute. These states, however, are not learned by man, but received as a gift from the Lord, by whom they are preserved in him; and these, together with the truths of faith, are what are called ***remains***, which are of the Lord alone. In proportion as man in adult age extinguishes these states, he becomes dead; and when about to be regenerated, these constitute the rudiments of that process, he being led into them by the Lord, who, as was observed, operates by remains. These ***remains*** with every man are what are here called ***every living soul in all flesh***. 1054. ***And I see it***, signifies that it is such as to admit of his **<term>regeneration</term>** <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new by God.</note>, as is manifest from this consideration, that when the Lord is said to *see* any one it means that he knows his quality; for the Lord knows all from eternity, and has no need to see what they are. When man's state is such as to admit of **regeneration**, the Lord is said to see him, and to lift up his countenance upon him; but when he cannot be **regenerated**, then the Lord is no longer said to *see*, or to *lift up his countenance upon him*, but to turn away his eyes or his countenance, although it is not the Lord who averts himself, but man. On this account, when previously treating of the whole human race, of whom many are incapable of **regeneration**, it is not there said, *I see the bow in the cloud*, but, when the bow *is seen in the cloud*, (verse 14.) *To see*, when predicated of the Lord, is the same as to remember, and denotes, in the **<term>internal sense</term>** <note>The deeper spiritual meaning of the Scripture that lies beneath the literal stories.</note>, to be merciful, as was shown above, n. 840, 1049; see also what was said, n. 626.

1055. That ***I will remember the everlasting <term>covenant</term>*** <note>A holy agreement or spiritual connection between the Divine and humanity.</note>, signifies that the Lord may be present with man in **charity**, as is evident from what has been previously asserted and demonstrated respecting the meaning of a **<term>covenant</term>**, of which no other can be said to be *everlasting* than that of love towards the Lord and the neighbor, which is *everlasting* because it endures from eternity to eternity. The universal heaven is founded upon love, and indeed all nature is so likewise, for nothing of union or conjunction exists in nature, whether it be animate or inanimate, which does not derive its origin from love. All that is natural exists from what is **spiritual**, and the **spiritual** from what is **<term>celestial</term>** <note>The highest level of existence, relating to pure love and the heart, as opposed to the "spiritual" which relates to truth and the intellect.</note>, as was previously observed, and hence love, or something like it, is implanted in all things both in general, and in particular. With man alone there is not love, but its contrary, he having destroyed the order of nature in himself. When, however, he is capable of **regeneration**, or of being again restored to order, and of receiving **mutual love**, then there is a **<term>covenant</term>** or conjunction effected by **charity**, of which it here treats.

1056. ***Between God and every living soul in all flesh which is upon the earth***, denotes with every man who is capable of receiving it, as is proved by the fact stated above, that it here treats of those who are capable of **regeneration**, represented by *every living soul in all flesh*.

1059. ***This is the token of the covenant, which I establish between me and all flesh that is upon the earth***, signifies that there should be evidence of the Lord’s presence in **charity**, not only with the man of the church, but also with him who is out of the church, as is demonstrable from the signification of *all flesh*, being every man, and consequently the whole human race. The Lord is equally present in **charity** with those who are out of the church, and are denominated **<term>gentiles</term>** <note>A term used here to describe people who are not part of the Judeo-Christian religious tradition but who live good, moral lives.</note>, as with those who are within the church, as may be seen above, n. 932, 1032. With Christians, however, there is a cloud in opposition to the Lord and the truths of faith, which is so dense as to occasion darkness, and then hatred occupies the place of **charity**, thick darkness. It is still worse with those who profane the truths of faith, which the **gentiles** cannot do, in consequence of their ignorance of them, for no one can profane that of whose quality and existence he is unconscious. This is the reason why more **gentiles** are saved than Christians, as the Lord has declared, (Luke thirteen: twenty-three, twenty-eight, twenty-nine, thirty;) and further, that all their infants are of the Lord’s kingdom, (Matthew eighteen: ten, fourteen; nineteen: fourteen; Luke eighteen: sixteen.)

1061. The sons of Noah who left the ark represent the people who formed the **<term>Ancient Church</term>** <note>A historical-spiritual era described in these writings as existing after the Flood, characterized by symbolic worship.</note>. Those "going forth from the ark" are the regenerated, as is proven by the stories that follow, which will make this meaning clear.

1062. The fact that *Shem* signifies the internal church, *Ham* the corrupted church, and *Japheth* the external church will also become clear as their specific characters and qualities are described. In the Ancient Church—just as in every church—there were three types of people: those who were internal, those who were "corruptly" internal, and those who were external.
*   The **internal** people make **<term>charity</term>** <note>Spiritual love and goodwill toward others.</note> the most important part of their **<term>faith</term>** <note>Intellectual belief or religious conviction.</note>.
*   The **corruptly internal** people make faith the most important thing, but they leave out charity.
*   The **external** people do not think much about the inner, spiritual man, but they still do good works and respectfully follow the ceremonies and rites of the church.

Aside from these three, no one can truly be called a member of the spiritual church. Because all three groups belonged to it, they are all said to have "gone forth from the ark." The internal members were called *Shem*. The corruptly internal, who valued faith without love, were called *Ham*. Finally, the external members, who focused on rituals and good deeds rather than deep inner reflection, were called *Japheth*. Their specific qualities are described in the verses that follow.

1063. *Ham being the father of Canaan* means that a form of worship consisting of outward rituals without inner heart arose from the corrupted church. This is symbolized by Canaan. This verse serves as an introduction to the stories that follow. That *Ham* signifies a corrupted church (or those who separate faith from love) is evident from the Book of Psalms: "He struck down all the first-born in *Egypt*, the beginning of their strength in the tents of *Ham*" (Psalm 78:51 <note>original: "lxxviii. 51"</note>). The "first-born of Egypt" represents faith without charity. In this theological system, faith is called the "first-born" of the church (as seen in sections 352 and 367), and is therefore called the "beginning of strength." This is also seen in Genesis 49:3 <note>original: "Gen. xlix. 3"</note>, where *Reuben*, the first-born of *Jacob*, represents faith and is called the "beginning of strength." 1064. The phrase "of them was the whole earth overspread" signifies that all religious teachings, whether true or false, originated from these three sources.

1065. *The three sons of Noah* represent these three universal types of doctrine found in churches. While there are countless smaller variations in teaching, there are no other "universal" kinds. This is because people who acknowledge neither charity, nor faith, nor even external worship do not belong to any church and are not discussed here; the text is specifically concerned with the nature of the church.

1066. *And of them was the whole earth overspread* indicates that all doctrines, both true and false, were derived from these sources. This becomes clear when we look at the meaning of *the earth*. In the Bible, the word *earth* (or *land*) is understood in different ways. In its broadest sense, it refers to the specific region or country where the church exists or has existed—such as *the land of Canaan*, *the land of Judah*, or *the land of Israel*. Because people live there, the word "earth" became a common way to refer to the church itself.

When ancient writers spoke of *all the earth*, they did not mean the entire physical globe. Instead, they meant only that part of the world where the church was present. This is shown in several passages from the Word <note>The "Word" is a term used here to refer to the Holy Scriptures.</note>:

1069. *His planting a vineyard* denotes that a church was thence derived, as is manifest from a *vineyard* signifying the spiritual church. In the Word, churches are often described by gardens, and the trees they contain, and are likewise so named in consequence of their fruits representing what is of love and charity; and hence man is said to be known by his fruit. Hence also the celestial church <note>The "celestial" church refers to a state of being motivated by love for the Lord, while the "spiritual" church is motivated by charity toward the neighbor and faith in the intellect.</note> was described by a paradisiacal garden, wherein were trees of every kind, which were symbols of the perceptions of that church, and its fruits of the goods of every kind which are of love. It is, however, otherwise with those who, notwithstanding their maintaining that faith alone saves, have nevertheless lived a life of charity; for their faith was influenced by charity from the Lord.

1078. *The father of Canaan signifies worship in externals without a corresponding internal, was stated above.* It is impossible for any other worship to derive existence from faith separate from charity, since the internal man is charity, and never faith without charity; and hence, whosoever is destitute of charity cannot possibly perform any other worship than that which is exclusively external <note>External worship refers to the performance of religious rituals, ceremonies, or prayers that lack a sincere inward motivation of love or faith.</note>; and as such worship derives its existence from faith separate from charity, *Ham* is therefore said to be *the father of Canaan*, and in what follows *Ham* is no longer treated of, but *Canaan*.

1079. *His seeing the nakedness of his father, denotes that he observed these erroneous and perverse opinions, as is evident from the signification of nakedness spoken of just above—and also in a former part of this work, n. 213, 214, as what is evil and perverted.* In this passage, *Ham* is the symbol of those who are principled in faith separate from charity, as is indicated by his observing the nakedness or the errors and perversities of his father, for such persons see nothing else in man. It is, however, otherwise with those whose faith originates in charity: for they observe what is good, and if they see any thing evil and false, excuse and, so far as they are able, endeavor to amend it, as is here related of Shem and Japheth. Where there is no charity, there is self-love, consequently hatred towards all who do not favor themselves; and hence such persons see nothing in their neighbor but his evils, and if they observe any good, they either regard it as nothing, or interpret it as evil; it is however, altogether otherwise with those who are in charity. By this are these two kinds of persons distinguished, more especially in the other world <note>The author uses "the other world" to refer to the spiritual world or the life after death.</note>; for then such as are not in charity manifest their disposition to hatred in all they think or do: they wish to examine every one, yea, to judge every one, and desire nothing more earnestly than to discover what is evil, continually purposing in their minds to condemn, to punish, and to torment. Those, however, who are in charity, scarcely see another's evils, but observe all that is good and true in him, and what is evil and false they interpret favorably. Such are all the angels, and this disposition they derive from the Lord, who turns all evil into good.

1080. **By his telling his two brethren** signifies that he gave in to a spirit of mockery, which follows naturally from what has been described. The only reason they do not do this openly is because they are held back by external pressures—such as the fear of the law, or losing their life, status, profit, or reputation. Consequently, they nurture these evil attitudes internally while putting on a friendly mask externally. This creates two distinct "spheres" <note>A "sphere" (original: *sphæra*) refers to the spiritual atmosphere or aura that emanates from a person's true character.</note> that are clearly felt in the afterlife: an inner one full of hatred, and an outer one that looks like goodness. Because these two atmospheres are totally at odds, they struggle against one another. When the outward mask is eventually removed in the next life and they can no longer hide, they rush into all kinds of wickedness. Even while the mask is on, their hatred can be felt lurking behind everything they say, which ultimately leads to their suffering and spiritual torment.

1081. They are called **his brethren** <note>original: "fratres"</note> because he made a public profession of faith. This is based on what was previously explained: that charity is the "brother" of faith (see section 367).

1082. Verse 23. *And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and they both laid it upon the shoulder, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness.*
By **Shem** is meant the <term>internal church</term> <note>The "internal church" refers to the inward, spiritual part of religion—the heart and soul of worship.</note>; by **Japheth**, the corresponding **external church** <note>The "external church" refers to the outward rituals, ceremonies, and formal structures of religion.</note>. **Taking a garment** means they chose to interpret things for the best; and **both laying it upon the shoulder** means they did so with all their strength. **And went backward** signifies that they chose not to focus on his errors and mistakes. **And covered the nakedness of their father** means they made excuses for him. **And their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness** signifies that this was accomplished, and that such errors or mistakes in reasoning should not be dwelt upon.

1083. As previously shown, Shem represents the internal church and Japheth the external church. Wherever a church exists, it must necessarily have both an internal and an external side, because the human being who makes up the church is both internal and external. Before a person is "reborn" <note>This refers to the process of "regeneration," or spiritual growth and development.</note>, they live in external things. While being reborn, they are led from external things—and indeed, by means of external things—into internal things. Finally, when the process is complete, everything in the internal person finds its expression in the external. Thus, every church must have both an inner and an outer life, just as the "Ancient Church" <note>A term for the spiritual era following the Flood, represented by Noah.</note> did, and as the Christian church does today. ...separate from internal things turns away from the Lord, is clear from the meaning of *Canaan*, and of *being cursed*. The Lord is as far from cursing and being angry with anyone as heaven is from earth; for who can believe it possible that He who is all-knowing and all-powerful, ruling the universe by His wisdom, and thus infinitely above all human weaknesses, can be angry with such poor and miserable dust as humans are? This faith can never be accursed, since the faith of that church—being the truth—was sacred. Although it is not "real" faith when it lacks love, it is still the means by which a person is reformed and reborn. Therefore, it can eventually be joined to love and is, in a sense, a "brother" to it. For this reason, *Canaan* was cursed, and not *Ham*. Furthermore, the inhabitants of the land of *Canaan*, including both the Jews and the Gentiles, were generally of such a nature that they made all religious worship consist of nothing but outward ceremonies. These are the <term>mysteries</term> <note>original: "arcana"</note> contained here; had there been no deeper spiritual meaning, *Canaan* would never have been substituted in the text for his father.

1095. **Verse 26. *And he said, Blessed be Jehovah the God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.*** *Blessed be Jehovah the God of Shem*, signifies all good to those who interiorly worship the Lord; *Shem* is the internal church; *and Canaan shall be his servant*, denotes that those who place worship solely in external observances, are amongst the persons capable of performing [only] vile services to the men of the church.

1096. ***Blessed be Jehovah the God of Shem***, means every good to those who worship the Lord from what is internal, as may be seen from the signification of the word *blessed*. *Blessing* implies all celestial, and spiritual, and natural good, these being typified by it in the internal sense. ...therein, whosoever and whatsoever he may be, must be productive of some use, since use alone is there regarded by the Lord. 1098. In order to show what is meant by *Shem and Japheth*, or in other words by the man of the internal and of the external church, and afterwards what is intended by *Canaan*, we will subjoin the following remarks. The man of the internal church attributes to the Lord all the good which he does, and all the truth which he thinks; but of this the man of the external church is ignorant, although he still acts rightly. The man of the internal church makes charity the essential of the worship of the Lord, and indeed regards internal worship as more important than that which is external; but the man of the external church makes external worship the essential, being ignorant what internal worship is, although he performs it. The man of the internal church believes that he acts contrary to conscience if he does not worship the Lord from an internal principle; but the man of the external church believes that he acts contrary to conscience if he does not reverently observe external rites. The conscience of the man of the internal church is more abundantly stored, because he is better acquainted with the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning hidden within the literal words of the Bible.</note> of the Word; but the conscience of the man of the external church is more sparingly supplied, he knowing less of that sense. The former, or the man of the internal church, is he who is called *Shem*; and the latter, or the man of the external church, he who is denominated *Japheth*; but he who places worship solely in externals, and is destitute of charity and consequently of conscience, is here called *Canaan*.

1099. Verse 27. *God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.* **Japheth** signifies, as established previously, the <term>corresponding external church</term> <note>The "external church" refers to people who focus on the outward rituals and visible actions of faith rather than deep abstract theology.</note>; and **God’s enlarging him** signifies his <term>illustration</term> <note>In this context, "illustration" means spiritual enlightenment or the clearing of the mind to understand divine truths.</note>; and **he shall dwell in the tents of Shem** denotes the presence of the internal aspects of worship within its external forms; and **Canaan shall be his servant** means here, as before, that those who place worship solely in outward forms can only perform menial or basic roles within the church.

1100. It has been shown previously that **Japheth** represents the corresponding external church. This includes people who participate in external worship and may be unaware of the deep complexities of the "internal man" or the soul's inner workings, but who nevertheless live a life of **charity** <note>Charity here is defined as active love and kindness toward others.</note>. The Lord is present with these individuals because He works through charity wherever it is found. This is similar to little children: though they do not understand the technical definitions of charity or faith, the Lord is more present with them than with many adults, especially if they live in mutual love. The same applies to simple-hearted people who live in innocence and mercy. It is of no benefit for a person to possess great knowledge unless they live according to it; knowledge is merely a means to reach goodness. A person who has been made good possesses a far richer treasure than a scholar who has extensive knowledge but lacks goodness. The good person already possesses the very thing the scholar is still searching for through his studies. However, it is different for the person of the **internal church**, or **Shem**, who possesses both deep truth and a life of charity and <term>conscience</term>. Those who know little but possess a true conscience are enlightened in the afterlife, even becoming angels with inexpressible wisdom—these are the ones signified by **Japheth**.

1101. Regarding the phrase **God’s enlarging Japheth**, which signifies his enlightenment: while "to enlarge" literally means to extend borders, in a spiritual sense it means to enlighten. Through enlightenment, the "boundaries" of wisdom and intelligence are expanded. We see this in the Book of Isaiah: "Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thy habitations" (Isaiah 54:2), which represents receiving light on spiritual matters. The mind of someone in the external church is "enlarged" when they are taught the truths of faith. Because they already live in charity, this instruction confirms and strengthens them. As they learn, the "cloud" over their intellect—where their charity and conscience reside—is cleared away.

Jehovah shall save the tents of Judah," (12:6, 7;) where the *tents of Judah* represent the worship of the Lord from the holy principle of love.

When a man feels or perceives in himself that he is well affected towards the Lord, and loves his neighbor, and is willing to do him all kinds of good offices, without any view to his own interest or honor, and when he feels that he has compassion for those who are in distress, and especially for such as are in error as to the doc-trines of faith, he may know that he dwells in the tents of Shem, or in other words, that he has with him internal motives by which the Lord operates.

It was also given me to apperceive the nature of their internal respiration <note>The author posits that the earliest humans breathed "internally" through a spiritual connection, rather than purely through the lungs and air as we do today.</note>: it proceeded from the navel towards the heart, and thus through the lips, without any thing sonorous, and it did not enter into the ear of another by an external way, and strike what is called the *drum of the ear*, but by a certain way within the mouth, in fact by the passage called at this day the *Eustachian tube* <note>The passage that connects the middle ear to the back of the throat.</note>. It was further shown me, that by such speech they were enabled to express more fully the sentiments of the mind, and the ideas of thought, than can possibly be done by articulate sounds, or by sonorous words, which in like manner are directed by the respiration, but such as is external: for all spoken words are entirely directed by various applications of respiration; but this, with the antediluvians <term>antediluvians: those who lived before the Great Flood of Noah</term>, was directed much more perfectly, it being done by internal respiration, and this, as being interior, is also more perfect, and more applicable and conformable to the ideas of thought. Moreover, they were able to express the mind’s meaning by slight motions of the lips, and by corresponding changes of the countenance: for being celestial men, whatsoever was the object of their thought shone forth and manifested itself from the face and eyes, which underwent a conformable variation. It was utterly impossible for them to assume an expression in the countenance which was not in agreement with their thoughts. In their days, simulation, and much more, deceit, was reckoned a crime of the greatest enormity.

1119. It was shown me to the life, how the internal respiration of the most ancient people flowed tacitly into a kind of external respiration, and thus into a tacit speech, perceived by another in his interior man. They said, that that respiration, with them, underwent variations according to the state of their love and faith towards the Lord; the reason of which they stated to be, because they had communication with heaven, and therefore it could not be otherwise; for they respired with the angels in whose company they were. The angels have a respiration, to which internal respiration corresponds, and this, with them, undergoes variations in a similar manner. For when any thing contrary to faith and love towards the Lord presents itself to them, their respiration is straitened <note>In this context, "straitened" means the breathing becomes constricted or tight due to spiritual distress.</note>;

This form of speech made deceit impossible, as their outward appearance perfectly mirrored their internal thoughts and their connection to heaven.</summary>

## THE INTERNAL SENSE.

1139. IT was before observed, that there are four different styles in the **Word** <note>The "Word" is the term used for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>. The first is that of the most ancient church, which is such as is used from the first chapter of Genesis to this chapter. The second is historical, such as is used in the following books of Moses, and in the other historical books. The third is prophetical. The fourth is a middle style between the prophetical and that of common discourse. Concerning these styles, see n. 66.

1140. In this chapter and in the following, even to the account of Heber, the most ancient style is continued; but it here becomes a middle style between the style which consists of relations constructed in the historical form merely, and the style which consists of true historical relations. <note>The author suggests that the earliest chapters of Genesis are allegorical stories written in a "historical form," whereas later chapters describe actual historical events.</note> For by Noah, and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and Canaan, nothing else was or is meant, than the ancient church, abstractedly, as to its worship. By Shem is meant internal worship; by Japheth, corresponding external worship; by Ham, internal worship corrupted; by Canaan, external worship separate from internal. Such persons never had any existence, but those kinds of worship had such names given them, because all other different kinds, or all specific differences, might be reduced to those as fundamentals. By Noah, then, nothing else was meant but the ancient church in general, comprehending,

(videlicet)</note>, different kinds of worship. It is by virtue of the internal sense that the Word of the Lord lives, this sense being like the soul, of which the external sense is as it were the body. The case with the Word is like that of man: when his body dies, his soul lives, and when the soul lives he is no longer acquainted with the things that relate to the body: thus when he enters the society of angels, he knows not what the Word is in its literal sense, but only what it is in its soul. Such was the man of the most ancient church <note>The "most ancient church" refers to the earliest spiritual era of humanity, characterized by an intuitive, direct connection to the Divine rather than a reliance on written scripture.</note>: were one of them living at this day on earth, and were he to read the Word, he would not at all remain in the sense of the letter, but it would be to him as if he did not see it; he would perceive only the internal abstracted from the letter, and this in such a manner as if the letter had no existence; thus he would dwell in the life or soul of the Word. The case is the same with every part of the Word, even with the historical parts, the particulars recorded in which actually occurred just as they are related; notwithstanding which they do not contain the minutest word, which does not, in the internal sense, involve <term>secrets</term> <note>original: "arcana," meaning deep spiritual mysteries or hidden truths within the scripture that are not visible to a casual reader.</note>, which never become apparent to those who keep their attention

### 1144. Verse 1.
*And these are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them were sons born after the flood.*

"These are the generations of the sons of Noah" signifies the branching out of the doctrines and worship of the ancient church, which is represented here by the figure of Noah. Shem, Ham, and Japheth have the same meaning here as they did previously: Shem signifies true internal worship; Ham signifies corrupt internal worship; and Japheth signifies external worship that matches the internal. By "sons being born to them" are signified the <term>doctrinals</term> derived from those three types of worship. "After the flood" signifies the period of time starting from the beginning of this new church.

### 1145.
The fact that the "generations of the sons of Noah" signify the branching out of the teachings and worship of the ancient church (Noah) is clear from the meaning of "generations" (or births). In the literal or historical sense, generations are simply the family line of one person descending from another; but in the internal sense, they all relate to celestial and spiritual matters—specifically things belonging to charity and faith. Consequently, "generations" in this passage refer to the developments of the church, and therefore to its <term>doctrinals</term>, as will be made clearer in the following text.

### 1146.
That Shem, Ham, and Japheth have the same meaning as before—Shem as true internal worship, Ham as corrupt internal worship, and Japheth as external worship corresponding with the internal—is evident from our previous discussions. We have already shown that they represent these specific kinds of worship and defined what those terms mean; therefore, there is no need to dwell on the subject any longer.

### 1147.
The "sons being born unto them" signify the <term>doctrinals</term> derived from those branches. In the internal sense, "sons" denote the truths of faith, but they can also denote "falsities" (errors). Therefore, they represent <term>doctrinals</term>, which can encompass both truths and errors depending on the church in question. This spiritual meaning of "sons" was established previously in sections 264, 489, 491, and 533.

### 1148.
"After the flood" signifies the time starting from the existence of this new church. This is consistent with what was said in earlier chapters: the "flood" describes the end of the "Most Ancient Church" and the simultaneous beginning of this "Ancient Church." The church before the flood is called the Most Ancient Church, but the church after the flood is called the Ancient Church. <note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, the "Most Ancient Church" represents a state of direct perception of divine truth, while the "Ancient Church" represents a state where truth is learned through doctrine and symbols.</note>

**1149. Verse 2.** *The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.* The sons of Japheth signify those who maintained external worship corresponding with internal. Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras were so many several nations who maintained such worship; by which nations, in the internal sense, are signified so many several <term>doctrinals</term> <note>Formal religious teachings or systems of belief.</note>, which were the same as rituals, which they observed as holy.

**1150.** That the sons of Japheth signify those who maintained external worship corresponding with internal, was said above. External worship is said to correspond with internal, when its essential principle is contained within it. The essential of worship is adoration of the Lord from the heart: this cannot exist, unless the heart be principled in charity or neighborly love; for the Lord is present in charity or neighborly love, and may then be adored from the heart: thus adoration is from the Lord, for the Lord gives all power and all very being <note>original: "omne posse et omne esse"</note> <note>A philosophical distinction: "posse" is the ability or potential to act, while "esse" is the fundamental essence or state of being.</note> in adoration. Hence it follows, that the quality of adoration or worship is according to the quality of the charity in which the man is principled. All worship is adoration, because, to be worship, adoration of the Lord must be in it. The sons of Japheth, or the nations and people who were called the sons of Japheth, lived among each other in mutual charity, in friendship, in civility, and in simplicity, wherefore also the Lord was present in their worship; for when the Lord is present in external worship, then internal worship is contained within it, or it is external worship corresponding with internal. There were many nations of old, as there are some at this day, who place worship in externals, and do not know what internal things mean, or who, if they know, do not think about such things: if such acknowledge the Lord, and love their neighbor, the Lord is in their worship, and they are the sons of Japheth; but if they deny the Lord, and love only themselves, and are unconcerned about their neighbor, particularly if they bear hatred towards him, their worship is then external separate from internal, and they are the sons of Canaan, or Canaanites.

1153. The "sons of **Gomer**" also signify those who maintained external worship, but theirs was derived from the nation of Gomer. In general, all variations in external and internal worship are measured by the quality of the adoration of the Lord within them. This adoration is further measured by the amount of love for the Lord and neighborly love <note>The author uses "charity" and "neighborly love" interchangeably to describe active kindness and spiritual connection to others.</note> it contains. The Lord is present in love, and therefore present in worship; it is this presence that determined the differences between the nations named here.

Humility, in this sense, is a person's acknowledgment that in themselves they have no life and no goodness; rather, they acknowledge that everything within themselves is "dead," even like a carcass. It is the further acknowledgment that everything truly alive and good comes from the Lord. 

The more a person lives in this acknowledgment—not just with their lips, but from the heart—the more they are in a state of true humility. Consequently, they are more capable of true adoration and worship, and possess more love, charity, and happiness. These qualities are inseparable and joined together. 

From this, we can see the different qualities of worship. The nations named here as the "sons" of Gomer and Javan are those who maintained an external worship that still matched their internal heart, though it was somewhat more "remote" <note>Meaning further removed from the core spiritual source.</note> than the worship of the nations mentioned in the previous verse; this is why they are called "sons." In these descriptions, the generations represent a progression from what is interior (spiritual) to what is exterior (physical). The more <term>sensual</term> <note>A "sensual man" in this context refers to someone focused entirely on their physical senses and the material world, rather than spiritual realities.</note> a person becomes, the more they focus on the "outside," and the further they are removed from the true worship of the Lord. 1157. **Verse 5. *From these were spread abroad the islands of the Gentiles in their lands, every one according to his tongue, according to their families, as to their nations.*** By *these were spread abroad the islands of the Gentiles*, signifies that the different kinds of worship prevailing in many nations had their rise from these; *islands* are particular tracts, consequently particular kinds of worship, which were still more remote; *lands* signify the common or general principles or parts thereof: *every one according to his tongue, according to their families, as to their nations*, signifies that those kinds of worship were according to the genius <note>In 18th-century English, "genius" refers to the inherent nature or character of a person or group.</note> of each: *according to his tongue*, is according to the opinion of each; *according to their families*, is according to their probity or uprightness; *as to their nations*, means as to both opinion and probity in general.

1159. "**Every one according to his tongue, according to their families, as to their nations.**" —That these words signify, according to the genius or disposition of each; that **according to his tongue** means, according to the opinion of each; that **according to their families** means, according to the <term>probity</term> <note>Moral integrity and goodness of character.</note> of each; that **as to their nations** means, as to both opinion and probity, in general; may appear from the signification of a tongue, and of families, and nations, as mentioned in <term>the Word</term> <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible, specifically emphasizing its deep, symbolic meaning.</note>; concerning which, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said elsewhere. The ground and reason why **tongues**, or languages, in an **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the author’s method of interpreting the Bible as a series of spiritual symbols rather than just literal history.</note>, signify opinions, and consequently principles and persuasions, is, because the correspondence of the tongue or language with the intellectual part of man, or with his thought, is like that of the effect with its cause; such also is the <term>influx</term> <note>The spiritual process by which thought or energy flows from a higher level (like the soul or heaven) into a lower one (like the physical body).</note> of man's thoughts into the motions of the tongue in discourse, and such also is the influx of heaven; concerning which, by the divine mercy of the Lord, some experimental testimony will be given hereafter. That **families**, in an internal sense, signify probity, and also <term>charity</term> <note>Spiritual love and active goodwill toward others.</note> and love, is a truth grounded in this circumstance, that all things relating to mutual love are regarded in the heavens as consanguinities and relationships, consequently as families; concerning which, see number 685; wherefore, in the Word, such things as relate to love and charity are expressed by **houses**, and also by **families**, though we will not stay to prove it at present. That a **house** is used according to such signification, may be seen, number 710. That **nations** signify both opinion and probity in general, appears from the signification of a nation or nations in the Word. Nations, in a good sense, signify things now relating to will and understanding, consequently the good things of love and the truths of faith; but in an opposite sense, they signify evils and <term>falses</term> <note>A technical term used by the author to describe spiritual untruths or incorrect religious concepts.</note>. The case is similar in respect to the signification of houses, families, and tongues, as might be proved by many passages from the Word. The reason of their having this signification, is, because the most ancient church was distinguished into houses, into families, and into nations: the husband and wife, with their children, their men-servants, and maid-servants, constituted a **house**; several houses, which, in relationship, were not far distant from each other, constituted a **family**; and several families constituted a **nation**: hence, nations signified in one complex all the families together: the

1160. **Verse 6. *And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.*** By **Ham** is here signified, as before, faith separate from <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, "charity" does not just mean giving to the poor, but the active spiritual love for one's neighbor.</note>: by the **sons of Ham** are signified the offspring or consequences of such separate faith: **Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan**, were so many nations, by which, in an **internal sense**, are signified <term>knowledges</term>, <term>sciences</term> <note>The word "science" here refers to the Latin *scientia*, meaning intellectual information or factual knowledge, rather than modern experimental science.</note>, and modes of worship, which belong to faith separate from charity.

1161. That by **Ham** is signified faith separate from charity, appears from what was said and shown concerning him in the foregoing chapter.

1162. Hence it follows, that by the **sons of Ham** are signified the things which belong to such separate faith. In order to know what is meant by Ham, and thence what by the sons of Ham, it must first be known what **faith separate from charity** is. Faith separate from charity is no faith; and where there is no faith, there is no worship, neither internal nor external; or if there be any worship, it is corrupt; wherefore, by Ham, in like manner, is signified internal worship corrupted. It is a false notion to suppose, that faith consists in the mere **science** or **knowledge** of things celestial and spiritual separate from charity; for sometimes the very worst of men are most eminently distinguished for such science, who live in continual habits of hatred, revenge, and adultery, consequently who are infernal, and after the life of the body become devils. Hence it may appear that **science is not faith**. But faith is an **acknowledgment** of the things that belong to faith; and acknowledgment is by no means external, but internal, and is the operation of the Lord alone, by charity, in man: acknowledgment belongs not to the lips, but to the life, and by the life of every one it may be known, what is the nature and quality of his acknowledgment. The **sons of Ham** are all those, who are scientifically skilled in the **knowledges** of faith, and have not charity. Such persons, whether they are scientifically skilled in the interior **knowledges** of the Word, and in its very mysteries; or in the **science** of all things contained in the literal sense of the Word;

### 1163.
That *Cush*, *Mizraim*, *Phut*, and *Canaan*, were several distinct nations, by which, in an <term>internal sense</term> <note>The "internal sense" is the deeper spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal historical narrative.</note>, are signified knowledge, sciences, and rituals, which belong to faith separate from charity, may appear from the *Word* <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, where those nations are frequently mentioned. Wherever they occur they signify such things: as for example:

*   By *Cush*, or *Ethiopia*, are signified the interior knowledges of the Word, applied to confirm false principles.
*   By *Mizraim*, or *Egypt*, are signified sciences, or various <term>scientifics</term> <note>The term "scientifics" refers to raw facts, data, or items of information stored in the memory.</note>, applied to explore the mysteries of faith, and thereby to confirm false principles.
*   By *Phut*, or *Lybia*, are signified knowledges acquired out of the literal sense of the Word, and applied in like manner to confirm false principles.
*   By *Canaan*, or the *Canaanites*, are signified rituals, or the observations of external worship, when they are separated from internal worship.

All these things, when they are separate from charity, are called the sons of *Ham*. By these same nations are also signified simply knowledges and sciences when not used for false purposes: by *Cush*, the interior knowledges of the Word; by *Egypt*, sciences; by *Phut*, knowledges derived from the literal sense of the Word. This is the reason why they are used in both a good and a bad sense, as may appear from the following passages.

### 1164.

where *Egypt* denotes those who believe nothing but what they can grasp by <term>scientifics</term>, which leads to all things being involved in doubt, denial, and falsehood; this is signified by his "coming up, covering the earth, and destroying the city." *Cush* here denotes the more universal and interior knowledges of the Word, applied to confirm preconceived principles of what is false. *Phut* denotes knowledges taken from the literal sense of the Word, which are based on how things appear to our physical senses. 

So in *Ezekiel*: 

“The sword shall come upon *Egypt*, and there shall be pain in *Cush*, when the slain shall fall in *Egypt*, and they shall take her multitude, and her foundations shall be destroyed, *Cush*, and *Phut*, and *Lud*, and all *Ereb*, and *Chub*, and the sons of the land that is in league with them shall fall with them by the sword,” (xxx. 4.

It may be expedient here to premise what is meant by making **internal worship** external. It was said and shown above, that internal worship, which is grounded in **love and charity**, is real worship, or worship itself, and that external worship, without this internal, is no worship: but to make internal worship external, is to make external worship **essential** <note>Meaning the most important or defining part of the practice.</note>, more than internal, which is to invert the above true order; as by saying, that there is no internal worship without external, when yet the truth of the case is, that there is no external worship without internal. As for example; supposing a person to live where there is no church, no preaching, no sacraments, no priesthood; if it be asserted, that such a person cannot be saved, or that he cannot exercise any worship, when, nevertheless, he may worship the Lord from what is internal [this is to make worship consist of that which is formal without that which is essential, and thus to make internal worship external].* <note>The editor notes that in the original manuscript, this sentence was left incomplete. ### 1186. 
That Ashur denotes reasoning, appears from the signification of Ashur or Assyria in the Word, where it is constantly used to denote the things belonging to reason in both senses, namely, things rational, and also reasonings: by reason and things rational are properly meant those things which are true, but by reason and reasonings are meant the things which are false. Because Ashur, or Assyria, signifies reason and reasonings, it is generally mentioned in connection with *Egypt*, which signifies <term>scientifics</term> <note>In this context, "scientifics" refers to factual knowledge or external information stored in the memory, rather than inner spiritual wisdom.</note>, because reason and reasonings are grounded in facts. That Ashur signifies reasoning, appears from Isaiah:

> “Woe to *Ashur*, the rod of mine anger :—he does not think what is right, and his heart does not meditate what is right ;—he has said, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, because I am intelligent,” (x. 5, 7, 13 ;)

where *Ashur* denotes reasoning, of whom therefore it is stated that he does not think and meditate what is right, and it is said, that by his wisdom he has done it, as being intelligent. So in *Ezekiel*:

> “Two women, the daughters of one mother, committed whoredom in *Egypt*; they committed whoredom in their youth. The one committed whoredom, and doted on her lovers, on the *Assyrians* her neighbors, which were clothed with blue, captains and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses.—*The sons of Babel came to her,*—and polluted her by their whoredoms,” (xxiii. 2, 3, 5, 6, 17 ;)

where *Egypt* signifies factual knowledge, *Ashur* signifies reasoning, and the sons of *Babel* signify falsehoods originating in evil lusts. Again, in the same prophet, speaking of *Jerusalem*:

> “Thou hast committed whoredom with the sons of *Egypt*:—thou hast committed whoredom with the sons of *Ashur*:—thou hast multiplied whoredom even in the land of *Canaan* unto *Chaldea*,” (xvi. 26, 28, 29 ;)

where *Egypt*, in like manner, denotes factual knowledge; *Ashur* denotes reasoning: reasoning grounded in facts, and applied to things spiritual and celestial, is called whoredom <note>The author explains that "whoredom" is used here as a biblical metaphor for the misuse of intellectual or spiritual truths, rather than a literal reference to immorality.</note>, both in this and other passages of the Word; it must be obvious to every one that whoredom with the *Egyptians* and *Assyrians*, according to the literal sense, is not here meant.

These three constitute the intellectual faculties of the man of the spiritual church, the succession of which is in this order.
