They are not the type of people who use natural sciences to reason about spiritual or heavenly things and then create their own systems of belief. Instead, they learn the <term>knowledges of faith</term> <note>The facts, concepts, and doctrines regarding religious belief.</note> from other sources. Once they have learned these facts, they keep them in their memories just like any other information. They view this knowledge only as something to "know," with no intention of using it to improve their lives, except when it helps them gain social status or money. 

Because of this, their knowledge of faith is kept separate from their knowledge of the natural world; there is almost no connection between the two. This is why the Philistines are described as "coming forth" from the previous nations rather than being "born" from them. Because the Philistines have this character, they cannot help but distort the facts of faith by using their own flawed logic, which leads them to create false teachings. For this reason, they belong to a class of people who find it very difficult to be <term>regenerated</term> <note>The spiritual process of being "born again" or internally transformed by God.</note> and to receive true charity. This is because their hearts are "uncircumcised" <note>In a spiritual sense, this means the heart is closed off from divine love and remains focused on selfish desires.</note> and because their false principles and intellectual habits create constant opposition to spiritual growth.

**1199.** Verse 15. *And Canaan begat Sidon his first-born, and Heth.* Here, Canaan signifies "external worship" that has no internal or spiritual heart. *Sidon* signifies the outward knowledge of spiritual things; because these are the first or most important parts of such external worship, Sidon is called the "first-born" of Canaan. *Heth* signifies the outward knowledge of "celestial" <note>Things relating to the highest form of love and divine goodness.</note> things.

**1200.** It was shown earlier that Canaan represents external worship lacking any internal spirit. The type of worship called "Canaan" is the kind that was common among the Jews both before and after the Lord's coming. They focused strictly on outward obedience and rituals, yet they were so ignorant of anything internal that they believed there was no life other than that of the physical body. The nature of the soul, faith, the Lord, spiritual life, and life after death were completely unknown to them. This is why, even during the time of the Lord's appearance, many of them denied the resurrection, as shown in the Gospels (Matthew 22:22–33; Mark 12:18–28; Luke 20:27–41). 

When a person does not believe in life after death, they inevitably disbelieve in anything internal, spiritual, or heavenly. This describes people who are consumed by their own physical cravings because they live only for the world and the flesh—especially when their desires are rooted in "filthy avarice" <note>An obsessive and corrupt greed for wealth.</note>. Despite this internal state, such people often maintain a form of religious worship, attending synagogues or churches and following established traditions.

<summary>This page analyzes the spiritual meaning of the Philistines and Canaanites, defining them as those who possess religious knowledge or perform rituals but lack an internal, living connection to the divine.</summary>

Such external worship is what is signified by *Canaan*. The other kinds of external worship, spoken of above, were such as contained in them internal principles.

1201. That *Sidon* signifies the exterior knowledges of things *spiritual*, appears from his being called the first-born of *Canaan*; for the first-born of every church, in an internal sense, is faith (see sections 352, 367); but, in the present case, where there was no faith, because there were no internals, it signifies nothing but the exterior knowledges of spiritual things, which were in the place of faith. These were the kind of knowledges that the Jews had, which not only related to the rites of external worship, but also to the several things appertaining to that worship, such as <term>doctrinals</term> <note>Specific points of teaching or formal principles of a religion.</note>. That this is the signification of *Sidon*, appears also from this consideration, that *Tyre* and *Sidon* were the ultimate borders of *Philisthea*, and were near the sea; whence by *Tyre* are signified interior knowledges, and by *Sidon* exterior knowledges, and this specifically of things spiritual. This also appears from the Word <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>; as in Jeremiah: “Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the *Philisthines*, to cut off from *Tyre* and *Sidon* every helper that remaineth; for Jehovah will spoil the Philisthines, the remains of the island of *Caphtor*,” (xlvii. 4;) where by the Philisthines are signified the sciences of the knowledges of faith and charity: by *Tyre* the interior knowledges, and by *Sidon* the exterior knowledges of things spiritual. So in Joel: “What have ye to do with me, O *Tyre* and *Sidon*, and all the borders of *Philisthea*?—because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my desirable good things,” (iii. 4, 5;) where *Tyre* and *Sidon* manifestly denote knowledges, and are called the borders of Philisthea; for silver and gold, and desirable good things, are knowledges. So in Ezekiel: “The princes of the north, all of them, and all the *Sidonians*, who have gone down with the slain. So in Zechariah: “*Hamath* also shall have its border thereby, *Tyre* and *Sidon*; for he was very wise,” (ix. 2;) speaking of *Damascus*; *Tyre* and *Sidon* denote knowledges. So in Ezekiel: “The inhabitants of *Sidon* and of *Arvad* were thy mariners; thy wise ones, O *Tyre*, that were in thee, were thy pilots,” (xxvii. 8;) where *Tyre* denotes interior knowledges, wherefore her wise ones are called pilots; and *Sidon* denotes exterior knowledges, wherefore

## 1202. ##
Because these knowledges are the first and principal things appertaining to such external worship, in which there is no internal worship, *Sidon* is called the first-born of *Canaan*, according to what was shown in the preceding article.

## 1203. ##
Hence it appears that Heth signifies the exterior knowledges of things <term>celestial</term><note>Related to the will and to love, as opposed to "spiritual" things which relate to the understanding and faith.</note>. It is usual with the prophets to join together things spiritual and celestial, or, in treating of spiritual things, to treat also of celestial things, by reason that they are dependent on each other, and there is no perfection unless they be in conjunction: thus it is provided, that there be a resemblance of the <term>celestial marriage</term><note>The union of truth and good, or faith and love, which is the foundational balance of the universe in this theological system.</note> in all and every particular of the Word. From this circumstance, and likewise from several passages in other parts of the Word, it appears that by *Sidon* are signified the exterior knowledges of things spiritual, and by Heth the exterior knowledges of things celestial, in both senses, viz., as well without internals as with internals; and also, that they simply denote exterior knowledges. Spiritual things, as has been often before observed, are such as have relation to faith, celestial things such as have relation to love; also, spiritual things are such as have relation to the understanding, and celestial things such as have relation to the will. That Heth signifies exterior knowledges without internal, appears from Ezekiel: “Thus saith the Lord Jehovih <note>original: "Jehovih" — a specific name for God used when the subject is the "good" of love.</note> unto Jerusalem, Thy birth and thy nativity are of the land of *Canaan*; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother a *Hittite*.—Thou art thy mother’s daughter, that loathed her husband and her sons: and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which loathed their husbands and their sons. ## 1204. ##

**Verses 16, 17, 18.** *And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite, and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite, and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. ## 1205. ##

That the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgasites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites, were so many several nations, significative of so many different kinds of idolatry appears from several passages in the Word; for these were the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, who, by reason of their idolatries, were rejected, and in part extirpated. Nevertheless, in the <term>internal sense</term><note>The deeper spiritual meaning of the biblical text that lies beneath the literal historical narrative.</note> of the Word are not signified those nations, but the idolatries themselves prevalent among them, and, in general, those idolatries as prevalent with any people whatsoever, in particular as prevalent amongst the Jews. For they who make worship to consist merely in things external, and are altogether unwilling to be instructed in things internal, and reject them when they are instructed, are most prone to every species of idolatry, as appears plainly from the case of the Jews: in internal worship alone, there is a bond which withholds man from idolatry; but when that bond is removed, then there remains no other restraining power. There are, however, idolatries, not only of an external sort, but also such as are of a more interior nature. External idolatries are eagerly embraced by those who cultivate external worship without internal; the more interior kinds of idolatry are embraced by those who cultivate an external worship the interiors of which are defiled. Both these kinds of idolatries are signified by these nations. Interior idolatries are so many several falsities and evil lusts, which men love and adore, and which are thus in the place of the gods and idols worshipped amongst the Gentiles. But what particular kinds of idol-falsities and lusts are signified by these...

**Verse 19.** *And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, in coming to Gerar, even unto Azzah, in coming to Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, even unto Lasha.* By **Sidon** are here signified exterior knowledges <note>Basic facts or introductory concepts about spiritual life.</note>, as before: by **Gerar** are signified those things which are revealed concerning **faith**: by **Azzah**, those things which are revealed concerning <term>charity</term><note>In this system, "charity" refers to active love for one's neighbor and the desire to do good.</note>: by the border of the Canaanites being from Sidon, in coming to Gerar, even unto Azzah, is signified the extension of knowledges to truth and goodness with those who attend to external worship without internal: in coming to **Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, even to Lasha**, signifies the falsities and evils wherein they terminate.

That by **Sidon** are signified exterior knowledges, appears from what was shown above, at verse 15.

That by **Gerar** are signified those things which are revealed concerning faith, consequently faith itself in general, may appear from the passages where Gerar is mentioned, Genesis 20:1; 26:1, 6, 17; but concerning this signification, by the divine mercy of the Lord, more will be said hereafter.

## 1210. ##

That by **Azzah** (or Gaza) are signified those things which are revealed concerning charity, may appear, first, from this consideration: that wheresoever the **Word** <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> treats of things spiritual, it also treats conjointly of things celestial: that is, when it treats of the things appertaining to faith, it also treats of the things appertaining to charity. It may likewise appear from the other passages in the Word where mention is made of Azzah: and it may further appear from this consideration, that knowledges extend themselves to faith, even unto charity, which is their last term or limit.

## 1211. ##

That "the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon in coming to Gerar, even unto Azzah," signifies the extension of knowledges with those who maintain external worship without internal, appears from the signification of Gerar and Azzah. The boundaries, that is, the terms or limits, of all knowledges which respect worship, whether it be external or internal, are in that direction; for all worship is grounded in faith and charity, and if it be not so grounded, it is not worship, but idolatry. ## 1212. ##

“In coming to Sodom and Gomorrah, and Admah and Zeboim, even unto Lasha.”—That these words signify falsities and evils, wherein knowledges terminate, may appear from the signification of the same expressions in the historical and prophetical parts of the Word. There are in general two origins of falsities, one arising from the lusts of self-love and the love of the world, and the other from knowledges and <term>scientifics</term><note>In this context, "scientifics" refers to the raw facts, data, and information stored in the memory, which can be used either for good or for constructing deceptive arguments.</note> by means of reasonings; the falsities thence derived, when they would domineer over truths, are signified by Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim. That falsities and the evils thence resulting are the boundaries or limits of such <term>external worship</term><note>Religious practice that consists only of outward rituals, lacking any genuine internal love or faith.</note> as is without <term>internal</term><note>The "internal" refers to the heart, intention, and true spiritual understanding of a person.</note>, may appear plain to every one. In such worship, all is dead and lifeless, so that which way soever the man who maintains such worship turns himself, he falls into falsities: there is no internal principle to guide and keep him in the way of truth, but only an external one, which carries him away, according to the impulses of lust and phantasy. Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, being often mentioned in the historical and prophetical parts of the Word, the particular signification of each, by the divine mercy of the Lord, will be shown as they occur.

1222. That by “the elder brother of Japheth” is signified, that the worship in this church was external, appears from the signification of <term>Japheth</term>, as denoting the <term>external church</term>; concerning <term>Japheth</term> see the foregoing chapter, verse 18. and above in this chapter, from verse 1 to 5. Here, <term>Shem</term>, the elder brother of <term>Japheth</term>, signifies, in particular, that the <term>internal church</term> and the <term>external church</term> are brethren; for such is the connection and relationship subsisting between internal worship and external worship, when this is influenced by internal, because in each <term>charity</term><note>In this theological context, "charity" refers to an active, spiritual love for one's neighbor, which gives life to outward religious rituals.</note> is the principal; but the <term>internal church</term> is the elder brother, as being prior and interior. “The elder brother of <term>Japheth</term>” likewise implies, that the second ancient church called <term>Heber</term><note>Heber represents a specific historical-spiritual shift where the "Ancient Church" began to focus more on rituals and external laws.</note>, was as a brother of the first ancient church; for by <term>Japheth</term>, in the <term>internal sense</term>, is signified nothing else but external worship influenced by internal, whatever be the church which is spoken of; consequently, by <term>Japheth</term>, also, is signified the worship which prevailed in this new ancient church, which was chiefly external. Such is the nature of the <term>internal sense</term><note>The "internal sense" is the method of interpreting the Bible where people, places, and events represent spiritual states and divine truths.</note> of the Word, that the historical circumstances of the <term>literal sense</term> are not attended to, when respect is had to the universals that are abstracted from the <term>literal sense</term>, for they mutually regard each other in a different manner: hence the elder brother of <term>Japheth</term> here signifies, in the <term>internal sense</term>, the worship which prevailed in the new ancient church, denoting it to be external. Unless this had been the signification of these words, it would have been needless to add, that <term>Shem</term> was the elder brother of <term>Japheth</term>.

1223. Verse 22. *The sons of Shem; Elam, and Ashur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.* By <term>Shem</term>, is here signified, as before, the <term>internal church</term>: by the sons of <term>Shem</term> are signified the things appertaining to <term>wisdom</term>: <term>Elam</term>, <term>Ashur</term>, <term>Arphaxad</term>, <term>Lud</term>, and <term>Aram</term>, were so many several nations, by which are signified the things appertaining to <term>wisdom</term>: by <term>Elam</term> is signified <term>faith</term> grounded in <term>charity</term>; by <term>Ashur</term>, reason thence derived; by <term>Arphaxad</term>, <term>science</term><note>Here, "science" refers to the systematic arrangement of facts and memory-knowledge, rather than the modern experimental sciences.</note> thence derived; by <term>Lud</term>, the knowledges of truth; by <term>Aram</term>, the knowledges of good.

1224. Hence it appears that these names signify in the <term>internal sense</term>, namely<note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, that the ancient church, which was an internal church, was endowed with <term>wisdom</term>, <term>intelligence</term>, <term>science</term>, and the knowledges of truth and goodness. Such are the things contained in the <term>internal sense</term>, although nothing is expressed by names, which in the <term>literal sense</term> seem only to imply, that there were so many several origins or fathers of nations, and thus nothing doctrinal, much less spiritual and celestial, appears to be involved in them. The case is similar in the writings of the prophets, where sometimes there occurs a series of names, by which, in the <term>internal sense</term>, are signified things, which are arranged in a beautiful and connected order.

1225. That by <term>Shem</term><note>Shem, the son of Noah, is interpreted here as a symbol for the "internal church," which focuses on the heart and spiritual motives rather than just outward ceremony.</note> is signified the <term>internal church</term>, was said and shown in the foregoing chapter, verse 18, and the subsequent verses.

1226. That by the sons of <term>Shem</term> are signified such things as appertain to **wisdom**, appears from this consideration: that <term>Shem</term> is the <term>internal church</term>, the sons of which are no other than the things of **wisdom**. All that is called **wisdom** is begotten of <term>charity</term><note>In this context, charity means an active love for others flowing from God.</note>—that is, by <term>charity</term> from the Lord, from whom all **wisdom** comes, because he is **Wisdom** itself. From this source comes true intelligence, true <term>science</term><note>Here, 'science' refers to factual or empirical knowledge of the world and the senses.</note>, and true knowledge; all of these are the "sons" of **wisdom**. They are the sons of the Lord through <term>charity</term>. Since they are the sons of the Lord by <term>charity</term>, **wisdom** is attributed to each of them; for in each there is **wisdom** from which they derive their life. This is so true that neither intelligence, nor <term>science</term>, nor knowledge has any life except from **wisdom**, which is the offspring of <term>charity</term>, which, in turn, is the offspring of the Lord.

With those called the sons of <term>Ham</term>, there existed a *corrupt* <term>internal church</term>; and with those called the sons of <term>Canaan</term>, a *corrupt* <term>external church</term>. It is the same thing whether we speak of internal and external worship, or of an internal and external church.

### 1260—1265. GENESIS.

**1260.** ...changed into evil, and truth into what is false. Hence the meaning of *nations* and *people*, in this negative sense, very frequently occurs in the *Word* <note>The "Word" is a term used here to refer to the Bible or Holy Scripture.</note>; as in Isaiah 13:4; 14:6; 18:2, 7; 30:28; 34:1, 2; Ezekiel 20:32; and in several other places.

**1261.** Just as *nations* signified principles of good, so also did *families*, because every *nation* consisted of *families*. For the same reason, *houses* had the same meaning, since every *family* consisted of several *houses* (see above, n. 710). *Families*, however, signify principles of truth when they are associated with *people*, but principles of good when associated with *nations*. This is seen in the Book of Psalms: “All the *families* of the *nations* shall bow themselves before thee; for the kingdom is Jehovah’s, and he is the governor amongst the *nations*” (Psalm 22:27, 28). And again: “Give unto Jehovah, ye *families* of the *peoples*, give unto Jehovah glory and strength” (Psalm 96:7). In this and the preceding verse of this chapter, families are associated with principles of good because they were families of *nations*.

**1262.** From this, it may appear that by the *earth* is here also signified the *church* <note>In this interpretive system, "the earth" usually represents the external church or the people within it, rather than the physical soil.</note>. When mention is made of the *earth* or of a *country*, the angels do not perceive the physical *earth* or *country*, but the *nation* or *people* dwelling there. Furthermore, when a *nation* or *people* is mentioned, they perceive their quality or ruling character. Therefore, by the *earth*, nothing else is signified but the *church*, as was shown above (n. 662, 1066).

**1263.** The phrase “after the flood” signifies the timeframe starting from the beginning of the *ancient church*. This is because the flood represented the end of the *most ancient church* and the beginning of the *ancient church* <note>The "Most Ancient Church" represents humanity’s earliest state of innocence, while the "Ancient Church" represents a later state of spiritual development following a period of decline.</note>, as was shown above (n. 705, 739, 790).

**1264.** Thus it appears that although this chapter contains what seem to be mere names of *nations* and *families*, it actually contains all the different types of worship—regarding the good principles of charity and the truths of faith—that existed in the *ancient church*. In fact, it contains more than a person can possibly believe or conceive. Such is the nature of the Lord's *Word*.

## CHAPTER ELEVEN.

### ->**CONCERNING THE SITUATION OF THE <term>GRAND MAN</term>: ALSO, CONCERNING PLACE AND DISTANCE IN THE AFTERLIFE.**<-
<note>original: "Maximus Homo." This is a central concept in Swedenborg's work, suggesting that the entire collective of heaven functions together as a single, immense human organism, where every individual or society corresponds to a specific part of the body.</note>

1273. *When souls have recently died and are about to be separated from the company of the spiritual angels, they begin their transition into the world of spirits. Eventually, they are led to the specific society they belonged to during their physical life. To get there, they are guided by angels through several <term>mansions</term> <note>Spiritual stations or dwellings.</note>, which are distinct societies connected to one another. They are welcomed everywhere they go, yet they continue moving from one to the next. This journey continues for some time until they reach the society that matches the life they lived in the body; there they remain, and from that point, their life begins anew.* 

*If a person was a pretender, a hypocrite, or a deceitful individual—someone skilled at faking a good character or putting on an "angelic" face—they might occasionally be welcomed by good spirits. However, after a short time, they are separated from that group and wander alone without any angelic companions, begging to be let in. Instead, they are rejected and sometimes punished, eventually being drawn down among the <term>infernals</term> <note>Those living in the hells.</note>. Conversely, those who are raised to the company of angels after a state of <term>vastation</term> <note>A process of spiritual purification where a soul is stripped of worldly or false layers to reveal its true inner essence.</note> also pass through various societies. They are received everywhere with kindness and charity until they finally reach an angelic community that perfectly harmonizes with their specific character—be it their charity, piety, integrity, or sincere kindness. I have personally been guided through these various dwellings in this same way and had the opportunity to talk with the inhabitants of the different societies, so that I could become fully acquainted with how this process works. I was then permitted to reflect on these "changes of place" and perceive that they are only appearances; they are actually nothing more than changes of internal state, even while the "body" remains in the same location.*
<note>In the spiritual world, "moving" from place to place is a visual representation of a change in a person's thoughts and feelings.</note>

1274. *Among the remarkable things regarding the afterlife are the following: FIRST: The societies of spirits and angels appear to be in distinct locations...*

*...even though locations and distances in the afterlife are nothing more than variations of one's inner state. SECONDLY: That locations and distances are arranged in relation to the human body. THIRDLY: That spirits and angels are never so far apart that they cannot be seen; however, only those whom the Lord permits come into view. FOURTHLY: That when someone thinks of another spirit (such as those who were acquainted during their physical life), that spirit becomes present instantly if the Lord allows. This is how things are in the world of spirits, and even more perfectly so in heaven; how much more so, then, in relation to the Lord, to whom everyone must be immediately present and under His direct gaze and providence! These things may seem unbelievable, yet they are true.*

*1275. I was once in a community where tranquility prevailed—a state that somewhat approached a state of peace, though it was not yet true peace. There, I spoke about the condition of infants and also about the nature of "place." We observed that changes in location and distance are merely appearances that reflect the changes in a person's inner state. When I was transported there, the spirits who had been around me seemed to move away and appear beneath me; nevertheless, I was still permitted to hear their conversation.*

*1276. Regarding the positions of spirits in the world of spirits and angels in heaven: Angels are at the Lord's right hand, while evil spirits are at the left. In front are those of a middle nature; behind are the malicious. Above the head are those of an ambitious or high-aspiring temperament; beneath the feet are the hells that correspond to those who are on high. Thus, everyone has a specific position relative to the Lord—in every direction, at every height, and across every possible angle, whether horizontal, vertical, or tilted. Furthermore, these positions are constant and remain unchanged for eternity. The heavens, taken together, form a single "man," which is therefore called the <term>GRAND MAN</term> <note>original: "Maximus Homo." This is Swedenborg's concept that the entire spiritual world organized by God functions as a single, giant human organism.</note>. There is an exact <term>correspondence</term> <note>A spiritual law where every physical body part or function represents a specific spiritual reality or quality.</note> between this Grand Man and every individual part of a human being. By the Lord's divine mercy, more will be explained about this in the following parts of this work. This is why the arrangement of all things appears the same to every angel and to every person whose spiritual sight is opened by...*

1277. *The same holds true with respect to men, as to their souls, which are constantly bound to some society of spirits and angels. They also have their respective situations in the Lord's kingdom, according to the <term>genius of their lives</term> <note>The inherent nature, disposition, or ruling character of a person.</note> and according to their states. Nor does their distance from each other on earth alter the case: though persons may live here many thousands of miles apart, it is still possible for them to be together in one society—those who live in charity in one angelic society, and those who live in hatred and other evil affections in one infernal society. In like manner, their living together on earth does not alter the case: though great numbers may be together in one place here, they are all still distinguished according to the particular nature of their lives and according to their states, and each may be in a different spiritual society. Men, who are distant from each other some hundreds of thousands of miles, when they appear before the <term>internal senses</term> <note>The spiritual perception or "sight" of the soul, which sees beyond the physical world.</note> of each other, are so near that in some cases they are in mutual contact, according to their situation. Thus, supposing there were several on earth who had their internal sight open, they might be together and converse together, even though one were in India and another in Europe. This, also, I have been convinced of by experience. Thus all men on earth, both in general and in particular, are most immediately present with the Lord, and are under his inspection and providence.*

## 1284. *Verse 1. And the whole earth was (of) one lip, and their words (were) one.* 

By “the whole earth was of one lip,” is signified, that there prevailed everywhere one doctrine in general: <term>lip</term> <note>In this symbolic system, the "lip" refers to the spoken doctrine or the shared language of a religious community.</note> signifies doctrine; the **earth** is the church : by “their words (were) one,” is signified, that there prevailed one doctrine in particular.

## 1285. 

That by “*the whole earth was (of) one lip,*” is signified, that there prevailed everywhere one <term>doctrinal</term> <note>A specific point of teaching or a system of religious belief.</note> in general, appears from the signification of the lip, as used in the Word, concerning which we shall speak presently. In this verse, and by these words, is described the state of the ancient church as to its nature and quality, *viz.*, that there prevailed one doctrine in general : but in the following verse is described how it began to be falsified and adulterated : and afterwards, as far as verse 9, how it was altogether perverted, so that there remained no longer any internal worship. 

The subject soon after treated of is, concerning a second ancient church begun by <term>Heber</term> <note>Also known as Eber; in this context, he represents a specific era or branch of the post-flood church that eventually led to the Hebrew tradition.</note>; and, lastly, concerning a third, which was the beginning of the **Jewish church**; for after the flood there were three churches in succession. As to what concerns the first ancient church, of which it is said (notwithstanding its being **diffused** so widely through the world) that there was in it only one lip, and their words were one, that is, one doctrine in general and in particular, when, nevertheless, the kinds of worship, both internal and external, prevailing in it, were very different, as was shown in the foregoing chapter, where by every particular nation mentioned is signified some different doctrinal and ritual; the case is this. 

In heaven there are innumerable societies, and all various, but still they form a one, for they are all under the Lord’s guiding and governance, as one; on which subject see what was said above, n. 457, 551, 684, 685, 690. In this respect, heaven is like any individual man, in whom, although there are so many <term>viscera</term> <note>Internal organs of the body.</note>, and so many smaller viscera within the larger, so many organs and so many members, each of which has a different operation from the rest, yet they are all and each of them governed as one by one soul : or it is like the body in which there are different activities of force and motion, whilst, nevertheless, they are all ruled by one single motion of the heart, and one single motion of the lungs, and make a one. The true ground and reason why all these component parts can thus act as one is, because in heaven there is one single <term>influx</term> <note>A spiritual term for the "flowing in" of divine life and order from God into people and heaven.</note>, which is

But the land of Shinar <note>Shinar is interpreted here not just as a geographical location, but as a symbol for a specific corrupted state of the church.</note> signifies external worship whose internal is profane, as was shown above, number 1183. 

Thus, in the present case, by their finding a valley in the land of Shinar, is signified, that their worship became more unclean and profane. In the first verse the church is treated of as being of one lip, and their words one, or having one doctrine in general and in particular: but the subject treated of in this verse is the declension <note>Declension refers to a downward slide or deterioration in spiritual or moral standards.</note> of the church, expressed by their journeying from the east, that is, by their beginning to recede from charity. For in proportion as the church, or the members of the church, recede from charity, their worship recedes from the state of being holy, or approaches the state of being unclean and profane. This signification of a valley in the land of Shinar, is grounded in this circumstance, that a valley is a kind of low place between mountains, and mountains signify, as just observed, the holy states and feelings of love or of charity in worship. ### 1293.
“And they dwelt there.”—That these words signify life thence derived, may appear from the signification of *dwelling* as used in the Word, and denoting living. The expression *to dwell* occurs frequently both in the prophetical and historical parts of the Word, and, for the most part, in the internal sense <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper spiritual meaning hidden beneath the literal words of the Bible.</note> it signifies to live. The reason is, because the most ancient people dwelt in tents, and there performed the most holy worship; wherefore also tents, in the Word, signify the holy principle of worship, as was shown, n. 414: and as such is the signification of tents, therefore also *to dwell*, in a good sense, signifies to live, or life. In like manner, because the most ancient people used to journey with their tents, *to journey*, in the internal sense of the Word, signifies the institutes and order of life.

->## GENESIS. [CHAP. xi.]<-

**1294.** **Verse 3.** *And they said, each man to his companion, "Come, let us make brick, and let us burn them to a burning." And they had brick for stone, and bitumen had they for loam.*

"And they said, each man to his companion," signifies that the process had begun. "Come, let us make brick," signifies the falsehoods <note>original: "falsa" – In this context, these are specific false ideas or doctrines that people create themselves rather than accepting divine truth.</note> which they framed for themselves. "And let us burn them to a burning," signifies evils originating in self-love. "And they had brick for stone," signifies that they used these falsehoods instead of truth. "And bitumen <note>A naturally occurring petroleum spray or tar, used here as a sticky, flammable bonding agent.</note> had they for loam <note>original: "luto" – A natural clay or mortar used in building; here symbolizing natural goodness used to bind truths together.</note>," signifies that they had the evil of desire and lust instead of goodness.

**1295.** That the phrase "they said, each man to his companion" signifies that it was begun, or that they began, follows from the sequence of the subjects discussed. The subject of this verse is the third state of the church, when falsehoods began to prevail—specifically, falsehoods rooted in evil desires. 

There are two origins of falsehood: one arising from ignorance of the truth, and the other from evil desires. Falsehoods originating in ignorance are not as harmful as those originating in evil desires. Ignorance-based falsehoods might be the result of poor instruction since childhood, or from a person being so busy with worldly business that they have not had the chance to examine their opinions. They might also come from a simple lack of judgment. These types of errors do not cause much spiritual harm, provided the person does not stubbornly defend them through complicated reasoning or use them to justify their own selfish desires. If they do justify them this way, they make their "cloud of ignorance" even thicker until it becomes a darkness where truth cannot be seen.

However, the situation is different with falsehoods originating in evil desires, such as self-love and the love of the world. This happens when a person adopts a religious doctrine specifically to control others or draw attention to themselves. They pervert the doctrine to serve their own ends and try to prove it using both <term>scientifics</term> <note>From the Latin "scientificis," meaning factual knowledge, data, or information gathered from the world and the senses.</note> and the literal words of the Bible. Worship coming from such a motive is considered "profane" <note>To "profane" something is to take what is holy and treat it as common or use it for selfish, corrupt purposes.</note>, regardless of how holy it looks on the outside. Inwardly, such a person is worshipping themselves, not the Lord, and they only acknowledge "truth" if it can be twisted to favor them.

This kind of worship is what is meant by **Babel**. However, this does not apply to people who are born and raised in such a religious system but do not realize it is false, and who live lives of genuine kindness and charity. In their ignorance, there is still innocence, and in their worship, there is goodness. Whether worship is truly "profane" depends less on the ritual itself and more on the heart and character of the person performing it.

It distinguishes between errors made in honest ignorance and the dangerous "profane" worship that arises when religion is used to serve self-love.</summary>

**1296.** “**Come, let us make <term>brick</term>.**”—That these words signify the <term>falses</term> <note>original: "falsa" – in this system of thought, "falses" refers to specific incorrect ideas or fabricated doctrines that people create to justify their own behavior.</note> which they frame to themselves, appears from the signification of **brick**. **Stone**, in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, signifies **truth**; hence **brick**, as being made by man, signifies what is **false**; for **brick** is **stone** artificially made. That **brick** has this signification, may appear also from the following passages. In Isaiah: 

> “I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;—which sacrifice in gardens, and burn incense upon bricks,” (lxv. 2, 3:)

> “And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, that say in the pride and stoutness of heart, The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones,” (ix. 9, 10;)

where Ephraim denotes one that is intelligent, who is fallen into perverseness, and who calls <term>falses</term>, or <term>bricks</term>, <term>truths</term>, or makes them so: hewn stone denotes what is fictitious <note>Unlike natural stone, "hewn stone" here implies something altered by human tools, often symbolizing truths that have been manipulated by human reasoning.</note>. So in Nahum: 

> “Draw the waters for the siege, fortify thy strongholds; go into the mud, and tread the loam; repair the brick-kiln; there shall the fire devour thee, the sword shall cut thee off,” (iii. 14, 15;)

where to tread the loam denotes <term>falses</term>, and to repair the brick-kiln denotes worship grounded in them: **fire** is the punishment of evil lusts, and the **sword** is the punishment of <term>falsities</term>. So in Ezekiel:

where it was further commanded that he should lay siege to it, by which is prophetically implied, that worship was falsified. That **brick** signifies what is **false**, may further appear from the signification of **stone**, as denoting what is **true**; of which more will be said presently.

**1297.** “**And let us burn them to a <term>burning</term>.**”—That these words signify the evils proceeding from <term>self-love</term>, appears from the signification of **burning**, of **fire**, of **sulphur**, and of **bitumen**, in the Word, which are predicated of evil lusts <note>In this context, "lusts" (cupiditates) refers to intense, selfish desires that drive a person's will.</note>, especially of those which are derived from **self-love**. It was because stones signified truth, that the landmarks of the most ancient people consisted of stones, and that they set up stones as witnesses of a thing’s being so, or being true; as appears from the stone which Jacob set up for a pillar, (Gen. xxviii. 22; xxxv. 14;) and from the pillar of stones between Laban and Jacob, (Gen. xxxi. 46, 47, 52;) and from the altar which the sons of Reuben, of Gad, and of Manasseh, raised up for a witness near Jordan, (Josh. xxii. 10, 28, 34.) Hence truths are signified by stones in **the Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>: so that holy truths, which are those of love, are denoted, not only by the stones of the altar, but also by the precious stones on the shoulders of Aaron’s ephod, and on the breast-plate of judgment. 

As to what regards the altar, when worship began to be performed by the offering of sacrifices on altars, then the altar signified the representative worship of the Lord in general, and the stones themselves signified the holy truths of that worship: wherefore it was commanded that the altar should be built of whole stones, unhewn, and it was prohibited to lift up any iron upon them, (Deut. xxvii. 5, 6, 7; Joshua viii. 31;) by reason that hewn stones, and those upon which iron had been lifted up, signified artificial and thus fictitious exercises of worship, that is, such as originate in man’s ***proprium*** <note>original: "proprium" — a technical term referring to the human "self" or ego; specifically, the part of a person that acts from its own perceived power and intelligence rather than from divine guidance.</note>, or in the inventions of his thoughts and heart, which was to profane worship, as it is expressly declared, (Exod. xx. 25.) For the same reason, neither was iron lifted up upon the stones of the temple, (1 Kings vi. 7.) 

That the precious stones upon the shoulders of Aaron’s ephod, and in the breast-plate of judgment, in like manner signified holy truths, was shown above, n. 114. This signification of stones also appears from Isaiah:

> “Behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colors, and thy foundations with sapphires: and I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones: and all thy sons shall be taught of Jehovah, and great shall be the peace of thy sons,” (liv. 11, 12:)

the stones here mentioned denote holy truths, wherefore it is said, all thy sons shall be taught of **Jehovah** <note>A name for God in the Old Testament, representing Divine Love.</note>. Hence also it is said in John, “that the foundations of the wall of the city (New Jerusalem) were garnished with all manner of precious stones,” (Rev. xxi. 20:) the holy **Jerusalem** <note>In this context, the "New Jerusalem" signifies a new spiritual state or a reformed church.</note> signifies the Lord’s kingdom in the heavens and on earth, the foundations whereof are holy truths. In like manner, by the tables of stone, on which were written the precepts of the law, or the ten words, were signified holy truths, wherefore they were made of stone; see Exod. xxiv. 12; xxxi. 18; xxxiv. 1; Deut. v. 22; x. 1: for the precepts themselves are nothing but truths of faith. Since, then, by stones were anciently signified truths, and afterwards, when worship

1299. “*And bitumen had they for loam.*”—That these words signify that they were <term>principled</term> <note>To be "principled" in something here means to have it as one’s fundamental driving force or internal state.</note> in evil of lust instead of goodness, appears from the signification of <term>bitumen</term> <note>A naturally occurring petroleum substance like asphalt; here used to symbolize the "burning" or "sticky" nature of selfish desires.</note>, and from the signification of loam in the Word. 1311. Judgment is spoken of as taking place when evil is brought to its height, or, as it is expressed in the Word, when it is come to its <term>consummation</term> <note>Consummation refers to the point where an era or state of evil reaches its absolute limit, triggering a spiritual "reckoning" or judgment.</note>, or when iniquity is consummated. The case herein is this. All evil has its boundaries or limits as far as it is permitted to go: but when it is carried beyond these limits, the guilty party runs into the punishment of evil, and this both in general and particular cases. The punishment of evil is what is then called judgment: and as it appears at first as if the Lord did not see or notice the existence of evil, (for when man does evil with impunity, he supposes that the Lord does not regard it; but when he comes to suffer punishment, he then first thinks that the Lord sees him, yea, that the Lord punishes him,) therefore it is said, according to such appearances.

lip."—That these words signify that they all had one truth of faith, and one doctrine, appears from the signification of people, as denoting the truth of faith, and from the signification of lip as denoting doctrine. That people signifies the truth of faith, that is, those who are principled in the truth of faith, was shown above, in paragraph 1259; and that the lip signifies the doctrine of faith, was shown above at the first verse of this chapter. The people is called one, and the lip one, when all have for an end the general good of society, the general good of the church, and the kingdom of the Lord; for in this case the Lord is in the end, from whom they all form a one. But where each regards his own private good as his end, the Lord cannot possibly be present. This very thing, man's <term>selfhood</term> <note>original Latin: *proprium*; a technical term in this context referring to the human ego, or the part of a person that feels independent from God.</note>, or what is purely his own, excludes and removes the Lord; for the man who regards this as his end bends and inclines the general good of society, and that of the church, yea, and the kingdom of the Lord, towards himself, and this to such a degree, as if they only existed for him: thus he takes away from the Lord what is his, and substitutes himself in its place. When this is man's ruling principle, it communicates its influence to all his thoughts, yea, to the minutest particulars of his thoughts; as is universally the case with whatever has the supreme rule in the mind. 

This does not appear so manifestly in the life of the body, as in the other life: there a man's ruling principle manifests itself by a certain <term>sphere</term> <note>Here, a "sphere" refers to a spiritual aura or atmosphere that radiates from a person's inner character and is felt by others in the spiritual world.</note>, which is perceived by all around him; and this sphere, exhaling, as it does, from every particular of his constitution, is of the same nature and quality as himself. The sphere of a person who regards himself in all things, appropriates to itself, and, as it is there said, absorbs every thing which favors him; consequently, it absorbs all the delight of the spirits around him, and destroys all their freedom: it becomes unavoidable, therefore, that such a one should be separated from their society. But when the people is one, and the lip or language one, that is, when the general good of all is regarded as the chief end, then one never appropriates to himself the delight of another, or destroys another's freedom, but, as far as he is able, promotes and increases them. Hence the heavenly societies are as a one, and this solely in consequence of their mutual love received from the Lord. The case is similar in the church.

**1326.** "Wherefore he called the name thereof Babel."—That these words signify such worship, *namely*, the kind and quality of the worship signified by Babel, appears from what has been said heretofore concerning the worship here spoken of, *namely*, that it was inwardly full of self-love, consequently of every thing most filthy and profane. The truth of the case therefore is this; in proportion to the measure of self-love or <term>proprium</term> that intrudes itself into man's worship, internal worship recedes, or is annihilated. Internal worship consists in the affection of goodness and the acknowledgment of truth; but in proportion as self-love or <term>proprium</term> comes in, or enters, the affection of goodness and the acknowledgment of truth recede or go out. What is holy can by no means abide with what is profane, any more than heaven can abide with hell, but one must needs retire from the other. Such is the state and order which prevail in the Lord's kingdom. This is the reason that with such, whose worship is called Babel, there cannot exist any internal worship, but what they inwardly worship is somewhat dead, and, indeed, like a dead carcass: hence it is evident of what quality their external worship is, when its inward principle is thus corrupt. > “I will send and take all the families of the north, says Jehovah, and Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babel—and will bring them against this land, and against its inhabitants, and against all these nations round about, and will utterly destroy them, and will make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations; and this whole land shall be a desolation” (Jeremiah 25:9, 11). 

Here, the devastation of the interior things of faith, or of <term>internal worship</term>, is described by "Babel." For where the <term>worship of self</term><note>The state where an individual prioritizes their own ego, power, or reputation above divine principles or the well-being of others.</note> prevails, no truth of faith can remain, as was shown above; for <term>self-worship</term> destroys, lays waste, and leads away into captivity everything that is true. This is why Babel is also called a "destroying mountain" (Jeremiah 51:25). See further what was said above concerning Babel in entry number 1182.

1328. **“And from there Jehovah dispersed them over the faces of the whole earth.”**

These words signify that <term>internal worship</term> was annihilated, which can be seen from the meaning of "being dispersed" as being scattered or dissipated. In its most immediate sense, the phrase "being dispersed over the faces of the whole earth" applies to those who sought to build the city of Babel.

<header>GENESIS. [CHAP. xi.</header>

...but since these are the types of people who deprive others of all knowledge of the truth, as was just observed, these words signify at the same time the loss of <term>internal worship</term><note>Sincere, heart-centered devotion and spiritual understanding, as opposed to mere outward ritual.</note>. One is a direct result of the other. In this passage, the consequence itself is what is being highlighted, as this is the third time these words are repeated.

The fact that the first "ancient church" was stripped of the knowledge of truth and goodness is clear from history: the nations that made up that ancient church eventually became idolaters for the most part, though they still kept up a form of external worship. The situation of those who are idolaters outside of the church is not as bad as those who are idolaters within it. The former are only "external" idolaters <note>Meaning they worship idols because of their culture or lack of information.</note>, whereas the latter are "internal" idolaters <note>Meaning they know spiritual truths but choose to worship themselves or worldly things instead.</note>. This is clear from what the Lord says in the Gospels: Luke 13:23, 28–30, and Matthew 8:11, 12. This, then, is the reason why the state of this ancient church was changed.

->**Verse 10.** *These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a son of a hundred years, and begat Arphaxad two years after the flood.*<-

**1329.** By "the generations of Shem," the text signifies the branches or origins of the second ancient church. **Shem** represents internal worship in general. "A hundred years" signifies the state of this church at its very beginning. **Arphaxad** was the name of a nation, used here to signify <term>science</term><note>In this context, "science" refers to "memory-knowledge"—the collection of facts and information one learns about spiritual things before they are fully understood by the heart.</note>. "Two years after the flood" signifies a second <term>postdiluvian</term><note>original: "post diluvium"; occurring or existing after the biblical Great Flood.</note> church.

**1330.** The fact that "these are the generations of Shem" signifies the branches of the second ancient church is clear from the meaning of "generations." This term refers to the origin and development of <term>doctrinals</term><note>The specific systems of teachings or formal beliefs of a religion.</note> and forms of worship, as discussed previously in entry number 1145. 

In this and other parts of the Word <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, "generations" or "births" refer only to things relating to the church. Consequently, they refer to the development of doctrines and worship, which are the only things contained in the <term>internal sense</term><note>The deeper, spiritual meaning hidden behind the literal stories of the Bible.</note> of the Bible. Therefore, whenever a new church is established, the text mentions its "generations." We see this with the "most ancient church" in Genesis 2:4: *"These are the generations of the heavens and the earth."* Similarly, when other churches were born before the flood, it says, *"This is the book of the generations"* (Genesis 5:1). 

The same applies to the churches after the flood. There were three of these:
1. The first was called **Noah**.
2. The second was named after **Heber** (the Hebrew church).
3. The third began with **Jacob**, and later with **Judah** and **Israel**.

When the first church is described, it begins with: *"These are the generations of the sons of Noah"* (Chapter 10:1). The second, named after Heber, is described here in this verse: *"These are the generations of Shem."* The third is described in verse 27 of this chapter: *"These are the generations of Terah."* Therefore, "generations" signify nothing other than the origins and developments of the doctrines and worship of the specific church being described. The reason the generations of this second church are reckoned from Shem, or why its beginning is described from Shem, is because Shem signifies <term>internal worship</term><note>Sincere, heart-centered devotion and spiritual understanding, as opposed to mere outward ritual.</note>, and, in the present verse, the internal worship of this church; not that the internal worship of this church was such as was signified by Shem in the preceding chapter, but only that we are to understand the internal worship of this church.

**1331.** Hence then it appears that Shem denotes internal worship in general. What were the nature and quality of the internal worship which prevailed in this church appears from those who are successively named as derived from Shem, namely, that it was <term>scientific</term><note>In this historical context, "scientific" refers to knowledge stored in the memory or intellectual understanding, rather than modern experimental science.</note>; which is also confirmed by the numbers of years, when they are investigated and unfolded.

**1332.** That “a hundred years” signifies the state of that church in general appears from what was said and shown above concerning numbers and years (sections 482, 487, 488, 493, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, 893) as denoting times and states. **1334.** That **Arphaxad** was a nation so called, and that thereby is signified <term>science</term><note>Meaning intellectual knowledge or the collection of facts regarding spiritual matters.</note>, appears from what was said in the foregoing chapter, verse 24, section 1226.

**1335.** That by “two years after the flood” is signified another post-flood church, may appear from this consideration: that by a “year” in the <term>Word</term><note>A term often used to refer to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, as also by a “day” and by a “week,” is signified a whole period, whether smaller or greater, consisting of fewer or more years—essentially, a period in an abstract sense—as may be seen from the passages quoted above (sections 488 and 893). The case is the same in respect to the expression used here, “two years after the flood,” by which is signified a second period of the church, which was when this second church commenced.

**1336.** *Verse 11. **1337.** That this is the signification of what is said in this verse has no need of further proof, as it appears from what has been said and shown above concerning the same expressions. It may, however, be helpful to observe that the internal worship of this church was nothing else but a kind of knowledge-based worship. Consequently, it consisted of a certain degree of love which may be called the “love of truth”; for at the commencement of this church there was scarcely any <term>charity</term><note>Active, selfless love for one's neighbor, which the author considers the essential heart of true religion.</note> remaining, and consequently scarcely any faith, which originates in charity alone.

**1357.** There are three universal kinds of idolatry; the first is grounded in self-love, the second in the love of the world, and the third in the love of pleasure. All idolatrous worship centres in one or other of these as its end. The worship of idolaters can have no other end, because they have no knowledge of eternal life, nor concern about it, and even deny its existence. These three kinds of idolatry are signified by the three sons of Terah.

Cities at that time were no other than families which dwelt together, and several families formed a nation. That several nations were born of Abraham, appears not only from the posterity of Ishmael, or the Ishmaelites, but also from the posterity of several of his sons which he had by his wife Keturah, who are mentioned by name, Gen. xxv. 1—4.

**1361.** That the church, from being idolatrous, became <term>representative</term><note>A "representative" church is one where external rituals, objects, and people serve as symbolic mirrors of deeper, heavenly realities. In this system, the physical act or person points to a divine truth regardless of the person's own holiness.</note>, is a truth which cannot be known unless it be first known what is meant by a representative. The things which were represented in the Jewish church and in the Word <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer to Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> are the Lord and his kingdom, consequently the <term>celestial</term><note>Refers to things belonging to the highest heaven, characterized by love and the will.</note> things appertaining to love, and the <term>spiritual</term><note>Refers to things belonging to the middle heaven, characterized by faith and the understanding.</note> things appertaining to faith; besides many other things connected with the former, as are all those belonging to the church. The things representing are either persons, or things existing in the world or on the earth—in short, whatever is an object of the senses—insomuch that there is scarce any object but what is capable of being a representative. 

It is, however, a general law of representation that the person or thing which bears the representation is not at all reflected on, but only that which is represented. As for example: Every king, whosoever he was, whether in Judah, or in Israel, or even in Egypt and other places, might represent the Lord; their regal function being representative of itself, whence even the very worst of kings might sustain this representation. This was done by Pharaoh, who exalted Joseph over the land of Egypt; by Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon (Daniel 2:37, 38); by Saul, and the rest of the kings of Judah and of Israel, of whatsoever character they might be. It was involved in the ceremony of anointing them, by virtue of which they were called the <term>anointed of Jehovah</term><note>original: "Christi Jehovae" — the term "Christ" is the Greek translation of the Hebrew "Messiah," both meaning "Anointed One."</note>. 

In like manner all priests, how many soever they were, represented the Lord; the priestly office being representative of itself, whence even wicked and impure characters could sustain this representation as well as others; because, in representatives, the private character of the person bearing the representation is not at all reflected on. Nor was representation confined to men only, but it extended also to beasts, as in the case of all those which were offered in sacrifice: lambs and sheep representing celestial things, whilst doves and turtledoves <note>The original English OCR uses "turtles," an archaic term for turtledoves.</note> represented spiritual things; and rams, goats, bullocks, and oxen, being equally representative, but of celestial and spiritual things in a lower degree. And as animated existences bore their representations, so also did things inanimate; as the altar, yea, the very stones of the altar; likewise the ark and tabernacle with all their appurtenances, as also the temple with all things belonging to it, as may be obvious to every one;

In the ancient churches, <term>representatives</term><note>Physical objects or rituals that serve as symbolic mirrors of spiritual realities.</note> extended to all objects of the senses; as mountains and hills; valleys, plains, rivers, brooks, fountains, and pools; groves and trees in general, and each species of tree in particular, insomuch that every tree had some determinate signification: and thus when the significative church ceased, these objects became representative. The case with respect to representatives was this; that, in the sight of spirits and angels, all things appeared holy which were done according to the appointed rites; as when the high-priest washed himself with water, when he ministered in his pontifical vestments, or when he stood before the lighted candles, whatsoever he might be in his private character, were he even the most impure of mankind, and even in heart an idolater: so also in regard to the other priests; for, as just observed, in representatives the person was not reflected on, but the thing represented, altogether abstractedly from the person; and abstractedly, likewise, from the oxen, bullocks, and lambs which were sacrificed, and from the blood which was poured out about the altar, and also from the altar itself, &c. After all internal worship had perished, and had become not only merely external, but also idolatrous, this representative church was instituted, in order that there might be some sort of conjunction between heaven and earth, or between the Lord, through heaven and man, after that conjunction had perished which had been before preserved by the internals of worship. But the nature and quality of this conjunction, effected by representatives alone, will, by the divine mercy of the Lord, be spoken of hereafter. Representatives do not commence till the next chapter, all the contents of which, and of those which follow, both generally and particularly, are purely representative. These in general are four, one more interior than another, the three more interior kinds being as the sons of one parent, and the fourth as the son of the third. Idolatrous worship may be either **internal** or **external**; the internal is what brings man under condemnation, but the external not so much so. In proportion as idolatrous worship is of a more interior nature, the more it condemns: but in proportion as it is more external, it condemns less. **Internal idolaters** do not acknowledge a God, but adore themselves and the world, and make idols of all their lusts: whereas, **external idolaters** may acknowledge a God, although they do not know who is the God of the universe. Internal idolaters are known by the life which they have acquired to themselves; and their idolatry is of a more interior kind, in proportion as their life so acquired departs from the life of <term>charity</term><note>Charity here refers to the active spiritual love for others, which is considered the core of a truly religious life.</note>: whereas external idolaters are known only by their worship, and, notwithstanding their being idolaters, they may still possess the life of charity. Internal idolaters are capable of <term>profaning</term><note>To "profane" is to possess knowledge of sacred truths but to live in a way that intentionally violates or mocks them, which is viewed as a severe spiritual state.</note> holy things, but external idolaters are not: wherefore external idolatry is tolerated in order to prevent such profanation; as may appear from what was said above, numbers 571, 582, and at verse 9, number 1327.

Verse 29. *And Abram and Nahor took to themselves wives: the name of Abram's wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.* This signifies marriages of evil with falsity in idolatrous worship, which are so circumstanced: by husbands are signified evils, by wives false principles <note>In the symbolic language of this commentary, "marriage" represents the joining together of a person's will (desires) and their understanding (thoughts). In a negative context, "husband and wife" represent the union of a bad intention with a false idea.</note>.

1370. It would take too much space to show that these are the particulars contained in this verse, for this would be to explain the various kinds and derivations of idolatries. These can only be understood from a knowledge of the opposites of heavenly things, that is, of the <term>profanations</term><note>The act of taking what is holy and treating it as common or using it for selfish ends.</note> of them; as of the celestial things of love, and of the spiritual things of the same, as also of things rational derived thence, and lastly, of <term>scientifics</term><note>External facts or intellectual data stored in the memory that have not yet been integrated into a person's spiritual life.</note>. The profanations of these constitute the genera and species of idolatries; which are not constituted merely by the worship of idols, for this is only external idolatry, and may be joined with affections of goodness and truth, and thus with charity, as amongst the gentiles that live in mutual charity. Interior idolatrous worship, in its various kinds, is what is signified in the Word by external idolatrous worship. The nativities and generations of the various kinds of such worship, and also their marriages, which are those of evil and falsity, are altogether circumstanced according to the relationships and marriages described in verse 27, and in this.

1371. Verse 30. *And Sarai was barren, she had no child.* This signifies, that evil and falsity produced themselves no further.

1372. This may appear from the signification of the word barren, of which elsewhere: for son and daughter, as was shown above, signify truth and goodness, and, in the opposite sense, evil and falsity: hence to be barren here signifies, that the evil and falsity of idolatrous worship produced themselves no further.

1373. Verse 31. *And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go into the land of Canaan: and they came to Haran, and there abode.* Hereby is signified, that they who were in the practice of idolatrous worship, were instructed in the celestial and spiritual things of faith, in order that a <term>representative church</term><note>A form of religious community where spiritual truths are portrayed through external symbols, rituals, and the lives of historical figures.</note> might thence have existence.

1374. That this is the signification of these words, may appear from what has been said above, and from what will be said in the next chapter.

<summary>This page explains the symbolic meaning of the marriages and family lineages in Genesis 11, interpreting them as the union of evil intentions and false ideas within idolatry. It concludes with Terah’s departure from Ur, representing the beginning of spiritual instruction that would eventually lead to the establishment of a new church.</summary>

### CONTINUATION OF THE SUBJECT CONCERNING SITUATION AND PLACE, AND ALSO CONCERNING DISTANCE AND TIME, IN THE OTHER LIFE <note>The "other life" refers to the spiritual world or afterlife.</note>.

1376. *I HAVE frequently discoursed with spirits concerning their idea of place and of distance, suggesting to them that they are not any thing real, but only apparently so, being nothing else but the states of their thought and affection, which are thus varied, and are exhibited to view, in the world of spirits; but not so in heaven among the angels, they not being in the idea of place and time, but in that of states. This, however, is inconceivable to those spirits to whom corporeal and terrestrial ideas still adhere, and who imagine every thing to be just as it appears: it is with difficulty also that they can be convinced that they are no longer in the body, but are living as spirits: being unwilling to admit the existence of any mere appearance, or of any fallacy in the things about them, it being their desire to live in fallacies. Thus they preclude themselves from all right conception and acknowledgment of what is true and good, which are at the utmost distance from all fallacy. It was frequently shown them, that change of place is nothing but an appearance, and also a fallacy of sense: for there are two species of changes of place in the other life; one being that spoken of above, where it was shown that all spirits and angels constantly keep their situation in the <term>Grand Man</term><note>original: "Maximus Homo." A central concept in this work where the entire heaven is organized in the form of a human being, with every spirit corresponding to a specific organ or function.</note>, which is an appearance: the other is this, that spirits appear in one place, when yet they are not there, which is a fallacy.*

1377. *That place, change of place, and distance, are appearances in the world of spirits, may appear from this fact, that all souls and spirits whatsoever, since the first creation, appear constantly in their places, nor ever change them, unless when their state is changed, and as their state is changed, places and distances are also varied to them: but as every one has a common or general state, which is his ruling or governing one, and all particular and individual changes of state have still a respect to the common or general one, therefore, after those changes, they return to their own situation.*

<summary>This page marks the symbolic transition from ancient idolatry (represented by Terah) to a new spiritual era (Abram) and introduces a philosophical discussion on how space and time in the afterlife are actually reflections of an individual's internal state.</summary>

# GENESIS. [CHAP. XI.

1378. *I have been informed, both by discourse with angels and by experimental evidence, that spirits, as spirits, with respect to the <term>organical forms</term><note>The spiritual structures or "organs" that compose the body of a spirit.</note> which constitute their bodies, are not in that place where they seem to be, but that it is possible they may be very far distant thence, and yet appear to be there. I am well aware that they who suffer themselves to be imposed upon by <term>fallacies</term><note>In this context, "fallacies" refers to illusions created by relying strictly on physical senses rather than spiritual truth.</note> will not believe this, but nevertheless the fact is certainly so. For the conviction of those spirits who believed nothing to be true but what they saw with their eyes, although it might be a mere fallacy, this fact was illustrated by the consideration, that somewhat of a similar nature is exhibited amongst men in the world. Thus, in the case of the sound of the voice in speaking, when it enters the ear of the person spoken to; unless he knows, from the skill in discriminating sounds acquired by habit, and from the testimony of sight, that the speaker is at a distance, he would believe no other than that the speaker was close to his ear. So, also, in the case of vision, when exercised on remote objects; unless the spectator saw at the same time intermediate objects, and thereby was enabled to compute the distance, or else knew it previously, he would be led to suppose the distant object very near to his eye. Still more particularly is this the case with respect to the speech of spirits, it being of a more interior nature; and also with respect to their vision, that likewise being a more interior vision. It was further declared to them, that on this account they ought not to doubt a fact, much less to deny it, because it does not appear obvious to the senses, and they cannot by their means perceive it, when manifest experience evinces it to be so. Such is the case also with respect to many things within the sphere of nature, which are contrary to the fallacies of the senses, and are yet believed, because they are confirmed by visible experience. To mention only the instance of a ship's sailing round the globe; they who suffer their judgment to be carried away by fallacies would imagine, that both the ship and the sailors, when they come to the opposite side, would fall off; and that the <term>antipodes</term><note>A term for people living on the opposite side of the globe. Historically, many found it hard to believe people could stand upright on the "bottom" of the world without falling off due to gravity.</note> cannot possibly stand on their feet. The case is similar with respect to the place of spirits, and many other facts in the <term>other life</term><note>The spiritual world or afterlife.</note>, which are contrary to the fallacies of the senses, and nevertheless are true; such as, that man has not life from himself, but from the Lord; not to mention various other instances. From these and other considerations, incredulous spirits might be induced to believe, that what has been above said concerning the situation and place of spirits is really so.*

1379. *Hence also it may appear, that the <term>ambulations</term><note>The act of walking or moving from place to place.</note> and translations of spirits, and their progressions, which are often beheld, are nothing else but changes of state; that is, that they appear as changes of place in the world of spirits, but as changes of state in heaven. The like is true in respect to several other*

<summary>This page explains that distance and location in the spiritual world are appearances based on one's internal state rather than physical space, using the analogy of how humans perceive sound and the curvature of the Earth.</summary>
